->### The English Translator’s Preface to Jacob Boehme’s Apologies.<-

<sig>A 2</sig>

*Courteous Reader,*

In the lifetime of Jacob Boehme <note>original: "Jacob Behme"</note>, there were some learned men of his own country who highly prized and esteemed his writings, though others judged and found fault with them. To these critics, the author, in his written answers, has clearly shown that they have NOT understood his meaning, but have unfairly made their own mistaken interpretation the basis of their censure. It is no wonder, therefore, that among those of us who speak another language and have only a translation—in which much of the accuracy and fitting expression of an author is inevitably lost—that men here also find such fault with them as they do. 

If this is examined, it will be found that their lack of true understanding has caused the negligent and heedless opinion that his writings cannot be understood. This has even reached the point where those who believe they grasp his "deep matter" are suspected by certain academic wits <note>likely referring to university-trained scholars or theologians</note> of being merely misled by such a foolish notion <term>conceit</term>. 

However, those eminent people—both his countrymen and his adversaries—never once charged him with writing things that were unintelligible, even though they themselves did not correctly perceive the author's meaning. This is apparent in these **Four Books of Apology or Defense**, written in answer to several objections regarding certain things contained...

<summary>This preface by the English translator argues that criticisms of Jacob Boehme’s work stem from a lack of understanding rather than the writing being inherently nonsensical, noting that even Boehme's original critics recognized his work as intelligible.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, translation, preface, academic wits, apologies, interpretation, theology</keywords>

...contained in that doctrine, set down at length in the treatises of his *Sublime Mysteries*, if they are read and weighed in the balance of due consideration.

The FIRST Apology was an answer to *Balthasar Tylcken*, who wrote a treatise against several sections <note>original: "Clauses"</note> in the *Aurora* <note>Boehme's first book, "The Morning Redness," written in 1612, which explored the relationship between God and nature</note> concerning the knowledge of God *in* and *by* nature. However, although God in himself is totally *incomprehensible* and *unmanifested* in his *abyss* <term>Abysse: a reference to the 'Ungrund', the infinite, groundless void out of which Boehme believed God and the universe emerged</term>, nature is his *manifestation* or *revelation*. For if his omnipotent power did not show itself *by making itself discernable*, it would never be known, but remain *eternally hidden*. Indeed, all the effects that we perceive to be created and produced at any time in physical things are brought to pass by the same powers that have, do, and will work perceptibly in God from eternity to eternity.

All that is in God is only goodness. His very wrath is his *fire* and the cause of his *light* and glory in himself; in that context, it is most just and good. It also serves for the punishment of the perverseness of his creatures, whom he made very good like himself and gave them the power to remain so. But because they were creatures, they were made out of darkness. Once created and brought into the light, they could and did love themselves. All creatures who exist without the light or who lose the light are nothing but darkness; by that means, they exalted their darkness above the light within them,

# The English Translator's Preface to Jacob Boehme's Apologies.

...*holiness*, are undeniably GOOD. On the contrary, the *wrathful, fierce, envious, proud, surly, churlish, wanton, vain, stubborn, obstinate, crafty, false liars, injurious, intemperate, and violent* are accounted bad or EVIL, and they are so indeed. Now, that which is *evil* cannot be like *God's love*.

But here is the general mistake: all *people* <note>original: "Men"; used here in the universal sense of humanity</note> consist of both an *outward and inward man*. That which the *outward man esteems good* is good only insofar as it is a *similitude* <term>Similitude: a likeness or representation</term> of that which is *inwardly good*. But since the *outward man* (who is framed of the *earth*) has gained the *predominance* through the *Fall of Adam*—who then died to the *inward man*—that which most *pleases the outward man makes it stronger and more rebellious against the power of the inward man*. 

And so, through *outward good things*—not knowing how to use them—the *inward man* is destroyed bit by bit. Therefore *God*, in his *bowels of compassion* <note>An archaic expression meaning "deepest mercies" or "heartfelt pity"</note>, sends us *what is most suitable for us* for the *weakening or daily killing and slaying* of our *outward man*. He does this through *tribulations, afflictions, crosses, and contradictions or oppositions* from others, to make us *conform* to the *image* of CHRIST, who was *tempted, persecuted, and afflicted*. As the *Apostle* says, "He who will live *godly* in this *world* must *suffer persecution*" <note>A reference to 2 Timothy 3:12</note>. 

Our *author* <note>Jacob Boehme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose work is being defended here</note> received this treatment from some, as is manifest by their *objections* and their striving to make his *marvelous gifts* disliked by those who did not know any better than to think the *censures* cast upon him were right. Therefore, for the vindication of the *truth*,

*...and for the sake of those who were but beginners in the ways of Christ, he then answered the things that were laid to his charge with such evidence that even his adversaries may be convinced and reconciled to acknowledge the same truth with him.*

The **SECOND** *Apology* was also an answer to a book by Balthazar Tilken <note>original: "Tylckens"</note> against Jacob Boehme’s <note>original: "Behme's"</note> hints of Predestination, mentioned in some of his treatises written before the year 1621. Through these, the great controversies between the Lutherans and Calvinists about the will of God and of man are kindly reconciled. However, because Tilken did not apprehend the ground and depths in them which resolve those questions, he very much opposed this author. Also, the tutor to Tilken's children, whose name was* Dr. Charles Weisner, *initially took great distaste at him as well, as may be seen by a letter at the end of the Epistles printed here. But through personal conversation with* J. B., *he received such satisfaction and contentment that he asks God's forgiveness for his former hard opinion of the author. But* Balthazar Tilken *also wrote against the book of the Incarnation and Person of* **CHRIST** *and of the Virgin* **MARY**; *the author has answered all of these particularly in this Apology.*

The next *treatise concerns the* **Four Complexions** <term>Complexions: referring to the "four humors" (sanguine, choleric, melancholic, and phlegmatic) which were historically believed to determine a person's temperament and health</term>, *compiled at the request of some friends upon the necessary occasion of a certain person.*

[The person previously mentioned] was very much tempted, afflicted, and perplexed by *Satan*. In this work, the author has very accurately described the *Nature* of the *Choleric*, *Sanguine*, *Phlegmatic*, and *Melancholic* *Complexions* <term>Complexions: according to the medical theories of the time, these were the four "humors" or temperaments that governed human health and personality.</term>. He explains their *Effects* upon the *Soul* that *inhabits* them like a *House* in this outward *Tabernacle* <term>Tabernacle: a biblical term used here to describe the physical human body as a temporary shelter for the soul.</term>. He also provides the *Cures* and *Remedies* to make these temperaments advantageous to the soul's progress on the way to *Eternity* while it is in this *Life*. No treatise was ever written before so fully, briefly, and yet convincingly—at least among the books of *Philosophy* or *Theology* <note>original: "Divinity"</note> commonly known. It was formerly translated into *English* by a worthy *Person* in very *elegant* language; however, those who enjoyed reading the author thought it was the work of another person because it did not use the same phrasing as his other books. For this reason, I was prompted to re-translate it—though perhaps not in such a good style—using the kind of expression that makes it recognizable as one of his works.

The following piece contains his *Considerations* regarding a book published by *Esaias Stiefel* <note>Esaias Stiefel (1561–1627) was a German sectarian leader whose mystical views on perfection and the nature of Christ led to controversy; Boehme wrote several treatises addressing and correcting Stiefel's ideas.</note> concerning the *Threefold State of Man*, the *New Birth*, the *River flowing out of Zion* <note>original: "Sion"</note>, and the *New Jerusalem*. Within this work, he distinctly handles that *Threefold State and Condition of Man*. He also writes of the *Resurrection at the Last Day* and explains what that *Body* is *WITHIN* this *Corruptible Body*, which shall rise again and put on *Incorruption*.

# The English Translator's Preface to Jacob Boehme's <note>original: "J. B's."</note> Apologies.

*40. Questions of the Soul: and here at the end of this book: so that now all his works are printed in the English language <note>original: "Tongue"</note>.*

*Judge not according to appearance, but read, weigh, examine, and judge with righteous judgment. Or rather, "Judge not, so that you be not judged," which was one of the precepts of CHRIST; and the Apostle Paul says: "If we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged."*

*Judgment is the mental framing or pronouncing <note>original: "denouncing"</note> of the sentence and the severity of the consuming fire of God's wrath—that which, in reality, anyone is capable of and will certainly receive at the Last Day. To perform this judgment upon others, whom we cannot know as well as we know ourselves, awakens that fiery wrath within our own selves. This ought not to be; for if the eternal fire which is in our hearts and souls is kindled against a person who is not liable by his own guilt, then if it does not burn him, it may and will burn ourselves.*

*But if we kindle that fire of indignation against ourselves, as we justly and deservedly may, it will consume self-love and all the dark matter <term>dark matter: here referring to spiritual impurity or the "grossness" of the soul, not the modern physics concept.</term> of our souls. It will change the soul into light, just as fire changes iron. Then the eternal fire will have no fuel to ignite upon within us—neither now, nor at the Last Day. Instead, we shall be able to dwell with "everlasting burnings" <note>referencing Isaiah 33:14, suggesting the soul becomes compatible with God's holy fire</note> just as light exists within fire, having judged and condemned ourselves.*

*For then we shall walk in righteousness and speak with uprightness; we shall despise the gain of deceit and shake our hands to refuse <note>original: "from holding of"</note>*

<meta>This page begins Jacob Boehme’s defense of his first book, *Aurora*, against a "pasquil" or libelous attack. It establishes the theological framework of the "Anger-Fire" resulting from the Fall of Man to explain the malice of his opponent.</meta>

# A brief and well-intended answer from the author concerning his book *Aurora*, against the hostile *pasquinade* <note>original: "Pasquil"; a lampoon or satirical protest posted in a public place</note> or *libel*; regarding some opposed and falsely recited *articles* or *conclusions* that were misunderstood by this *libeler*.

---

-> 1. <-

Into what calamity, misery, anxiety, and great perplexity we are plunged by the heavy fall of Adam is daily demonstrated. Through this fall, we have not only obscured and darkened our noble image—so that we can no longer see or understand the *divine light* unless we are born of God again—but we have also awakened and stirred up within ourselves the *original, fierce wrath of eternal nature*. Thus, the fierce wrath, venom, and poison of that nature have begun *springing up* and *burning* within us.

2. This is rightly called God’s *anger-fire*, which should not have become active and manifest, but should have remained shut up in the *center*. It was meant to remain enclosed in *love* within the *divine light*, serving only as a cause of *life* and *movement*.

3. So long as it remains shut up in the light, it is a *spring or fountain of joy and knowledge*. But if the *light is extinguished*, it becomes an *evil, opposing poison* in which nothing operates but pure *self-enmity or hatred*; there, all *love* and *desire for good* instantly come to an end.

4. We poor children of Eve must now feel this within ourselves with great pain, sorrow, and misery. We feel how that fierce wrath *stirs, drives, and vexes us*, so that we *no longer* interact with one another in love as children of God. Instead, we act very venomously, spitefully, hatefully, and with murderous intent. We *maliciously persecute, despise, slander, and reproach one another; we also rob, murder, and do all manner of evil*, and always wish death, fierce wrath, and all evil upon one another.

5. This great misery and evil can be clearly traced in this libel. It is obvious what kind of mind, knowledge, and will produced it, as the author undertakes not only to *misconstrue* the words,

# I. Part. The Property of an Enlightened Mind. Apol. I.

...but also to *wrest* the whole understanding into a false meaning or sense, and to pronounce the author to be a *devil*. In a very vaunting, reproachful, *spiteful*, malicious, and odious manner, he *likens* the author’s will, intent, thought, sense, and mind to the devil—all without any knowledge of who the author is, how he lives, or what spirit’s child he is, or *whether* he seeks God or this world.

6. Thus he takes it upon himself to insinuate his innate poison into the heart, thought, *sense*, and will or intention of the author. All of this is very *horrible*, lamentable, and miserable, in that he does not know himself, nor from what mind *his zeal* proceeds, nor by *whose* driving he runs.

7. He cannot see that his whole writing is a mere venomous pasquinade <note>original: "Pasquil"; a lampoon or satirical protest</note> or libel, and an evil intention. For even though what I have spoken is not *reprehensible* <note>original: "reproveable"; worthy of rebuke or blame</note> by him, he still cannot leave it un-reproached. By this, a person may clearly see from what spirit and mind his work has flowed, and how a miserable, fierce wrath has ruled in him; yet he still dares to claim in his *title* that his work is Christian-like and well-intended.

8. If he would set anything *better* in its place, it might indeed be tolerated. But I can find in all his writing no divine knowledge or light—which he nevertheless highly boasts of, as if he had an enlightened mind and thoughts and were practiced in them.

9. An enlightened mind or thoughts (if the light is from God) proceed *friendly* and lovingly. It instructs a person in what they should do and what they should leave undone. It acknowledges others in brotherly duty. It does not hunt men’s minds into the jaws of the devil; rather, such minds are *gentle* in reproving and teaching with good instruction. They reprove in general terms; they do not seize a man privately, particularly, and singly, nor do they make a *den* of thievery or murder by the *wayside* of the Good Way.

10. An enlightened mind, which has practiced thoughts (as the libeler would seem to have), knows that the gifts of God are *without* end or number. It knows that God leads his children wonderfully and gives to one a different gift to express than to another, as the *Apostle* also witnesses.

* 1 Corinthians 12:10–11.
</margin>

11. That *God gives to one, from the gift of his Spirit, the power to do miracles or wonders; to another, the ability to interpret tongues; to a third, to prophesy; to a fourth, to speak with tongues, etc.* All of this is *from* the one and only *Spirit of God*, which speaks from the great wonders of the eternal wisdom of God. Thus the Spirit drives and teaches the children of God, so that the unmeasurable wisdom of God may *appear* in his children.

He is not thorny, prickly, *misconstruing*, or vainly frivolous. He suddenly perceives what is in a person and from what spirit they speak—for the Spirit of God itself knows...

# I. Part. *The Three Principles clearer than the Aurora.* Apology I.

Then I saw that my writings were still extant <note>original: "Extant"; still in existence or surviving</note>, and I wondered that it had happened that way. I understood then that they had had them in their hands for TWO years already, and that all along one good friend had given them to another to write out copies of them.

38. I also understood that they were in the hands of *many men* altogether *unknown* to me, and that many enlightened and honest, pious hearts found great satisfaction in them—people who sought not poison, but a right *way* to the Divine Life and Christian *living* <note>original: "Conversation"; in this period, it referred to one's conduct, behavior, or way of life</note> within it.

39. These people undoubtedly did not have such venomous eyes that the vision of the *Serpent* <note>a reference to the Devil or malicious intent</note> so suddenly slipped into the *center* of their minds and sought to pervert them. Instead, they left it to the Spirit of God and asked for *instruction*, which they also obtained.

40. I firmly believe that the Devil is sitting in the *libeller*—in his mind, eyes, heart, and thoughts—and that he suddenly *infested* him and drove him on to strife.

41. Certainly, if the libeller had searched further, he would have found out who the author was.

42. And if he had *written to me* even a little, to know how I came by such meanings and writings, I would have written back to him very friendly and in a Christian manner. This would have suited a Christian well, especially an enlightened mind.

43. You only cast a mist before men’s eyes, driving them into God’s anger and letting them lie *there*, while you go your way—and furthermore, you **forbid anyone to investigate it further.**

53. Yes indeed, the devil might thereby be exposed or revealed, and he would not want that. Or, quite likely, my book has struck your **Calvinist vein** <note>referring to the strict Calvinist doctrine of predestination, which Boehme often critiqued as being too harsh</note>.

54. I cannot help that. If you or others *will not* read my book, then leave it alone. It is not printed; who told anyone to write a copy of it? Leave it to me; I have written it only for myself. It has nothing to do with you. I have *not* run about with it and *presented* it to anyone; it has come out against my will and desire, and *without my knowledge*, as those who first obtained it well know.

<meta>This page continues Jacob Boehme’s defense of his work, specifically his first book, *Aurora*. He addresses accusations of seeking personal fame and argues that his complex, "magical" style is necessary for expressing divine mysteries, drawing parallels to the parables of Christ.</meta>

### Part 1. His *Aurora* needs further explanation. Apology 1.

55. But regarding what you accuse me of—that I sought my own fame through this—that is a falsehood. A Christian *does not seek his own honor*, but God’s honor, and, through His love, the honor of his neighbor. Christ did not seek His own honor but His Father’s; He desired no honor from man. Why, then, should I desire it?

56. The *true knowledge* of God is not from this world but from God. Why, then, should it seek a home here? Look at yourself and consider.

57. I say with good reason: *in such a manner* you have no understanding of my writings. You only stain them for me with a foreign interpretation, as will be further shown to you here—though briefly, for the sake of the reader who reads your reproachful paper, so that he may distinguish between *both* of us.

58. He who desires a full explanation should read the book *The Threefold Life of Man*; he will find more there than he might even *search for*, especially in *The Three Principles*, which the attacker or satirist <note>original: "Libeller or Pasquiller"; a "pasquil" was a common term for a public lampoon or anonymous satire</note> *does not dare to believe*. Yet if he wants to be called a Christian and do what is right, let him read that; he will see what kind of spirit’s child I am. *Perhaps* we shall come closer together, and he may change from a Saul into a Paul <note>a reference to the dramatic conversion of the Apostle Paul</note>; I heartily wish this for him. I would much rather have a sincere, good, and *Christian discussion* with him concerning our Immanuel <note>Hebrew: "God with us"</note> than this *controversy*.

<margin>\* Mystical, symbolic, prophetic, or in parables or metaphors.</margin>

59. Truly I say that my book, which he opposes in *some places*, needs a better explanation for the sake of easier understanding. I am also very ready to provide it if anyone desires it, for in some places it is still written in a very \* *mystical style* <note>original: "Magick understanding"; in Boehme's context, "magical" refers to the hidden, spiritual power and symbolic language of the divine, rather than sorcery</note>.

<margin>† Matthew 7:6.</margin>

60. But there are also such mysteries within it that the *learned scholar* or *Master Alexen* <note>likely a reference to a specific critic or a stereotypical academic</note> cannot count them, for it has pleased God to have it so. Look upon the writings of the Prophets and see whether they are clear in all places; besides, Christ himself also taught in parables or metaphors. † *Men should not cast pearls before swine.*

61. But concerning the *Articles of Faith* <note>the fundamental doctrines of the Church</note>, which in this book are still expressed in a mystical way, these are set down *clearly enough* in my other writings—more than the attacker or satirist requires or understands. Yet if anyone desires more clarification, it shall be granted to them; and if they desire proof, it shall also be given.

62. But to him who does not desire it, I have not written it for him; let him leave it alone. I write for myself and chase after no one. I have not put it out to any bookstore to sell; if some God-fearing people had not sincerely, earnestly, and with true Christian intent asked and pleaded for it, I would not have given it to anyone at all.

<margin>\* Matthew 5:15. † Matthew 25:25.</margin>

63. But since honest, God-fearing hearts are found whose Christianity is indeed *sincere* and earnest, should Christian love be withheld from them? Or has God \* *given me this gift* so that I should put it *under a basket* <note>original: "stool"; a reference to the biblical command not to hide one's light</note>, or † *bury it in the earth* <note>referring to the Parable of the Talents, where a servant is punished for hiding his master's money</note>?

# I. Apol. A Christian must break his own Evil will. Part I.

64. *Christ* says, "*No one lights a lamp or candle and puts it under a stool or under a basket, but sets it upon a table, so that all who are in the house may see by it.*" The divine light will not be hidden; those to whom God gives it should let it shine, for God will require an account of their talent <note>original: "Talent"; referring to the biblical parable where a talent represents a unit of value or a gift entrusted by God</note>.

65. Moreover, what is it that men argue about and dispute so much in the Christian religion? The Christian religion is not about strife, contention, or opinion; it consists of the *new birth* <note>original: "New Regeneration"</note> out of Christ, in faith, through the Holy Spirit, in humility, love, and righteousness.

66. A Christian must be *born of Christ*; he must have a Christian will and desire, and lead a Christian life <note>original: "Conversation"; in this period, "conversation" referred to one's conduct or way of life</note>. It is not only knowledge that will do it—merely comforting oneself with Christ’s sufferings while being a deceitful hypocrite in the presence of God, speaking one thing while willing, desiring, and doing another. One cannot let the evil, poisonous ***worm of the fire of corrupt nature*** keep burning and be only a **Christian in name** <note>original: "Lip or Mouth-Christian"</note>.

67. It does not consist of knowing a great deal, so that a man might flatter himself with Christ’s sufferings and set them high on a pedestal <note>original: "Pinnacle"</note>, and yet *keep the evil, envious, ignited, poisonous worm continually in his heart, constantly feeding its fire with fuel.* I say that this very cloak will become hellish fire to many: that they have known God’s will but will not enter into it and surrender themselves to Him.

68. A Christian must break his own *natural* will and surrender himself to God’s will. He must always quench the fire of his own will and continually bring *all the thoughts* of his mind into obedience to God—into the love and mercy of God in Christ, into His becoming man (or incarnation), suffering, dying, death, and resurrection. He must will nothing but God’s will in Christ.

69. But this is his desire: that God may be his will and deed, and that God in him may be his knowledge. He should continually *kill* <note>original: "slay"</note> the will of his flesh and desire only God’s *will* in himself, so that it may rule, drive, and be the active force in him.

<margin>Note where man's ability to do good comes from.</margin>
70. For man of himself does no good thing; but the law of God, which God writes in his nature, does the good. That very law is the eternal *Word of the Deity* and takes upon itself divine and heavenly substance <note>original: "substantiality"</note>, namely the new body; for it has become man, and it must also become man in us.

<margin>Revelation 17:1, 2.</margin>
71. And in that body stands the right willing and doing, the performance, and the *ability* of a Christian man. Without that, there is no *Christian*, but only the Antichrist and a spiritual *prostitution* <note>original: "Whoredome"</note>, as the Revelation of *St. John testifies*.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:4.</margin>
<margin>Psalm 5:4.</margin>
72. Therefore, it does not lie in disputing, intellectual pride <note>original: "flying high"</note>, being overly *precise*, or *despising* and condemning one's brother to the devil. For God *wills that all men should be helped or saved;* and *He is not a God who wills evil*.

# I. Part. How Faith is Generated. Apol. I.

Earthly fuel produces an earthly source or quality, and a light according to that source or quality; whatever a man kindles in himself, *that* burns in him.

87. But God’s Kingdom consists of power, love, and joy; it searches for nothing, for it has all things already. Only the soul searches; it desires to enter into the Kingdom of *Rest*. In the earthly body, it is stuck in *unrest* <note>original: "unquietness"</note>; and therefore it searches for its native country, from which it departed in *Adam*—traveling from *Jerusalem* to *Jericho*. That is, it went into itself, into the origin of the *first principle* <term>the foundational source of being, often associated by Boehme with the "fire" of the soul's desire</term>. Out of itself, it goes through the *first principle* into the spirit of the *outward world*, into the multiplicity—namely, into the stars and elements, into the source of torment <note>original: "torment-house"</note> where it finds and learns academic arts. It insists on being like God and knowing both evil and good; and indeed, it experiences that, but realizes: *It would be better to be in Paradise*.

88. Therefore, all contention and strife concerning the Kingdom of God is only fighting with a shadow, a *Babylonian* work <note>referring to "Babel," the biblical city of confusion; Boehme uses this to describe organized religious conflict</note> in the Kingdom of *Antichrist*.

89. A true believing Christian should *not strive* or contend with anyone about religion; let him strive only against *himself*, against flesh and blood <note>the sinful human nature</note>. Let him endeavor for this: how he may do the works of God through the love of his neighbor. Let him seek only God’s will, surrender himself to that, and lead his life in obedience to the will of God. Let him withdraw himself from this world, for he is not at home in this world; and let him seek his brother as a member of his own soul, and take him along with him.

90. As one *member* of the body wishes and does all good for the *other*, so a believing soul will continually want its fellow member to be with it. It endeavors to show its brother any good; it always shows him its light and, through its imagination, *sets it before the eyes of the soul to be looked upon* <margin>As an object.</margin>. It says, "Come, I pray, *here*." It is for this reason that this pen has written so much, which the lampooner <note>original: "Pasquill"; a name for a satirical or insulting critic</note> or libeller does not understand, for the *sting* of malice is within *him*.

91. Oh, how miserably and horribly he has written regarding the propagation of man and *of the will of God*! A man whom the devil already assaults enough might fall into despair because of it. Therein lies heresy: that a man dares to *pervert* the will of God—who wills only good—and turn God’s will into a will of evil or *malice*.

92. How very blind he is regarding the knowledge of God! He knows absolutely nothing of the eternal nature or of the origin of the will—what the will toward good and toward evil is. *He rejects my little "A.B.C." book* <margin>The AURORA.</margin> <note>Boehme's first book, *Aurora*, which was confiscated and suppressed by local authorities</note> *and puts the* Babylonian Grammar *in its place; he thinks academic "art" must do the work*.

93. Oh, listen, libeller: Do you have the *knowledge of this world*? Then I have the *knowledge of the divine world*. You have learned yours, and

# I. Apol. Election is to be searched for in Christ. Part. I.

My [gift] is bestowed upon me by Grace in the Love of God; I shall stand firm with my [understanding] against yours; they are like the Sun and the Moon to one another. An honest man, who fears God and seeks only God's will, may very well *distinguish* my writings from yours.

94. Do you suppose that men are satisfied by your writings? Can they satisfy the heart and the poor, captive soul which is stuck in the Prison of Darkness? You teach that God has not *chosen* <note>original: "Elected"</note> all of them; that God *hardens* one part of them and does not draw them, through Christ, to the Father. You give the analogy of a **Potter**—as if the soul were merely manufactured or created <note>referring to the biblical analogy in Romans 9, often used to argue that God creates some people specifically for destruction</note>. Although you do not state it in those exact terms, your words give that impression.

95. Why do you not explain the origin of the will to evil and to good? What is it in God that draws men to good and to evil? If you boast of having an enlightened mind, you must know that and explain it for the comfort of the poor soul. This way, the soul may *not be wavering and unsettled, thinking that God has not created it to be a vessel of honor, or that it is not born or generated in the lineage of* Christ. You bring up the examples of *Cain* and *Abel* and use twisted, perverted scriptures while leaving out the *best part, namely* <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note> the Love of God, which does not desire evil. In doing so, you cast a snare around the neck of the soul.

96. Well, you have come to my warehouse, to which I have invited the children of God. But I tell you, I have no such *goods* <note>original: "ware"</note> as you are looking for. I have only comfort for the children of God, and not despair for the devils. I will display the goods I promised; if you will not buy, leave them alone.

97. I have not invited the **Devil's advocates** to it, but Christ's children, who would gladly be saved. Although you boast much that the *choice* <note>original: "Election"</note> of Grace is not to be searched for outside of Christ, you do not explain how it is to be searched for *in* Christ. Instead, you lay it aside *as if God would not have all* **men**, *and as if He hardened some out of a predestined purpose*.

98. In that respect, I will show you some of my goods; if you will buy, well and good, and so you may be a brother in Christ. But if not, it is because you yourself are unwilling. God indeed desires it, but if you yourself will not, then you harden yourself.

99. The center from which evil and good flow is *in you*. Whatever you awaken within yourself—be it *fire* or *light*—that will be received again by its *own kind*: either by God's *anger-fire* or by God's *light-fire* <term>Boehme's terms for the two aspects of God: His wrath/severity (anger-fire) and His love/mercy (light-fire)</term>. Each of them *chooses* <note>original: "Electeth"</note> for itself that which matches its own quality.

100. If anyone wishes to be a **devil**, then God's *anger* will have him, for he shares its quality. The *choice* <note>original: "Election"</note> or choosing is immediately there. But if he wishes to be an **angel**, then the *choice* or choosing is also immediately there.

<summary>Boehme rejects the idea of unconditional predestination, arguing that God's "Election" is not an arbitrary choice to harden certain people. Instead, he claims that individuals determine their own fate based on whether they align their inner will with God's light and love or His wrathful "anger-fire."</summary>

101. But even if a man has been evil and wicked, and it seems likely that the **Anger** of God has **already** chosen or **Elected** him for damnation—if that man still lets the **spark** of **God's Love** back into the light of his life, it is offered to him and **calls** to him as long as he lives. In that case, the **Elector** (the one who chooses for the Kingdom of Heaven) is just as suddenly present **IN THAT spark**. Furthermore, † there is great **joy and honor, more so than for the ninety-nine chosen ones who need no repentance.** <note>original: "Elected"; referring to the Parable of the Lost Sheep in Luke 15:7.</note>

102. The soul of man originates from that **Center** which is called God the Father—meaning, out of the beginningless Eternal Nature. Within itself, the soul possesses the **Center** for both fire and Light, for evil and for good. Whatever IT **chooses** <note>original: "Electeth"</note> for itself, it is chosen by that thing in return and consumed by it; this can be seen in the example of the devils.

103. They were once angels in God’s Light, but their **Center** elevated itself even higher than the proper law of the angelic nature allowed. This awakened within them the **Mother** <note>In Boehme’s thought, the "Mother" refers to the generating source or matrix of a particular state of being.</note> of the Source in fierce wrath. That wrath suddenly seized their "will-spirit" and **elected** or chose them to be creatures of the **dark world**.

104. Do you suppose now that it was God's **predestined, intentional Will** to have it be so? If that were true, then God must have a devil’s will within Himself as well as an angelic one. This is completely contrary to Holy Scripture, against God’s Love, and against the Light of Eternal Nature.

105. But the **libeller** <note>original: "Pasquill"; a term for a writer of anonymous lampoons or insults.</note> does NOT understand at all what God’s Love and Anger are, or even what is truly called "God." He wants to speak of God’s Will, but he is merely fighting with shadows and engaging in **deceptive trickery**. <note>original: "Jugling"</note>

106. Since he does not understand it, and since—through the Grace of God—I see his miserable blindness and how he burns in the poison of the Source, he acts as a true **advocate** for the Anger of God and for the devil, trying to lock up and keep the poor soul within God's **Anger**. Therefore, I will reveal something to him. Now, if he is willing to accept it <note>original: "buy"</note>, well and good; then let **IMMANUEL** <note>Hebrew: "God with us."</note> be for US, and the **dark world** for the devil.

107. But if he will NOT, then I have written this for the readers of his libel. If the reader is a Christian and intends to be saved, he will be well able in his understanding and mind to distinguish between us.

# I. Apol. How Man is a Total Image of God. Part. II.

...all the Three Worlds; an Image of God, wherein God dwells, and wherein God beheld, found, and manifested or revealed himself.

198. Now the Eternal Word was his *law*, of his spiritual nature, so that this introduced and in-breathed spirit of man should direct its imagination into no other source or quality but only into God's love and meekness. It was meant to eat only of the divine substantiality <note>original: "Substantiality"; in Boehme’s theology, this refers to the spiritual "body" or essence of the divine realm.</note> and drink the water of eternal life; then its body would have remained paradisiacal.

199. The body had paradisiacal fruit to *eat*, which grew for it *within* all fruits. The outward body of this world was, in the source or quality of the light-world, as if swallowed up—and yet it was there. Just as the light swallows up the darkness and holds it captive within itself, yet the darkness remains, though it is not manifested in the light.

200. So also should the outward image of this world, as well as the inward source or quality of the fire from the first principle <note>The "First Principle" refers to the raw, energetic, and often "wrathful" foundation of nature, which must be tempered by light.</note>, have remained hidden within the paradisiacal substantiality and quality; and man should have brought his life and *will* into that paradisiacal quality.

201. He was to set or put his spirit’s imagination into the heart of God—that is, into the *center* of the Light—and then the soul would have continually eaten of the light’s substantiality. Understand that the "foolish fire" <note>original: "foolish Fire"; likely referring to the raw, untamed drive of the soul’s first principle before it is enlightened.</note> would have received the divine quality into itself and would have burned forth in that divine quality: namely, in love and meekness.

202. Through that burning, or life, the divine substance would have been introduced into the *outward* body—that is, heavenly flesh—and the holy body would have existed in the *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; an alchemical term used here to describe the spiritual essence or life-force that governs and perfects matter.</note> of the second principle. The outward dominion of the physical world would have remained hidden within the inward world, while still being manifested in the outward.

203. *Such* a body was also created in the beginning: one formed from the inward substantiality of the pure element <note>Boehme distinguishes between the "pure element" of the spiritual realm and the four material elements (earth, air, fire, water) of our world.</note> which is manifested in paradise, and an outward body from the four elements which stood manifested in the outward world. But the inward was meant to hold the dominion and keep the outward as if swallowed up, just as the light does the darkness.

204. Understand that each principle should stand freely and purely in itself, and direct its imagination or desire toward God. Then God’s light would have filled all in all, and the earnest, severe fire-source or quality of the first principle (the eternal nature of the dark world), as well as the outward nature and quality of the stars and elements, would not have been manifested.

205. Man would have lived in the divine source of love and would have remained immortal and incorruptible; no sickness, nor any want, necessity, or death, would have touched him.

211. 212. He brought the earthly quality and substance into the pure elementary flesh, which had been created out of divine substance. <margin>* Luke 10:30.</margin>

229. The question is: what is the *wild nature* in which the Prince of Light from the Heart of God wrestled in his *humanity*? Is it earthly flesh? Or the essence or quality of the stars and the four elements? No. The Prince from the Heart of God did not come for the sake of those things. Rather, it was the *soul*, originating from the eternal *Father’s nature*, which through its own imagination and desire had introduced death and earthliness into itself. It had awakened the dark world's fierce wrath within the anger of God, and there was no remedy—neither in heaven nor in this world—unless the Prince of the Love of God came and wrestled with the fierce, wrathful anger of God, and quenched that fire within the human soul.

230. And therefore the Prince of God's Love—namely, God’s own Heart—became **A MAN** in the human nature and in human essence. He did not become a man in a "strange" essence, as the critic <note>original: "Libeller"</note> wonderfully suggests here. Also, he did not dwell in the **wild** nature of the stars and elements, nor in the beast-like flesh of the corrupt or perished physical manifestation <note>original: "Out-birth"</note> of the four elements. It is not in that essence that the **Deity** is united. It is not the **wild Adam-like** flesh which Christ took upon himself, as the critic explains it; for that critic has no understanding at all of the essence through which God became **MAN**.

231. Adam’s soul did not originally have an outward body made of the four elements, for it existed in God’s love, in Paradise. Paradise is not made of the four elements; it does not consist of four elements, but of **ONE**. It is the divine delight or dwelling place.

232. God does not dwell in the outward product <note>original: "Out-birth"</note> of the four elements, but in Heaven—in the pure element that is his Spirit’s physical substance. Adam also had that substance for a body, and he stood within the outward body just as gold is hidden within a coarse or slag-filled <note>original: "drossie"</note> stone.

233. The **inward** body keeps the **outward** body hidden, just as the light hides the darkness. The **Spirit of God** dwells in the inward body, for it contains within itself the Second Principle <note>original: "Second Principle"; in Boehme’s theology, this is the world of Light, Love, and the Kingdom of Heaven.</note>—namely, the Kingdom of Heaven—which is an image of the divine substance. The soul finds its gentleness <note>original: "Meeknesse"</note> there. It ate of that very body in which God dwelt, and its fire was calmed and softened by it; for therein it received God’s love and gentleness.

234. But as soon as the soul’s fire began to focus its **imagination** on earthly things and desired to eat of the four elements and stars, then the outward kingdom—namely, the **Third Principle** <note>original: "Third Principle"; the material, physical world we inhabit.</note>—drew the First Principle <note>The realm of God’s power and "fire."</note> into the soul’s fire and also into the heavenly body. This obscured the noble image so that it fell into helplessness and into **sleep**. It was then in a state of inability, as if captured by death, for the earthly influence <note>original: "Source or Quality"</note> now dwelt within it. Because of this, the soul’s fire became fierce, wrathful, stinging, and murderous; for it now had to eat both evil and good, and the noble image of the likeness of God disappeared.

235. Now when God saw that the noble image had disappeared or vanished, and that the outward kingdom had become lord over it, His **mercy pitied** it. He promised the Woman’s offspring <note>original: "Seed"</note> would be the crusher of the serpent, saying: *The offspring of the woman shall crush or bruise the head of the serpent* which caused your fall. He said the offspring of the woman would do this.

236. Understand this correctly: God would become man in the true human and heavenly substance which was locked in death in Adam. He did not become man in the earthly nature that was introduced into the noble image and soul. Rather, God’s Word has entered <note>original: "En-tered"; the text breaks here to the next page.</note> into the true human nature of the Second Principle, in which God dwelt before Adam’s fall—into that very essence that was locked in death.

249. Was *Mary* not extracted or begotten from *Joachim* and *Anna*? Was she not naturally conceived and born, just like all the children of Adam? If not, let him prove it; otherwise, his fancy <note>original: "conceit"; here meaning a fanciful or misguided notion.</note> will remain untrue.

250. But if he says that if *Mary* were begotten of *Joachim* and *Anna*, then Christ must have been begotten of "sinful seed" (as his arrogant spirit assumes and supposes), then I tell him once and for all: he is completely blind to the Divine Mystery and understands *nothing* about it.

251. He speaks indeed of the "High Blessing" of *Mary*, but he attributes it to a *strange* seed from which *Mary* was supposedly begotten. However, he provides no basis for what *kind* of seed that was—whether it was purely the Spirit of God, or heavenly substance <term>Substantiality: In Boehme's theology, this refers to the spiritual "body" or divine essence that was present in Adam before the Fall.</term>, or the "Seed in the Word," or if it also contained something of the human essence.

252. For to him, the human essence is sinful throughout; he believes Christ will not be born of man at all, but only of God, as if God had introduced a *strange humanity* in Christ. He explains it this way throughout: he believes Christ is only born like "the dew of the morning" <note>referring to a spiritual origin without earthly substance</note>.

253. But listen, Mr. Libeller! We will not be as malicious as you are. We are ready and willing to show you the true basis of the Mystery. If you *refuse to walk* in that way, then step aside; we have eyes to see things you do not. Do you have intellectual art? Then we have spiritual light.

254. You are not our *judge*, even though you condemn me. I am a child of God in Christ, and my vision proceeds from God’s vision. Therefore, with a good heart, I will show you my open face, even though you are unable to understand *how Christ was conceived and born of*

### Therefore, observe my confession of faith and acknowledgment, exactly as it follows:

->255.<-
God said to Adam, when he stood in Paradise and lived in the divine source or quality and substantiality: *In the day that you eat of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, you will die the death.* By "dying," He means not only the *outward body*, which first became "living" <note>original: "Living"; here meaning the start of a mortal, animal life subject to time and decay rather than spiritual eternity.</note> with the beginning of sin.

256. For the outward body did not fall down instantly when *Adam* transgressed the commandment and died. Instead, he now gained the "great life" and became *lord*. Before, he was weak or powerless, and the true, inner Man was potent or mighty. He formerly walked behind and served the Image of God, acting as a servant. But when the soul introduced the earthly source or quality, then he became *lord*, and the Image <note>The divine likeness or spiritual body</note> was shut up in death.

257. The spirit is the life; the flesh is not the life. The life of the heavenly flesh was God’s Spirit, and the life of the earthly flesh was the spirit of this world.

258. When the earthly essence drew into the heavenly and took dominion, then the heavenly vanished or disappeared. For the spirit of the heavenly departed out of the earthliness into its own principle. Then the Image, which was formed out of the divine substantiality, stood in death—not in the fierce wrath of the death of anger (as if the heavenly substantiality had been ignited by God's anger), but as a vanished, disappeared substance without quality or life.

259. For that which is generated out of *Love* receives no fierce wrath into itself. The substantiality of the Light is the water of eternal life; water produces no fierce wrath, but *quenches* the fierce wrath of the fire.

260. If the heavenly image or substantiality in *Adam* was taken out of the heavenly *limbus* <note>original: "Limbus"; in Böhme’s theology, this refers to the spiritual "matrix" or the essential "stuff" of the heavenly world from which things are produced.</note>, then surely its original *mother* was the water of eternal life. This water originates from the meekness or desire of the Light of God, just as the water in the depths of this world originates from the meekness of the sun's light through *Venus’s* desire <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, Venus represents the "fifth property" of nature: the desire for love and attraction that draws spiritual light into physical form.</note>.

<summary>Böhme argues that when Adam sinned, his spiritual, heavenly "Image" did not become sinful but rather became dormant or "dead" as his earthly, physical nature took control. He asserts that this heavenly substance is derived from God's love and light, which cannot be consumed by wrath.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s explanation of how the human soul became entangled with earthly matter and lost its original divine image. He argues that while the soul’s focus shifted to the "dark body" of this world, the original heavenly substance—which he calls "water"—remained pure but inactive, awaiting regeneration through Christ.</meta>

<page-num>37</page-num>
# I. Defense: How the Water could not take in sin. Part II.

261. What fierce wrath or anger, then, could enter the heavenly substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> of the holy body in *Adam*? Furthermore, that substance was not life itself; rather, the Spirit of God was the true life within the holy body.

262. But when the Spirit of God departed, that Image <note>The divine likeness or spiritual body</note> stood as if dead, *without life*. The soul then lived on earthly "fire-fuel." Although it is not entirely earthly in essence, that earthly essence is generated from the "first principle" <note>In Böhme’s system, the first principle is the dark, fiery source of nature, representing God's strength and wrath before it is lightened by the second principle of love.</note> in which the soul also exists.

263. Therefore, the soul also lusted after that quality <note>original: "source or quality"</note>. The soul had been given a heavenly body to "eat" from, rather than eating from both the heavenly and earthly bodies. It should have placed its desire <note>original: "Lust or longing"</note> and imagination only into the heavenly body; if it had, the soul-fire would have kept the *earthly body*—which belongs to the *dark world*—merely *attached* to it.

<margin>† The outward light of this world.</margin>
264. But when the soul chose to eat from both, the *dark body* gained power and † light, and it ruled over the true human body. Thus, sin began in the soul-fire, for it became ignited with a fierce, wrathful essence. Consequently, the soul-fire burned with that quality, and the divine light of the soul—which once shone in the gentle, heavenly substance—was *extinguished*.

265. In the beginning, the true human essence of the soul was the fuel for its life’s fire; however, later, the *earthly essence* became the fuel. This is what sin and the "opposing will" are. Now, the soul has no image or body that lasts eternally, unless it is reborn <note>original: "Regenerated"</note> through *Christ* out of its original substance, by means of the death of *Christ*.

266. This is why many kinds of *figures* appear in the soul’s inner image, depending on what it desires to be. These can include the images of wild beasts, serpents, or toads. Whatever essence and will the soul-fire *lives* and *burns* within, the *Fiat* <note>original: "FIAT"; the creative power or "let it be" that gives form to desire.</note> in the spirit of the will acts according to that essence and creates such an image. Thus, when the outward body dies, the soul remains in that specific form and quality.

267. During its earthly life, the soul can change its will, and then its *Fiat* changes its *figure*. However, after the death of the body, it no longer has any means to change its will, as can be seen in the case of the devils.

<margin>* John 3:5.</margin>
268. Therefore Christ said, *\*You must be born again through water and the Holy Spirit, or you cannot see the Kingdom of God.* Understand this to mean being born out of God’s water—the water of the original, true Image in which the Holy Spirit dwells, and in which *Christ* was conceived and born.

269. That water did not take sin into its essence, for that is impossible. That which comes from God’s gentleness cannot be ignited by God’s fierce wrath; instead, it remains like a dormant power <note>original: "impotency or weakness"</note> shut up in death—that is, in the stillness, in the *still nothing*.

<summary>Böhme explains that the Fall occurred when the soul's "fire" began consuming earthly essence rather than divine substance, causing the heavenly image to become dormant. He argues that this original purity remains "shut up in death" until a person is spiritually reborn through Christ.</summary>

# II. Part: How the Water Could Not Contain Sin. Defense I.

270. Adam lost the Life—that is, the true Divine Life—of his noble Image. Christ has brought that Life back again; he has generated that Image out of death once more. The living Word from God’s Heart entered into the Image that was shut up in death, and has assumed or taken *that essence* to himself and become a true man—a man to whom the *outward body only clung*. This outward body was swallowed up by the true Image, yet remained manifest in the outward world.

<margin>† Matthew 4:1–2; Mark 1:12; Luke 4:1–2.</margin>

271. With that, he also reclothed the soul in the *holy body*—that is, the innocent or immaculate one. Into that holy body, he took a *human soul* from the essence-seed of *Mary's* soul. Therefore, † *Christ had to be tempted afterward and go without outward food for forty days.*

272. For the soul had to be tempted to test whether, within that holy body, it would eat of God’s substance and satisfy itself. For this reason, the Devil was permitted to tempt the soul.

<margin>* The Devil.</margin>

273. Since the Devil *excused himself, claiming he could not stand firm because the *Matrix* <note>original: "Matrix"; Böhme uses this to mean the generative womb or source of nature</note> of the fierce, wrathful nature had pulled him too hard, he was now to tempt and test *this* man, just as he had tempted and tested *Adam* and overcame him.

<margin>† Matthew 4:8; Luke 4:5–6.</margin>

274. Therefore, God sent another or a second *Adam* and placed him upon the Kingly Throne which he <note>Lucifer</note> once held. There, he was to be tested to see if the Devil could also cause him to fall. † *The Devil now set before him the glory of this outward world—specifically, outward eating or food.*

<margin>* Matthew 4:3; Luke 4:3.</margin>

275. And though such food was not immediately at hand, the Devil suggested that he should use his noble Image and *divine strength* to enter the outward realm and *command stones to become bread*. This was to see whether the Devil could bring it to pass that the noble Image might *yet* become captivated and imprisoned in Death.

<margin>† Matthew 4:6; Luke 4:9.</margin>

276. And then he set before him the great power and authority he could have. He suggested that, through his divine omnipotence within the outward kingdom, he should † *fly from the Temple*. This was to test whether he might lead him into outward lust, so that God’s Spirit of Love might depart from *this* Image. While the Deity was only humble and lowly, the Devil wanted to lead him into pride.

277. Thirdly, he set before him dominion over the outward world. He suggested that he should be a *Lord in the Third Principle* <note>original: "Third Principle"; in Böhme’s cosmology, this refers to the visible, material world of time and space</note>. The Devil wanted him to settle for being a lord only in the inward realm, and told him he should fall down and pray to him or *worship him*.

278. For the Devil was concerned about the Kingly Seat that this man was destined to possess. Therefore, he—the Devil—was permitted to tempt HIM. If Christ stood firm, the Devil would be proven a liar, and judgment would fall upon his own lying mouth or tongue.

<summary>Böhme explains that Christ, as the second Adam, restored the divine Image by successfully resisting the same temptations of pride, power, and material desire that caused the fall of both Adam and Lucifer.</summary>

# Appendix I. How the Life Should Awaken Again in Abraham’s Seed. Part II.

### The Conception and Incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man"</note> of Jesus Christ, with its Circumstances, is as follows.

->279.<-

When the Divine Image in Adam vanished or disappeared, God pitied it and willed that this Image might be restored. He promised Adam and Eve the Crusher of the Serpent—namely, the Word and Power of the Deity—that would take the woman’s seed (meaning the essence of the disappeared Image) into itself. Through this, it would destroy the sting of the Devil and the wrath of God in the soul.

280. That very promised Word nevertheless remained present before the noble Image (which was then shut up in death) and desired its former dwelling house—its own likeness—as a delightful habitation.

281. But through the Promise, the Word placed itself before the soul again in the light of the soul's life. It set a limit or mark <note>original: "Limit or Mark"; Böhme often uses the term "Ziel" (goal/limit) to refer to the predestined point in time and lineage where Christ would enter humanity.</note> there, by which it would enter again into the true human essence that was enclosed in death, and awaken life from death.

<margin>* Or a mark for humanity.</margin>
282. That limit or mark was established in the Virgin Mary. It became blessed through the Word of Promise in Paradise and stood as a center or limit of humanity.

283. God’s Heart had promised and betrothed <note>original: "espoused"</note> or united itself to that limit. That limit became adorned with the highly precious Virgin of the wisdom of God—namely, with the mirror <note>original: "Looking-Glass"</note> or eye of the Holy Spirit. This was not done with anything foreign, but with the *first* life—the divine life—of the noble Image in Adam. From this life, Adam’s soul had departed into the spirit of this outward world—that is, into the qualities of the stars and elements, whose center is the abyss of the first principle.

284. This blessed limit was promised to the Fathers—namely, to Adam, Abraham, David, and others. Oh, how the Prophets delighted and rejoiced in this limit! The sacrifices of the Jews were a type <note>A "type" is a person, object, or event in the Old Testament believed to foreshadow something in the New Testament.</note> of this limit.

285. For when Adam had lost the pure and beautiful Image—meaning the power of God’s Heart, which stood in his body of heavenly substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> as a center of the Deity—the soul then stood only in the Father’s property. This refers to the eternal nature, which without the light of God is a fierce, wrathful, and consuming fire.

286. For the soul originates from that center—that is, out of the eternal nature of the Father. Therefore, the soul in Israel was led for a long time toward that limit or mark in the Father’s nature.

287. The † **Law** on Mount Sinai was given in fire and thunder within the Father's nature, and **Moses** was also called from the \* **bush** by the fire-flame within the Father's nature.

288. And Christ also said this when he came in the flesh: "Father, the **men were yours**, and you have given them to ME, and I give them **eternal life**."

That highly blessed limit or mark <note>original: "Limit or Mark"; Böhme's term 'Ziel' refers to the predestined goal or point of Christ's entry into humanity</note> existed within the covenant of grace through the sacrifices in **Israel**. The sacrifices were a sign or type of the limit which God set before them; and **Israel** was **ransomed from sin** in those sacrifices through that limit or mark.

290. **Israel** offered sacrifices with the blood of **beasts**, and God’s imagination <note>original: "Imagination"; here referring to God's focused creative vision or divine intent</note> looked upon those sacrifices through the limit or mark of his covenant. Since man had become **earthly**, God set this limit or mark before himself as a covenant of grace, so that his imagination might not enter into the earthly source or quality. This prevented his fire of anger from being **awakened** by man's earthliness and sin, which would have devoured them as happened in the time of **Elijah**.

291. The circumcision of the **Jews** was also like this: **Israel** had to shed its blood, and God's imagination looked upon that through the limit or mark of his covenant. For **Christ** was to destroy death by the shedding of **his** blood. That blood would fall into the anger of God—namely <note>original: "viz:"</note>, into the fire of the soul—and quench the **kindled fire of God**.

292. Therefore, God envisioned <note>original: "Imaged or represented"</note> the **blood-shedding of Christ** to himself within the covenant, and with this vision he quenched the fierce wrath in the soul. Through THAT, **Israel** was saved—specifically those who, with earnest sincerity, directed their will and imagination into the covenant. They received or conceived the **power** of the limit or mark in the covenant—that is, within God’s own mental representation.

293. For in God, that which is finished and past and that which is still to come are all one. Therefore, the new regeneration from Christ was reckoned or imputed to the children of the covenant **as if** they already stood in the new body of Christ—as if Christ had already drowned the anger with his blood-shedding, and as if life had already been reborn <note>original: "Generated"</note> out of death once more.

294. For that very life from the limit or mark stood in God’s imagination; it established itself there through the promise in Paradise. That very life was promised to **Abraham**, that it should be awakened again in his seed—not in a foreign seed, as the slanderer <note>original: "Libeller"; likely referring to a contemporary critic of Böhme's theology</note> imagines, but in the **seed of the noble image**. This image was given to **Adam** as a body from the heavenly substantiality <note>the divine essence or "spiritual matter"</note> out of the second principle <note>the world of light and love</note>.

<margin>† Ephesians 4:24.</margin>
295. And yet, when the soul entered into earthliness, that image became shut up in **still** death, as if it were nothing. It was meant to sprout out of death again, and in that rising be born as **a new man**, † in holiness, innocence, and righteousness.

## Part II. How we must sprout with the Lily. Defense I. <note>original: "Apol. I."; referring to Böhme's first Apologia or defense against his critics.</note>

304. If you would grow and sprout, like the Noble Lily Branch, out of the *Old Tree*, you must bring a humble heart. You must stand within the Incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man"</note> of Christ if you wish to grow, spring up, and speak from God.

<margin>† John 1:18.</margin>
305. For no one knows anything of God except the Spirit of Christ who is in God. As the Son in the bosom of the Father † searches out even the depths of the Deity within our own spirit, our spirit must also stand in the Spirit of Christ if we wish to understand the Divine Mystery.

306. <note>The OCR originally numbered this 305.</note> It is not enough for people to collect a heap of Scripture *texts* and create an opinion and meaning out of them. 307. In opinions, there is mere *doubting* whether a thing is right or not. Out of opinions, the *Antichrist* is generated. If we wish to speak of God, then we must speak from the *Spirit of Christ*, which alone knows what God is; otherwise, we are absolute **liars**.

<margin>* The one Eternal Element.</margin>
308. Christ’s Spirit must speak through us concerning the Divine Mystery, or else we speak out of the Babel of Confusion. Christ became *man* in our true human essence—meaning, in Adam's essence. Only the "Limit or Mark" <note>The "Limit" refers to the appointed time and person—Mary—destined for this event.</note> stood in *Mary*; that was the blessing. For, in that Limit, was the Living Word and the Spirit of God, surrounded and clothed with the Noble Virgin of the Wisdom of God <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in Böhme’s thought.</note> in the Divine Substantiality.

That Word was clothed with divine substantiality from the Water of Eternal Life, generated out of the gentleness of the Light of God's Majesty.

# I. Defense: God's Substantiality has been from Eternity. Part II. <note>original: "Apol. I."; referring to Böhme's first Apologia or defense against his critics.</note>

312. And within that *Substantiality* <note>term: Substantiality; for Böhme, this refers to the spiritual "matter" or heavenly essence of God's realm</note> was the *Tincture* <note>term: Tincture; a vital spiritual force or "inner quality" that gives life, color, and radiance</note> from the Fire and Light of God, which is the radiance, shine, and ornament of that essence.

313. And within the *Tincture* was the chaste, modest *Eye* of the wisdom of God. This wisdom is the *Holy Spirit’s embodiment* <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> in which he dwells. It is his eternal *mirror* <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"</note> in which he has recognized or perceived the great *wonders* from eternity.

314. And the Holy Spirit has proceeded from the Word—that is, out of the *Center* or Heart of God. He comes from the Father—that is, out of the *Fire* through the *Light* into the *Majesty* <note>term: Majesty; the radiant glory of God’s presence</note>, and into the essence of the paradisiacal and angelic world. Understand this as the pure Element, the *substantiality* of the heavenly *body*.

315. This very substantiality or embodiment, as just mentioned, was *Christ's* heavenly flesh and blood. For the noble Tincture turns the *water* from the divine glory into spiritual blood.

316. That very substantiality, which was in the Covenant where the promised Word of God stood, has *entered* into *Mary's* substantiality—that is, into the essence enclosed in death. It has become a body and has made that which was shut up *living* again. The divine and heavenly paradisiacal substantiality in the Covenant and *Mary's* substantiality have become ONE thing; Life sprouted or grew within Death.

317. Therefore, Christ has become our Life and Spirit, and also our Flesh and Blood. Therefore, he gives us—meaning our soul's fire—his heavenly body and blood to eat and to drink. With the *entrance* of the divine substantiality, our soul has again received heavenly flesh for its fire-life. It burns again in the divine source or essence out of the *substantiality of love*.

318. The holy *Tincture*, according to the property of the divine *fire*, belongs to the soul. The property of the water—that is, the gentleness of the Light—belongs to the body. The body is always under or beneath the soul.

319. For the soul comes out of the eternal fire of nature; it is the principle between the dark and light worlds. It contains the *center* of the fire-world within itself.

## Part II. God’s Substantiality has existed from Eternity. Defense I. <note>original: "Apol. I."; referring to Böhme's first Apologia or defense against his critics.</note>

321. ...it brings it through the sharpness <note>term: sharpness; Böhme’s term for the harsh, creative tension or "sting" within the first principle of nature</note> of the Father, and there it goes through death again out into the *Liberty* <note>term: Liberty; the "Ungrund" or the absolute stillness and freedom of God that exists beyond the driving forces of nature</note>, and creates the source-quality of the divine world; for the Spirit of God is understood to be within it.

322. It is not that there is an actual dying or death within it, but the fire-quality <note>original: "Fire-source"</note> is considered a "death." For the root of the fire is the "Dark World" with its harsh forms, which stands in contrast to the fire-nature. This is explained at length in the book *Six Points of the Great Mystery* <note>original: "Six Points of the Great Mysterie"; referring to Böhme's work *Six Theosophical Points*</note>.

323. Now understand the meaning correctly: God’s substantiality <note>term: substantiality; the spiritual "matter" or heavenly essence of God’s realm</note> has existed from eternity. It is unmeasurable and unfathomable; it is everywhere. Wherever a person can say "here is God," the divine substantiality is also there. However, it is not found in the outward world of the *Third Principle* <note>term: Third Principle; the visible, physical universe</note>, but in the heavenly *Second Principle* <note>term: Second Principle; the kingdom of light and love</note>.

<margin>John 3:13</margin>
324. Therefore Christ said in John 3:13, *“No one has ascended into heaven except the Son of Man who came down from heaven, and who is in heaven.”* His divine substantiality was in heaven, and yet it had entered into humanity—whereas humanity, on its own, is dead in *Adam* <note>Adam represents the fallen state of mankind, separated from the divine life</note>.

<margin>Genesis 28:12</margin>
325. Now, if anyone wishes to enter heaven, they must have his substance upon them. He is the *ladder* that Jacob saw, which reached to heaven at one end and into humanity at the other.

326. One should understand it this way: the body of Christ—that is, the *embodiment* <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> of the divine substantiality which revealed itself in the physical substance of human nature in *Mary*—is *greater than ALL.* <margin>John 10:29, 30</margin>

327. The divine substantiality did not enter entirely into the created image; that would be impossible, for it is unmeasurable. Instead, it revealed itself in human substance within the created image during the incarnation <note>original: "Becoming Man"</note> of Christ. It "kindled" the human element and gave it life—specifically into Adam's image, which was also in Mary and in all people.

->centered text<-
*Question.*

328. Now it may be asked: What kind of person was *Mary*, since the "Limit" <note>term: Limit; the "Mark" or boundary of the Covenant—the specific point in history and lineage where God's promise of a Savior was to be fulfilled</note> of God’s Covenant was placed in her? Or, how did Christ receive a body and soul in *her* and yet remain what he was from eternity?

->centered text<-
*Answer.*

329. Mary was, first, a physical descendant and daughter of *Eve* (the mother of us all), and of her biological mother *Anna* and her biological father *Joachim*. She was not an "immaculate, pure virgin" in the sense of the outward world, for the "Anger of God" <note>term: Anger of God; the first, harsh principle of nature that requires reconciliation with the light</note> also resided in her. She is redeemed and reconciled through the blood of Christ.

330. And according to the Second Principle, her image also stood shut up in death. But the "Limit" or "mark" stood in her—meaning in her image—though it was indiscernible and unperceivable. It was there in the same way that God is in all things, yet the thing itself knows nothing of him.

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s theological explanation of the Incarnation, specifically focusing on how the divine nature interacted with Mary’s human nature. # I. Defense: How the Heart of God was the Center in Christ. Part II. <note>original: "Apol. I. Part II."; referring to Böhme’s first "Apologia" or defense against his critics.</note>

For God does not dwell in the physical thing; he possesses nothing but himself. This is how the "limit" or "mark" <note>term: Limit or Mark; Böhme's term (German: *Ziel*) for the specific point or spiritual boundary where the divine promise was focused and where the Incarnation would occur</note> existed in Mary. God's promise in the Word of Life was within that limit or mark, yet it did not dwell *as* Mary, but within itself.

331. From all eternity, God had never moved himself according to his Heart <note>term: Heart; Böhme's way of referring to the second person of the Trinity, the Son, as the center of divine love</note>. But once he moved himself within the "mark" in Mary, then Mary became highly blessed. Through this blessing, she became pregnant <note>original: "impregnate"</note> with the Savior. For the Life entered into Death—that is, into the human essence that was enclosed in death.

332. At that time, the human seed still operated within the body. When the divine Life entered the essence of Mary's seed, her whole body—specifically the "body of the Image" <note>term: Image; the true spiritual form of a human as originally created by God, distinct from the fallen physical body</note> according to the *Second Principle*—became highly blessed. Through this wondrous new entrance and movement of God, it was brought to life, so that her essence became living. The "tincture" <note>term: tincture; a spiritual essence or life-force that gives quality, color, and power to a substance</note> of her blood was ignited by the divine tincture. This refers to the seed's tincture, which interacts with the entire body.

333. However, the outward kingdom of this world was not at this time broken off from Mary; it still held her captive. She had to enter eternal life through dying—specifically through her Son's death.

334. Her body did not simply vanish or disappear, for it was centered within the blessing. Instead, the earthly source-quality <note>term: source-quality; the inherent driving force or characteristics of a substance (German: *Quellbrunn*)</note> in her had to break or decay. All of Adam’s children must enter into life through one and the same entrance: the death of Christ. When Christ quenched the "soul-fire" <note>term: soul-fire; the intense, driving spiritual energy of the human soul which, in a fallen state, is a "fire" separated from God's light</note> on the cross in death, Mary's soul-fire was also quenched—meaning it was properly ignited in the Light of the divine Majesty.

335. The outward body remained as a covering over it as long as it existed within the quality of the stars and elements <note>note: Böhme refers to the physical world as being governed by the "stars and elements"</note>. Through death, the outward substance of that quality is broken away, and then the Image of God appears or shines forth.

336. Understand this correctly: in Mary, Christ took all *three principles* <note>term: three principles; Böhme’s system of the First Principle (the fire/soul), the Second Principle (the light/spirit), and the Third Principle (the physical world)</note> onto himself. But he did so in divine order, not mixed together as Adam did. Adam introduced the outward kingdom into the inward soul-fire through his imagination, which caused the light to be extinguished.

337. Upon himself—that is, upon the "mark" of the living covenant—he assumed the soul’s essence (the *First Principle*) into the living substantiality. He then took the essence of the Image (the *Second Principle*) and the outward kingdom (the *Third Principle*), for he was meant to be Lord of all.

338. At the end of four months <note>note: early modern biology often held that the soul entered the fetus at the end of the fourth month of pregnancy</note>, he became a living soul, which then resided within the Image. But the Deity was the center of that Image—a center which can neither be added to nor diminished.

<summary>Böhme explains that in the Incarnation, Christ assumed all three principles of existence (divine, soulful, and physical) in perfect order, unlike Adam who corrupted them. He clarifies that Mary remained in her physical body until death, but her spiritual "Image" was revitalized by the divine presence.</summary>
