## II. Part: How the Heart of God was the Center in Christ. Defense I. <note>original: "Apol. I."; referring to Böhme’s first *Apologia* or formal defense against his critics.</note>

The Divine Substantiality <note>term: Divine Substantiality; Böhme's concept of the spiritual "matter" or holy substance of God's kingdom</note> *also* receives neither addition nor reduction; it becomes neither smaller nor larger. It has only manifested or revealed itself in the human Image <note>term: Image; the true spiritual form of humanity as originally created by God</note> and brought it to *Life*.

339. Thus, in *Mary’s* conception, a *Living Essence* arose within her seed that was no longer shut up in death, nor was it a sinful one. For where God’s light shines forth, there is no sin within. Sin originates in that place where God’s light does *not* shine; but where it shines, there is pure love and gentleness <note>original: "meeknesse"</note>.

340. The Heart of God <note>term: Heart of God; Böhme’s term for the Son, the second person of the Trinity, representing divine love</note> was the *center* in the person of Christ. The essences were *sanctified* and enlightened by the movement of the Deity. Understand this according to the *Second Principle* <note>term: Second Principle; the realm of light and divine love, as opposed to the "First Principle" of darkness/wrath or the "Third Principle" of the physical world</note>. For the divine and human essences became flesh and blood and became a man—one single person.

<margin>* Philippians 2:7.</margin>
341. The outward kingdom was attached to the inward, but in this Person, the inward held the dominion; the outward was the servant. Therefore the Scripture says, *he took upon himself the form of a servant* <note>original: Philippians 2:7</note>, so that he might release us from servitude or bondage.

342. Thus, I say: in what Christ is according to our human image and according to the soul, he is a creature like us, taken from us. But in what he is according to the Deity and according to the Divine Substantiality, he is *above* nature and higher than the heavens; in that respect, he is no creature, but GOD himself.

343. But his divine substance IS manifest WITHIN his creature—that is, within his humanity. According to his humanity, he is the same kind of person as *Adam* was before his "imagination" <note>term: Imagination; for Böhme, this refers to Adam’s desire turning away from God toward the material world, which caused the Fall</note> and Fall; he is the second *Adam*.

344. The *first* Adam was meant to possess the kingly seat, but since he did not remain steadfast, God generated for himself another or second Adam out of the *first*. Now, if he had not been "natural" <note>term: Natural; possessing the actual physical and psychological properties of a human being</note>, he would have been unlike the first Image, and he would not have been the Son of Man, as the libeler <note>term: Libeller; Böhme’s term for his critic, Balthasar Tilke, who accused him of heresy</note> supposes.

345. Had he not possessed a natural soul, then he would not have had all the Three Principles <note>term: Three Principles; the three dimensions of reality: 1) the dark fire/wrath, 2) the light/love, and 3) the physical/outer world</note> within his *person*. What, then, would he have committed into the hands of his *Father* at the moment he died on the cross? Or what would have suffered on the wood of the cross, if he had not been natural?

<margin>† Luke 24:39.</margin>
346. When he had risen from the dead, he showed himself to his disciples and said, † *Behold me; a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see me have* <note>original: Luke 24:39</note>. Why then does the libeler say that it is I who would make Christ "natural" according to his holy, immaculate humanity? I am not the first to call him natural. He is my brother and the Son of Man; therefore, he must certainly be natural. Yes, even the angels are natural <note>note: Böhme means that even angels possess a "nature" or a specific kind of spiritual substance, rather than being mere abstractions</note>.

347. But as for what he says I have written: *that he became a man in the "wild," that is, in the outward birth;*

->**Part II. How Christ is Natural. Apology I.**<-

364. You must understand the *birth* or generation of the Holy *Trinity* if you intend to judge it. You must also understand the *Dark-World*, the fierce wrath and the *love* of God, what God is in love and anger, and what a devil or an angel is—and how he came to be a devil.

365. Also, you must understand the mystery of the *Divine Wisdom* <note>term: Wisdom; often referred to as "Sophia" by Böhme, representing the mirror or divine imagination of God.</note>. Especially, you must understand how the *dear name* of God originates from *eternity*, and how the *nothing* becomes introduced into nature, so that out of the "nothing," a source or quality <note>term: Source or Quality; Böhme uses the word "source" (German: *Quell*) to describe the distinct spiritual forces or "flavors" that make up existence.</note> comes to be. If you do not understand THESE things, then stay home with your personal conceits. Read my book, *The Threefold Life of Man*, and you will see with other eyes.

366. Christ says: *You must be born anew through water and the Holy Spirit, otherwise you cannot see the Kingdom of God.* He says, *YOU*, not some stranger—YOURSELF!

<margin>NOTE.</margin>
367. No *other* strange creature comes into us when we are born out of Christ. Instead, when we put our whole desire into God—into the incarnation <note>original: "becoming Man"</note> of Christ, into his suffering and dying—and become sorry for our sins and desire God's mercy in Christ, then our soul’s Will-Spirit <term>Will-Spirit; the soul's active desire and driving force</term> goes out from sin and evil (or malice) and enters into the incarnation of Christ. That is, it enters into the heavenly substantiality <term>Substantiality; the spiritual "matter" or essence of the heavenly realm</term>, which is *greater* than everything else. There, the Will-Spirit comes before the center—that is, before the Heart of God.

368. That Heart of God is *desirous* of humanity, and it grasps the Will-Spirit with its desire for humanity. Thus, the Will-Spirit receives the power of the center—a spark of divine power.

These remain throughout time, struggling with one another for control of the image. 457. The fire-source, or its quality, is fierce wrathfulness and it devours everything that enters it. The Dark World is a mere, fierce, wrathful *hunger*. But the Light World is pure *Love*. *Man has all three of these in his center.*

My critic <note>original: "Libeller"</note>, open your eyes and observe that by "eternal nature," out of which the angels were created, I do not mean the **Divine Principle**. Nothing can be created out of the light; a thing that is *substance* can only be created out of substantiality—that is, out of meekness.

487. Yet a *living spirit* cannot be made out of substance; life is not substance, but a *desire* for substance.

488. A spirit—as angels and souls are—comes out of the *Magia* <note>original: "Magia," Böhme’s term for the creative, magical power of desire</note> or desire of the fire-source or quality. 489. The *Center* is a desire for the manifestation of the Abyss <note>original: "Abysse," meaning the bottomless, ungrounded source of all being</note> into a foundation, of the "Nothing" into "Something," in order to manifest or reveal the hidden mystery of the eternal divine substance.

490. The Light has another *Center*. By the Light, "God" is understood or meant. The Heart of God is the *Center* of the Light, and the magical desire is the *Center* of the Fire. In the Fire, the "Liberty"—that is, the "Nothing"—becomes *manifested* (to speak in a way that creatures can understand).

491. In respect to the creature, God is as a "Nothing," and yet He is indeed EVERYTHING. In the fire, His majesty becomes manifest; in the fire is the finding of the "Nothing." God Himself finds Himself from eternity within Himself. Regarding the name "God," He is not nature; rather, nature becomes born or generated in the will of the eternal "Nothing."

492. There is only one Will, which is the Abyss. It desires a foundation or ground—that is, the manifestation or revelation of itself. In that desire, nature becomes manifested. The desire creates the nature, which drives itself from one desire to another; one form of desire creates the next, all the way to the fire. There, the "Principle" and "Life" are generated.

493. The *Fiat* <note>original: Latin for "let it be done"; here referring to the creative word or power of God</note> is the mother—that is, the desiring or the "hunger," as one might call it. It causes the desire to become substance according to the form of its property. It shapes the willing into a form or figure, in which we understand the *Center* of the spirit.

515. Consequently, the soul had nothing in the substance of this world with which it could kindle the eternal fire-source or quality, except for earthly substance. 516. But as for what belonged to its **Center** or origin, the soul was in the Dark World—that was its foundation—while according to the outward light, it was in this world. And so, when the body passes away, the sun-light is destroyed, and the soul **stands naked** in the Dark World.

517. Therefore, God brought **Divine** substantiality into the faded, disappeared image of man, and brought it into the anger—namely, into the fire of the Father’s nature. From this, the noble image rises again out of death into another world—namely, into the Liberty, which is outside of, beside, or beyond nature, into the light of the **Majesty**.

518. Just as the power—namely, the **Second Center** [the Son]—arises out of the death of the fire of the Father into another world—namely, into itself—so also does the noble image of man. It is all but one and the same entrance into the Divine Life.

# I. Apology: Fierce Wrath against Fierce Wrath. Part II.

553. The Soul is free, and God *draws everyone* who leans toward him. When the soul enters into him, then it *is chosen* <note>original: "Elected"</note> for the World of Light. So long as the Will remains in the intense wrath of the Dark World, covered by the outward world, *so long* God does not will it, and the soul is not drawn. But when it turns itself toward God’s Face and does even a little *imagine* <note>In Böhme’s terminology, "imagination" is the power of the soul to form itself into a specific state through its will.</note> into God’s Love, then the Divine Life starts to stir.

554. Understand that the *Word* has become *human* or Incarnate, and stands in the soul—namely, in the Father’s Principle, in the resonance. For by entering into the Anger, the Word has set the *Mirror* <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"</note> of his Covenant—namely, the Virgin of the *Divine Wisdom*—before the soul, so that the soul should behold itself in it.

555. *Wisdom* says continually, *“Come”*; then the Devil, standing behind, also says, *“Come.”* Now, whichever one the soul goes toward, *by that choice* it becomes chosen as a child.

556. God does not allow any soul (which has light) to extinguish its light because of some predetermined plan. The free will *extinguishes* it. The Devil sets himself in the form of an angel before the soul so that it might *imagine* in evil and good; thus, its imagination eats of evil and good, and so the soul becomes blind and *held captive* in its imagination.

557. Otherwise, if God did harden anyone out of a predetermined plan, or if he *let* someone's light *extinguish* because of a predetermined plan, then what David says in the 5th Psalm would not be true: *You are not a God who wills evil.* Indeed, he *permits* it to happen that an honest, virtuous man becomes evil; when the will leans toward evil, then he lets that man's light go out.

<margin>† John 1:12.</margin>

As long as a man lives in *this* Tabernacle <note>original: "Tabernacle"; a biblical metaphor for the physical human body.</note>, he has the power to become the child of God. For the Apostle also says this: *† He has given us power to become the children of God.*

559. Understand, this does not come from the will of the *flesh*—that is, the *outward* world, which does not belong to God's kingdom—but from the will of the *soul’s spirit*, which becomes generated or born in God. For God's predetermined purpose is that the right Divine Will should always be generated out of the soul. This is done when the soul *enters* into the incarnation of Christ, in which it is generated or born again to be God's child.

## II. Part. We should walk in Love. Apol. I.

560. For the soul's fire becomes introduced into *Christ’s* death, and sprouts again with a new, fair blossom out of the death of Christ into *divine liberty*—into the angelic world.

<margin>† John 6:54</margin>
561. That very blossom, or *spiritual will*, is God’s will. In that very will-spirit, the soul is an angel, for it possesses the *Second Principle* <note>In Böhme’s system, the "Second Principle" is the world of light and divine majesty, distinct from the "First Principle" of dark, fiery power.</note>—namely, God’s majesty. It continually takes in *divine substance*—namely, *Christ’s flesh*—which fills the heavens, so that the soul † *eats of Christ’s flesh and drinks his blood (John 6)* out of the water of the *gentleness* <note>original: "Meeknesse"</note> *of eternal life*.

562. Therefore, I say with good reason: it is not God’s predestined, intended will that any person becomes *lost*. Instead, loss comes from the will of his fierce wrath and anger, and from the dark world and the devil.

563. Therefore, anyone who will *judge* and blame God is a false or wicked *judge* and an advocate of God’s anger. Such a person does not know the difference between what God is in love and what he is in anger, and does not know where an evil or good will originates <note>original: "Originateth"</note>—yet they still want to be a judge. Such a person cries out continually, "It is God, God, who does this thing!"

564. The Prophets and Apostles often called the *total God*—according to both LOVE and anger, as well as according to all the three principles—by ONE WORD ("God"). However, a person should use right understanding and make a distinction between God’s love-will and his anger-will.

565. We see very plainly in *humanity* that a person wills both evil and good. He would always like to be an angel, but he would also like to have pride, greed <note>original: "Covetousnesse"</note>, and the power of this world. People should search for where *every will* takes its origin, and not always say, "God, God, God wills it."

<margin>* Matthew 7:12; 22:37–40</margin>

567. On the contrary, his fierce wrath and anger, which is the *root* of the outward world, wills *its own kind*—seeking fuel or wood for its fire.

568. Since God’s love has set before humanity the mirror <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"</note> of his wisdom through his becoming human (the Incarnation), why then does anyone go into the *anger*-mirror and let the devil sway them? God indeed sends prophets and teachers out of his predestined purpose who reveal and signify his anger to the world; why then do people follow *sin*?

585. The matter is not only about *high knowledge*, but about the taste or relish—that one becomes the "Bread of God" which God eats. It lies very little in knowing, but entirely in DOING. There must be action; the evil branches must be cut off so that good wine may grow.

# I. Apology <note>original: "Apol." - An 'apology' in this context is a formal defense of one's beliefs.</note>: We should walk in Love. Part II.

587. My profound knowledge does not make me happy or saved, for I do not know my *self* through my own power. It is not mine, but God’s Spirit that knows *itself* in me, and he draws me to himself with that knowledge; when he departs or withdraws, then I know nothing.

588. I have not received my knowledge from man at all. Why should I then argue long with man about it? No man can either give it to me or take it away from me.

589. I act foolishly by arguing with you, for you can take nothing from me. But I do this for the sake of other people who abuse my knowledge through your words; otherwise, I would not lift a finger in response to your cursings and judgments.

590. You should walk <note>original: "Converse"</note> in love as a Christian if you want to be God’s child. But if you judge your brother to hellfire for the sake of his *gift*, what will become of you? How do you know what has happened to him, or why he follows this path? How do you know upon what branch or root God has grafted him? You were not present at all when he sowed the *spirit of his wisdom*.

591. You say it comes from the Devil, and yet there was joy in heaven—in the Holy Ternary <note>original: "in Ternario Sancto"; the "Holy Ternary" refers to the Trinity or the divine manifestation within Böhme's mystical framework</note>, especially in the Father’s nature—when this seed was sown. I would NOT give the little grain that was sown in me for all this world’s goods. It is dearer to me than heaven and earth, and yet you tread it underfoot; just look at what kind of "angel" you are.

592. You write much, but if you were to go with your writings to the center <term>The "center" in Böhme’s thought is the inner generative source or core of divine and natural existence.</term>, there would be nobody home. You gather many texts of Scripture together—which are good in themselves—just so you might establish a preconceived opinion for which you have no foundational understanding.

593. You cannot bring that opinion into the center and then bring it out again; there is no spirit of depth in you, only collected material from other people’s mouths, and your own mouth does not even understand it.

594. But I write what I myself understand, and what I can bring into the foundation of the *center*.

595. Are you a master? Then *show* yourself to be one. Give me a writing concerning the *center* of the eternal and also of outward nature; let it be *seen* what you can do. Prove it in the light of nature <term>A Böhmean term for the innate intelligence within the natural world that reveals divine truths.</term>, and not from another person's mouth. Speak from your *own knowledge*, and then I will answer you.

596. Stop your contempt, and direct your efforts to the honor of God. Make them serve the *profit* and *salvation* of man, so that your work may be a sprout upon God’s table. If you do, I will answer you in a way that will make you *wonder*; and if you are sincere, you will greatly *rejoice*. You would then seek—and find—no Devil in *me*.

606. My critic <note>original: "Libeller"</note>: you suppose that at the day of the Last Judgment, a different kind of man will arise than the one *Adam* was before the Fall. 608. Tell me: if we were created animal-like in *Adam*, where does this shame come from? Why is the poor soul ashamed of the body’s deformity and of its way of reproducing?

609. Do you not say that those members were revealed on *Adam* and *Eve* after they sinned, and that <margin>* Genesis 3:7</margin> *they were ashamed*? This was because they saw that, according to the outward man, they had become like beasts. They did not see what the outward *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be done," referring to God's creative word</note> had made during the "sleep" until the earthly source or quality *awakened*. Then the soul became ashamed that an angel had turned into a beast.

610. As long as the earthly kingdom remained hidden, the soul did not know it. But when the earthly kingdom was drawn into the soul, then sorrow and horror began before the Abyss; for the soul saw its own root, which the outward body and spirit did not understand.

611. Or do you suppose that *Adam* was created for mortality? Oh, no! It is expressed at length in the book *The Incarnation of Christ*, in the book *The Threefold Life*, and also in *The Three Principles*; read it there.

### II. Part. God's Spirit is the same still. Apology I.

623. God has, in Christ, regenerated us in Love, not in his fire-property <note>original: "fires property"; in Böhme’s theosophy, the "fire-property" refers to the harsh, consuming, and wrathful aspect of God's nature, which must be tempered by the "light" of Love</note>; so that we should meet together with one another with a modest and amiable condescension and behavior, in a friendly will and intention, and heartily admonish one another as brothers.

624. We should help up the weak and *erroneous*, and friendly instruct them in the way; we should not plunge them from the narrow path into the water, or else cast them into God's anger in hellfire, as the critic <note>original: "Libeller"</note> does, where he says, "*Hellfire is yours*."

<margin>* Matthew 5:22.</margin>
625. Christ says: *Whoever says to his brother "you fool," he is guilty of hellfire, or "Raca" <note>original: "Racha"; an Aramaic term of contempt meaning "empty-headed" or "worthless"</note>, he is guilty of the Council <note>original: "Councill"; referring to the Sanhedrin, the high court of justice</note>*; what is he worthy or guilty of, who calls his brother a devil, and judges or condemns him to *hellfire*? O Man! Consider yourself; turn away from such wicked paths.

<margin>† Or Ladder.</margin>
626. We indeed have here in this valley of misery—before us in the way of our *pilgrimage*—a very small, narrow † bridge <note>marginal note: Or Ladder</note> into God's kingdom. Why should we ourselves be the first to throw one another down? If one goes astray, then let the other show him the way; let us deal with one another as brothers.

627. We are all born blind; so then, if light is afforded us by *Grace*, why then does one brother not afford *eyes* to the *other*? *Everyone sees* as God has favorably afforded him, according to the *sight given* to him; why will one brother hate the other because he does not know what the Lord has given to him?

628. O, how *miserable* is this time of ours! How the Devil hunts for us with *snares* and *nets*, so that one *brother* reproaches, despises, condemns, and flays the *other*, that he may captivate us in *God's anger*. How he does not grant us the high honor which he once had, but lost through pride!

629. Dear brothers, beware of pride, especially those who are *produced out of much learning and knowledge*; it is the pride of *Reason*, and it is man's *worst* enemy. It has set up nothing but wars and the contempt of others.

<margin>
* Sirach 3:18.
† Verse 28.
† Proverbs 16:18.
* A foolish Virgin.
</margin>
630. *Sirach* <note>original: "Syrach"; referring to the Book of Sirach or Ecclesiasticus in the Apocrypha</note> says: *The higher you are, the more humbly behave yourself; † Pride goes before a fall.* Our reason-knowledge is folly if God's Spirit in us does not kindle the knowledge. If I knew all Scriptures outwardly, and did not have the Spirit of understanding, what would my knowledge be other than a *conceit* <note>original: "Conceit"; here meaning a mere mental fabrication or vanity rather than true spiritual insight</note>?

631. It is not divine knowledge when someone confirms an opinion with many texts of Scripture collected and put together; for every text has its proper understanding in the place it stands, according to the *matter* treated of. Oftentimes it signifies much otherwise than the purpose for which it is drawn by someone to support HIS opinion.

632. Right knowledge consists in this: where anyone intends to judge, his knowledge in him should be confirmed by the Spirit of God. It must go forth from the *Center* <note>In Böhme’s writing, the "Center" is the inner spiritual source where the soul meets God</note>, and not from a strange mouth.

# I. Apology: God’s Spirit is the same still. Part II.

633. Or do you suppose that God’s Spirit has ceased to speak? Or that it is dead? So that the Spirit, which moves in God’s vision, dares not say any more: *Thus says the Lord*.

634. The Spirit shows the person what they should speak; it only guards and defends itself from the intermixing of the Spirit of this world and from the imagination of the Devil, so that the true human will-spirit—which goes out from the soul's fire into the Light—is not infected with its malice or curse.

<margin>* Psalm 18:10</margin>
635. There is no better medicine or antidote than the desire for love and humility. As long as the spirit proceeds and judges in love and humility within the vision of the divine power, its word is God's Word, for it is approved by the Spirit of God. It goes upon the *wings of the wind* in the pure human will-spirit, as David says: *The Lord rides upon the wings of the wind.*

636. You find in no prophet or apostle that any has spoken from another’s mouth, but rather from their own gift. Sometimes the Spirit has introduced a text and thereby clarified other Scriptures, but the main matter has been set down from their own spirit and mouth.

637. Who has prohibited us from daring to speak from the gifts of our spirit, insisting instead that we should only speak with a foreign <note>original: "strange"</note> mouth from our spirit, as the critic <note>original: "Libeller"</note> would have it?

638. Who has made a law that a man should take away the speech from the Spirit and change it into another form, except for the Antichrist? He has set himself up as Lord over God’s Spirit and has changed the speech of the holy children into *his own* style and will.

<margin>* NOTE.</margin>
639. Indeed, the high Apostles did not command this. Instead, they said: *Keep Jesus Christ in remembrance, who died for us and rose again*, and he commanded us to teach and preach that. They have not barred up the spirit of any person, or commanded that their tongue should be entirely changed into *their* words. Indeed, they have all spoken together, each from his own tongue, and yet from one Spirit, which was Christ’s.

640. We still have that very same Spirit today, provided we are born or generated out of him. Does it not dare to speak now what is necessary for this time? What is the reason that the center of the Holy Trinity manifests or reveals itself? It is even humanity’s seeking and desiring.

641. Men strive now over the person of Christ and over **God’s election**, and men raise wars and reproaches about it. God’s love will no longer permit this to be; he would rather manifest or reveal himself so that men might yet see what he does, and leave behind their strife over **God’s will** to enter a true apostolic life. They should no longer contend over knowledge, as has been done for a long time in Babel <note>original: "Babel"; Böhme uses this term to represent the confusion, prideful intellectualism, and sectarian division within the institutional churches of his day</note>.

<summary>Jakob Böhme argues that the Holy Spirit remains active and continues to speak through individuals today, just as it did through the Apostles. He critiques the institutional church ("Babel") for stifling personal spiritual gifts and calls for an end to theological warfare in favor of a humble, apostolic life.</summary>

# A Letter
### Or a
# PREFACE
## To Mr.
# J. D. K.
### *Written when this Treatise was Finished.*

---

->I.<-

Esteemed, truly honorable, and highly learned Sir: after wishing you the grace, love, and mercy of our dear IMMANUEL <note>original: "IMMANUEL" — a Hebrew name meaning "God with us," used as a title for Jesus Christ</note>, as well as all temporal welfare of body, I will not conceal from you, Sir, that I have received and read the book with the appendix. I have considered the opponent's <note>original: "Opposers"</note> understanding, perception, and opinion in the love and fear of God; and I sufficiently understand the mindset with which the man is proceeding, and that he has not understood my writings in the least.

2. Also, I very much pity the man, for he has plunged himself into such a lake regarding the *election* <note>original: "Election" — the theological doctrine concerning how God chooses individuals for salvation</note> of God, from which he certainly cannot escape unless he learns to understand the core <note>original: "Center"</note> of all things or substances.

3. He also goes lamentably astray concerning the *humanity of Christ* and concerning his mother *Mary*. His opinion is quite contrary to our Christian or spiritual faith, upon which our restored salvation stands.

<margin>
John 3:3.
1 John 3.
Hebrews 11.
Jude 8.
Acts 15.
</margin>
4. But I desire from my heart that this man might gain true sight, for he is *passionate* <note>original: "zealous"</note>; then his passion would be profitable. However, the way which he now goes is an *open gate* to all vanity or licentiousness <note>original: "Licentiousnesse" — a lack of moral restraint or disregard for accepted rules</note> and despair; and a severe account must be required of such people who lead men into despair and vanity.

Let us live in this knowledge, so that we may be found as the *first-fruits* of the Lord in Zion <note>original: "SION" — a biblical term for Jerusalem or the community of God's people</note>.

21. Regarding the Lord N. at N., if you should meet him, I ask you to evaluate his spiritual gifts; for he is passionate <note>original: "zealous"</note> and a great seeker of truth. May God grant that he finds what he seeks. I ask you to send the enclosed document to him at the earliest opportunity, which will be a favor to both him and me. <margin>† The first Apology to Balthasar Tylcken regarding the *Aurora*.</margin>
22. Regarding the vicious and spiteful satirical attack <note>original: "Pasquil or Libel" — a pasquil is a public lampoon or satire</note> written by that misguided, passionate person, I have written † twenty-three sheets in response. However, I have *held back* that *answer* until now so that the man would not be publicly embarrassed. I hoped that through the instruction of good people, he might gain some spiritual sight. I have continued to forbid its publication so that, if possible, he might *abandon* his malice or ill-will. Otherwise, if the answer were published, he would have little reason to boast, as he currently thinks he does. In the meantime, give this to him to consider for a moment.

23. If he will not be satisfied with acting in brotherly love, let him be certain that *wherever* God’s love is, His anger is also present. This will show him his error, so that he will be ashamed of it and *wish* he had never started it. But if he remains quiet, then this response may be stored in a known location. He may be certain that I see further than he understands.

24. For a wonderful time is now revealing itself, which is sufficiently indicated in my writings; it is certainly coming. Therefore, it is necessary to act with earnestness and sincerity.

* 1 Timothy 4:10.
Hebrews 11:26.
† Ephesians 6:24.

I willingly *suffer reproach for the sake of the truth* and the honor of Christ, for such suffering is the badge or uniform <note>original: "Livery" — the distinctive clothing worn by a person's servants to show whom they serve</note> of Christ. I send this to you in friendship and commit you, along with † all those who *love JESUS*, to the grace of *Jesus Christ*. Dated July 3, 1621.

# INTRODUCTION
## To the Answer
## To Balthasar Tylcken's Slanderous <note>original: "aspersing"</note> Pamphlet, regarding certain points or conclusions in the book *The Incarnation of Jesus Christ*, which he opposed.

-> **JAKOB BÖHME** <note>original: "JACOB BEHME"</note> <-
-> Warns his Fellow Brothers. <-

> *May the open fountain in the heart of JESUS CHRIST be our nourishment <note>original: "Quickening"</note> and life; and may it bring us into His light in brotherly love and childlike union, so that we may live <note>original: "converse"</note> in His power and virtue, and love and know ourselves in Him.*

---

-> 1. <-

<margin>* 2 Corinthians 5:1, 4</margin>
Dear sirs and brothers in Christ: Words cannot fully describe <note>original: "is not sufficiently to be spoken or written"</note> the dangerous dwelling place where we lie captive—here in the valley of *this earthly tabernacle* <note>original: "this Earthly Tabernacle" — a biblical metaphor for the physical body</note>, in flesh and blood, and in the kingdom of the stars and elements. We are subject to the opposition and assaults of the Devil, and we walk in his dangerous ways through the lusts of flesh and blood, unless the bright Morning Star of the heart of *Jesus Christ* awakens or arises within us.

2. How indeed the *world* so completely departs from the ways

We all see and know this only too well: how their own self-centered *reason*, derived from the stars and elements <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, "stars and elements" refers to the physical, worldly mind as opposed to the eternal, spiritual mind.</note>, sets itself against the open fountain of love in the heart of JESUS CHRIST. 3. 4. And yet one party lives as wickedly as the other. There is no desire for love, concord*, or unity in their hearts—only pride, high status, greed, and vain lust. Therefore, they blaspheme, scandalize, and reproach the children of God, accounting them as *fools* so that they themselves may remain hidden in obscurity.

5. And what is even more horrible is that *divine omnipotence* must serve as a cloak or mantle to hide their wickedness. They cover themselves with it and mix *God’s will* into it, as if *nothing* were done without God’s will, and as if everything were merely God’s purpose or *predestination*—as if He had determined within Himself from eternity what should be manifested in time, whether it be *evil* or *good*.

6. In reality, they understand nothing of God, nor His will or substance. Indeed, they are as blind to it as someone born blind is to the visible things of this world—as is clearly discovered and presented to view in this slanderous <note>original: "aspersing"</note> pamphlet against the book of...

Since he is so zealous, his zeal might then be profitable toward furthering the salvation of man.

8. But so long as he is in such a way as to blaspheme, reproach, and persecute—raging in blindness as *Saul* did—he will achieve nothing. He will only rave against God to his own greatest *condemnation* and will only confound those whom he thinks he is teaching, leading them deeper into darkness.

9. For he has conceived such an opinion in his own reason that it would have been much *better* had he never set it down on paper. 10. They understand nothing of God's will toward good and evil, much less do they know what God is. From this, horrible opinions are concluded. Yet this man, in such confused reason, so shamelessly intends to disgrace and suppress my writings—which have a far deeper ground *than he ever understood*. Therefore, I shall explain it a little to him, to *try* whether he or someone else will thereby become "seeing" in God.

11. This is not with the intent to condemn but to *instruct* from the talent which is given to me by God. For men know very well that I am no doctor from the schools of this world; if it were not given to me, I should not understand it.

12. And though I did not seek it so highly, yet it has been *given* to me without my knowledge. I sought only the fountain of *Christ* and understood nothing of the *mystery* of what THAT was; but now it is also afforded to me as a *favor* to see the Substance of All Substances—in which, without the light of God, I should indeed be blind.

14. Since he begins so craftily <note>original: "artificially" — in this context, meaning with human craft or cunning</note>, and drags **Scripture** by the hair of its head to support him, demanding it serve his will regardless of where the Foundation or Corner-Stone truly lies, or whether there is any such understanding in the cited **terms** or **texts** at all—doing this only so that he may cite Scripture and the letter of the law, trading words for words to cloak his erroneous meaning with a false appearance of authority—and though **many** times in my writings I am not even discussing the specific matter he tries to answer with Scripture, yet he **perverts** my meaning to the exact opposite to make it look suspicious; therefore, I will briefly and summarily answer his **asserted** objections. I do this not to argue with him, but for the consideration of those who read my writings.

<margin>2 Thessalonians 3:2</margin>
15. For a true Christian does not argue with anyone about **religion**. He who argues over words and despises his brother is blind and **does not have the faith**.

16. For FAITH is not a mere historical concept <note>original: "Historicall conceit" — an intellectual belief in the facts of history without a personal spiritual experience.</note>, but a right life. The Spirit of God must be generated in the **Center** through the Principle of the soul, and spring up in the Mystery of the Mind, and rule and shine within it. It must be a **person's** will and deed—yes, it must be their **inward** life and understanding—and a person must be resigned to it. Otherwise, there is no right faith or **divine** understanding in a person, but only fables and **Babel** <note>original: "Babel" — Böhme uses this to signify the "city of confusion" or the false, arguing church.</note>, contention and shouting—tearing and ripping at the husk while never enjoying the kernel.

17. Therefore I say now: Is **God’s Spirit** in my critic? If so, why is he a mocker and a brawler? If he has the **faith**, why then does he despise Christ’s children and **members**, whose **Christianity** is earnest and sincere? Christ said: <margin>John 13:35</margin> † *Love one another; by this, all men shall know that you are my disciples.* Also: <margin>1 Corinthians 5:12</margin> \* *Do you not judge those who are within? God will judge those who are without.* If he is in the Spirit of Christ, why then does he despise the Spirit of Christ? Or has Christ become at odds with himself?

18. Oh, dear sirs and brethren, take this into consideration, and look upon the Holy Scriptures **rightly** in the Spirit of Christ, and then you will find that a truly right Christian has no contention with anyone;

This Desire is the first "Center to Nature," which leads itself into its source-quality, into perceptibility and perception, and finally into the Fire—that is, into the **fourth form** <note>In Böhme’s system, the "Fourth Form" of nature is the fire-flash where darkness is transformed into light</note>. This is described sufficiently in my books, namely: *The Three Principles*, *The Threefold Life of Man*, and the *Second Book of the Incarnation of Christ* (specifically the sections on Christ's suffering and dying), and even more deeply in *The Six Points* <note>original: *Sex Puncta Theosophica*</note>. 46. I also know very well that Fire is the source-quality of every life, but I say that the root of Fire is *dark*. This Dark World is not called **God**, for it is a hostile quality in itself—a *cause* of Nature.

47. Indeed, it belongs to **God**. And **God**—who manifests Himself through the Dark World with the Fire in the Light of His Majesty—is its Lord. For it is generated in the *Desire* of the *Chaos*, out of the Abyss in the "Nothing," and introduced into Darkness through that Desire. But the longing delight of the *Chaos* toward revelation only takes this Sharpness and Fire's power into itself so that it might bring itself again through the *dying* in the fire into the Light. In this fire, the Darkness "dies"—understand this as the *substantiality* of the darkness dying—and it emerges through the Fire into the Light. This creates another, or second, Principle of a different source-quality: namely, *Joy, Meekness, and Love-Desire*.

48. Thus, the dark source-quality (the Spirit) remains within itself as an anguish and pain, and it is called God’s anger and fierce wrath. The kindled Fire at the Center in the *Fourth Form* is called a "Consuming Fire." This is why God calls Himself an angry, jealous, and fiercely wrathful **God**.

# II. Apology to T. The Eternal Virgin, no Procreator. Part. I.

He does not understand my meaning or thoughts; he is at odds with himself.

64. I speak from the *Center*, while he speaks from the substance that is generated. I understand that *Wisdom* is not the *Center* or the "opener," but God’s Spirit is that. To speak in a comparison <note>original: "Similitude"</note>: just as the soul in the body manifests or reveals itself through the substance <note>original: "Essence"</note> of the flesh, and the *flesh* would have no power or strength if there were not a living spirit in it, so also God’s Wisdom is the "spoken-out" substance through which the *power* and the Spirit of God manifest or reveal themselves in forms—meaning *divine forms* and shapes within the *wonders*.

65. She <note>Wisdom</note> indeed generates or bears, but she is not the *Divine Principle* or the *Center* of the *Genetrix* <note>original Latin: "Genetrix," meaning a female parent or procreator</note>; rather, she is the Mother in whom the Father works.

66. Therefore I call her a *Virgin*, because she is the modest chastity and purity of God. She carries no desire backward toward the fire <note>In Böhme's cosmology, "Fire" represents the first principle of God's wrath or raw power</note>; instead, her longing for delight goes forward with or within the *revelation* or manifestation of the Godhead <note>original: "Deity"</note>.

67. She could generate nothing if the Spirit of God did not work in her. Therefore, she is NO *Genetrix*, but the *mirror* <note>original: "Looking-Glass"</note> of the Godhead; the Spirit of God generates within her. He is her life; she is his *chest, cabinet, or body*. She is the Holy Spirit’s *physicality* <note>original: "Corporeity"</note>. Within *her* lie the colors of power <note>original: "Vertue"</note>, for she is the spoken-out substance which the Father grasps out of the *Chaos*—that is, out of himself, outside of, beyond, or before nature in the *Nothing*. He brings this substance forth with the *desire* toward nature, through the *first* principle <note>The realm of fire and potential</note>, through the fire of his power, into the *second* principle <note>The realm of light and love</note>, into the divine power and the light of the Majesty.

68. She is that which the Father, from eternity to eternity, continually *re-grasps* <note>original: "re-comprehendeth"</note>, and which the Father (who is fire and light) introduces into his life-of-fire, into the *center* of his heart.

69. She is the highest substantiality of the *Godhead*. Without her, God would not be manifested or revealed but would only be a *Will*. But through Wisdom, he brings himself into substance, so that he is 
***manifested or revealed to himself.***

70. Therefore I call her a Virgin, since she is in *marriage* with God. She generates *without* a fire-life, for in her the light or the true divine life manifests or reveals itself. She is a virgin of the modest *chastity* and purity of God, and *yet* she is in marriage with God.

71. You subtle, clever school or university of the stars <note>original: "Constellation"; Böhme refers to purely intellectual or "astral" knowledge as opposed to spiritual revelation</note>, if you *understood* the *ground* <note>the fundamental reality or essence</note> here, you would NEED NO more books. EVERYTHING lies within this; the Stone of the Wise Men, or the **Philosopher's Stone**, lies in this place. But first, take off your rough garment, and then you will see it.

## Of the Third Principle, which is the Bride of God: and how the Spirit of God is no Principle and yet is a Principle.

->72.<-

Now when I speak of the Third Principle <note>Böhme’s term for the physical, material world we inhabit</note>, I mean the outward world. Then my opponent says, "*God has made it through his Wisdom*," and proves it by *Scripture*; and I say so too. But I do not speak wordlessly; I explain *from what* it was made, for God has given me the knowledge. It is *not* I myself who know it, but God knows it *in me*.

73. Wisdom is his bride, and the children of Christ—who are in Christ within Wisdom—are also God's bride. Now then, if Christ's Spirit dwells in Christ's children, and if Christ's children are branches on his vine and one body with him, as well as one spirit—whose knowledge is it now? Is it mine or God's? Should I not then know in the Spirit of Christ what this world is created from? If he who created it dwells in me, should *he* not know it?

74. Therefore, I now submit and will know nothing of my own self—that is, in that part of me belonging to the outward world—so that he may know in me whatever he wills. I am not the *procreator* <note>original Latin: *Genetrix*, a female parent or one who brings forth</note> in this knowing, but my spirit is *his wife* or woman, in whom he generates knowledge according to the *measure* he chooses.

75. Just as Eternal Wisdom is the body of God, and he generates within her whatever he wills, so now if he generates knowledge, it is not I who do it, but he in me. I am as if dead in the generating of this knowledge, and he is my life; indeed, I have neither sought it out nor learned it. He inclines himself toward my "me-ness" <note>original: "Minehood," referring to the self-centered ego</note>, and my "I-ness" <note>original: "Ihood," the core of the individual self</note> inclines itself up into him.

76. But now I am "dead" <note>meaning dead to his own ego or selfish will</note> and understand nothing, but he is my understanding. Therefore I say, I live in God and God lives in me, and so I teach and write of him, dear brethren; otherwise, I know nothing.

77. I pray you, bear with my *folly* a little in what I tell you. I do this not for my own boasting, but for your *learning* and knowledge, so that you may know whom you scorn and despise when you deride me. I will not hide it from you, for I mean it from the heart.

78. I have written of three principles <note>In Böhme’s system, the Three Principles are: 1. The dark fire-world (God's wrath/power), 2. The light world (God's love), and 3. The outward world (our physical universe)</note> which are known in me, but only weakly; it has been with me like a student who goes to school.

The Spirit of God generates within her; he is her life, and she is his chest, *cabinet*, or body. She is the Holy Spirit’s corporeality; in *her* lie the colors of virtue, for she is the spoken-forth substance which the Father comprehends out of the *chaos*—that is, out of himself, without, besides, beyond, or before nature in the "Nothing." He brings this substance forth with the desire for nature, through the eternal nature, through the *first* principle (the fire of his might), into the *second* principle (the divine power), and into the light of the *Majesty*.

68. It is that which the Father, from eternity to eternity, continually *re-comprehendes*, which the Father (who is a fire and light) introduces into his fire-life, to the *center* of his Heart.

69. She is the highest substantiality of the *Deity*; without her, God would not be manifested or revealed, but would be only a *Will*. But through Wisdom, he brings himself into substance, so that he is *manifested* or *revealed to himself*.

70. And therefore I call her a Virgin, since she is in the *marriage* with God; so that she generates *without* a fire-life, for in her the Light (the true divine life) manifests or reveals itself. She is a Virgin of the modest *chastity* and purity of God, and *yet* is in the marriage with God.

71. You subtle, prudent school or university of the stars <note>original: "from the Constellation," referring to scholars who rely on worldly or astrological wisdom rather than spiritual insight</note>: if you *understood* the ground of this matter, you would NEED NO more books. ALL lies herein. The Stone of the Wise Men, or the *Philosopher's Stone* <note>A legendary substance in alchemy capable of turning base metals into gold and achieving immortality; here used as a metaphor for the ultimate spiritual truth</note>, lies in this place. But first, put off your rough garment, and then you will see it.

## Of the Third Principle, which is the Bride of God: and how the Spirit of God is no Principle and yet is a Principle.

->72.<-

Now when I speak of the Third Principle, I mean the outward physical world. My opponent says, "*God has made it through His Wisdom*," and proves it by Scripture; and I say so too. But I do not remain silent; I explain *from what* it was made, for God has given me this knowledge. It is not I myself who knows it, but God knows it *within me*.

73. Wisdom is His Bride, and the children of Christ are also God’s Bride because they are in Christ within that *Wisdom*. Now then, if Christ’s Spirit dwells in Christ’s children, and if Christ’s children are branches on His vine—one body with Him and one spirit—then whose knowledge is it? Is it mine or God’s? Should I not know in the Spirit of Christ what this world was created from? If He who created it dwells in me, should *He* not know it?

74. Therefore, I now submit and choose to know nothing of my own self—that is, in that part of me belonging to the outward world—so that He may know in me whatever He wills. I am not the *mother* <note>original Latin: *Genetrix*, a female parent or procreator.</note> in this knowing; rather, my spirit is *His wife* or woman, in whom He brings forth <note>original: "generateth"</note> knowledge, according to the *measure* that He chooses.

75. Just as the Eternal Wisdom is the Body of God, and He brings forth within her whatever He wills, if He brings forth knowledge now, it is not I who do it, but He in me. I am as if dead in the bringing forth of this knowledge, and He is my life. Indeed, I have neither sought it out nor learned it through study: He inclines Himself to my "me-ness" <note>original: "Minehood," the sense of individual ownership or self-will.</note>, and my "I-ness" <note>original: "Ihood," the core of the individual ego.</note> inclines itself up into Him.

76. But now I am dead to myself and understand nothing, for He is my understanding. Therefore I say, I live in God and God in me, and so I teach and write of Him, dear brothers; otherwise, I know nothing.

77. I pray you, bear with my *folly* <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 11:1, where the Apostle Paul asks his readers to tolerate his "foolishness" as he defends his ministry.</note> a little in what I tell you. I do this not for my own boasting, but for your *learning* and knowledge, so that you may know *whom* you scorn and despise when you deride me. I will not hide it from you, for I mean this sincerely.

78. I have written of the Three Principles <note>Böhme’s system of Three Principles describes the Dark World (God's wrath/fire), the Light World (God's love), and the Outward World (our physical universe).</note> which are known in me, though but weakly. I am like a student *who goes to school*; that is how it has been for me.

79. My opponent writes of *four principles*, and he also calls the *Spirit* of God a principle, according to his own meaning. Though I will not start a controversy over his meaning regarding this—he may make it *ten* principles if he likes, for Wisdom has neither limit nor foundation <note>original: "Ground" (German: *Ungrund*), referring to the fathomless nature of the Divine.</note>—he understands neither my meaning nor his own.

80. Let him tell me: *how* is the Holy Spirit a principle? Or what does he understand by a "principle"? Would he make the clear, bright Deity a principle? That Deity is eternal without foundation or beginning, dwelling in the "Nothing" <note>original: "Nothing" refers to the *Ungrund*, the absolute void or "non-being" from which God emerges into manifestation.</note> and possessing nothing but itself. I cannot *speak* of the principles in that way. Instead, I speak of the *Three Worlds* through which the incomprehensible Deity manifests or reveals itself.

81. *One* of these worlds exists by the power at work in the desire for Eternal Nature—that is, with the *spirit* of the *dark* source or quality. Through this, the Will of the still Eternity *sharpens* itself and brings itself into the fire through the *light*. Thus, the *sharpness* remains eternally only within itself, and yet, in the still Will of meekness, it receives a cause for the Kingdom of Joy. However, the Spirit does not remain *essentially* standing within that fierce, wrathful sharpness.

82. But the root is a darkness, and the *spirit* goes forth out of the *Chaos* <note>original: "Chaos" here refers to the unformed potentiality of the Divine before manifestation.</note> through the root, through the fire (the Father's property), and through the second center of love and the Kingdom of Joy, into the *light*.

83. Therefore, that *very Spirit* which is the life of everything in every substance or thing (according to its specific property) is NO principle. However, when considered according to the eternal nature of fierce wrathfulness, it is a principle.

84. In the same way, the *second* principle exists by the Divine World—that is, where the Divine power is poured forth with the radiance of Majesty, which is rightly accounted for by all THREE Persons of the Trinity.

85. But the "principle" in the fire is to be understood as the place *where the dying* occurs, and out of that dying another life exists. That is: out of the fire, a *light* emerges. Yet there is no actual dying, but rather a *consuming* quality or torment; and out of that *source-quality* or *torment*, the high, triumphing Spirit exists. It is there that God's "love-will" and "anger-will" separate themselves into two worlds—namely, into Light and Darkness. He is called "God" according to the Light and according to the poured-out virtue or power of His Wisdom.

86. But the eternal Divine *origin* is not in Eternal Nature. The "Will toward Nature" comes first, and THAT Will is the Chaos in which everything lies. The Spirit exists out of that and manifests or reveals itself through Light and Darkness. Therefore, I do not call the Spirit of God a principle, for it exists without and beyond all beginnings, yet it is manifested with the eternal beginnings revealed with God in the *Trinity*—though the *Ternary* <note>original: "Ternary" (Latin: *Ternarius*), Böhme's term for the "holy earth" or the manifested body of the Trinity.</note> is also in the Chaos, as I expressed in the book *The Six Points* <note>original: *De Sex Punctis*, one of Böhme's major treatises.</note>.

## Why the Outward World is its own Principle; its Model is Eternal.

->87.<-

Now, when I write about the *Third Principle*, I also say that God created all things *through* his *Wisdom*. However, this world was NOT *created* directly out of the Spirit that is called "God." This is because the world is described as both evil and good, and even as a "murderer's den of the devil." <note>Böhme argues that if the world were made of God's pure essence, it could not contain evil or suffering. Instead, it is a secondary manifestation.</note>

88. Furthermore, it is not generated out of the Divine Wisdom itself, but rather by or through that *Wisdom*. Wisdom is not the *matter* of this world; otherwise, I would have to call a stone "God's Wisdom"—and sin, too. Instead, it is generated out of the two eternal principles, from the substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> of both worlds—that is, out of the desires of BOTH.

89. God the Father, who is EVERYTHING, moved himself during the creation of this world—meaning, in the *forms* of *both* worlds and both natures. He created the angels (you must understand) out of the spirit of the eternal natures.

90. For if a spirit is to exist in the Kingdom of Joy, it must have the "center" within itself from which that joy originates—namely, the center of the Dark World, which is the sharp power. Without this, it would be a mere *stillness* without any *movement*. <note>In Böhme's philosophy, the "Dark World" is not "evil" in its origin; it is the necessary, energetic "friction" or "fire" that allows the "Light World" to shine and have life.</note>

91. Therefore, when Lucifer despised the Light, he remained in that part of the darkness; his will departed from the Light because he wanted to dominate through the power of *fire*. By doing this, he provoked God's anger according to the property of fire—that is, within the Principle of the fiery nature.

92. Thus I say that the outward world is a <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principle." Böhme uses this term to describe a complete, self-contained realm of existence with its own laws.</note> in that it has a *life of its own*. It is generated out of both the inward spiritual worlds—meaning, it is a revelation or manifestation of the First and Second Principles. It is a *model* or likeness of eternal nature, contained within the desire of eternal nature. It was manifested with a beginning and exists within time, and when time ends, it returns again into eternity.

<margin>John 1:5</margin>
93. This "model" (or time) has always existed within God's Wisdom. Wisdom manifested this through TWO spiritual WORLDS by the movement of the eternal Father. That which is revealed or manifested comes out of both eternal Principles—namely, the light world and the dark world. Thus, <margin>John 1:5</margin> *the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not understand it.* <note>original: "comprehendeth it not" (Latin: *non comprehenderunt*). ...I would eat of the *best grapes*; but I am like a *vine-gatherer* who *gleans* <note>Böhme likely refers to Micah 7:1, expressing a spiritual hunger or a sense of gathering what remains of the truth</note>.

# What the Hardening Is: And How the Love of God Warns the Sinner: Also how the Love of God is as Powerful for Preservation as His Anger is for Destruction.

->134.<-
->*Question.*<-

Now *Reason* <note>Böhme often uses "Reason" to represent the limited, human intellect that struggles to understand divine mysteries</note> says, "What is **THAT** now which does not will [to be saved]? Since *God* calls the *lost sinner* and wills in *Christ* to have them and regenerate <note>original: "new Generate"</note> them, is that the *Father’s* hardening?"

->*Answer.*<-

Yes indeed, it is the hardening of his *anger* and the *Devil’s will*. Understand that it is the *Dark World’s will* which hardens *man*; but it cannot do that **UNTO** *death*, except as a *dark night* <note>The "Dark World" or "First Principle" is the realm of fire and wrath that Böhme believes exists as the foundation of all things, which only becomes "evil" when it is not balanced by God's Light</note>.

135. But what does *God’s love*—namely, the *Second Principle*—do for that *man*? It often complains **IN** the *heart* when *man* desires *sin*, and says, "Do not commit it," or "Do not do it. *God’s anger* will burn in you; fear *God’s* judgment." It warns *man* of his wicked ways. Now, if he follows his *free will* and converts, then it is rightly said to the *honest* or *virtuous* person: as long as he is honest or virtuous, the *Light* must arise or spring up for him out of *darkness*, and then the *Light* begins to shine in the midst of the *darkness*.

<margin>
Colossians 2:14–15.
1 Corinthians 15:55, 57.
</margin>

He came for the sake of lost *man* because he wanted to seek and save him. Should *God’s anger* then be greater than his *love*? *Christ* has undeniably broken the hard *Death* and the fierce *anger of God* into pieces, which held us captive in the *center* of the *soul* in the bonds of the *Dark World* (that is, the *First Principle*). He *made a display in triumph over death in the soul on the cross* <note>original: "made a shew in Triumph of Death in the Soul, on the Crosse"; a reference to Colossians 2:15</note>, so that the *Scripture* in the *Spirit of Christ* says: *Death, where is your sting? Hell, where is your victory?* The snare is broken and we are delivered; thus sings the *Church of Christ*.

## II. *Apology* <note>original: "Apo:"; a defense or formal justification of his ideas</note> to Tilke. What God is. Part I.

...worlds: there he will see what God is, what His will and omnipotence are, and what is truly called "God."

142. For if His anger is all-powerful to *destroy*, then His love is also all-powerful to *preserve*. If this opposition <note>original: "Contrariety"</note> did not exist, there would be no life; there would be no good, and also no evil. For if there were no fierce wrath, there would be no motion. Thus, the essence <note>original: "Substance"</note> of all essences is a continual working, *desiring*, and *fulfilling*. The Fire desires the Light so that it may obtain a gentle nature <note>original: "Meeknesse"</note> and substance for its burning and life. And the Light desires the Fire; otherwise, there would be no light, and it would have neither power nor life. Both of them desire the dark anguish; otherwise, the fire and light would have no *root*, and everything would be nothing.

<margin>* Note this well.</margin>
143. Therefore, I say to you now: God’s love is as great as His anger, His fire is as great as His light, and His darkness is as great as either of the others. It is all *equally eternal* without a beginning. It begins itself from eternity with or by the darkness, and brings itself from eternity through the darkness into the source or quality—even into the fire. In the rising up of the fire is the *eternal death*, where the darkness and the light separate themselves, each into its own principle. The light also possesses itself. One dwells in the other *unperceived* <note>original: "unapprehended"</note> by the other; in eternity there is no parting asunder. Those who dwell in the darkness do not see the light, and those who dwell in the light see no darkness.

# I. Part. What God is. *Apology* <note>original: "Apo:"; a defense or formal justification of his ideas</note> to Tilke. II.

145. Then you say: so the **Darkness** is a cause of the Deity? # I. Apology to T. Of God’s Drawing. Part 1.

173. Now **Christ** has promised to hear; and even if I do not immediately find it in power or virtue, yet if I ask, THEN I believe that **God** has given me his **Spirit**. And though my heart and all the **World** should clearly say "No," yet I will let the **Words** of **Christ** be more certain to me than all **babbling** and **fictions**.

174. Am I indeed the dry **staff** or **Rod of Aaron**? <note>original: "Rod of Aaron" refers to Numbers 17:8, where a dry wooden staff miraculously sprouted blossoms to show God’s choice.</note> Within me lies the **drying** or withering through **Adam**; but if **Christ** has introduced his **sap** <note>original: "Sap" here means the vital life-force or spiritual grace of Christ.</note> into my withered **flesh** and into my **dark soul** again, shall I not take or receive it for myself? Shall I first wait for a special **drawing**?

175. I know that I can have no **good thought** in me unless it comes from **God**. Now, if I would gladly be saved, then I know that very **will** is **God’s drawing**. Why should I wait long for **another drawing**? If the Lord calls within me and bids me turn to him, is that not **drawing**? Indeed, what man can say he is not **SO drawn**? None at all: **God draws everyone**.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
176. * The **evil man** will not follow; he goes on in a disputable way and seeks **subterfuges** <note>original: "Subterfuges" refers to deceitful excuses used to avoid the truth.</note> or **excuses**. He says he is **holy**, yet his heart is a **thief**, and **covetous**, a **murderer**, and moreover a **proud devil**. He flatters himself only under **Christ’s purple mantle** <note>original: "Christs Purple Mantle" refers to the robe placed on Christ during his suffering; Böhme uses it here to describe hypocrites who "hide" their sins behind the name of Christ’s sacrifice without actually changing their behavior.</note> and tickles himself with **Christ’s suffering** and **death**, but will not enter into it. He will not die to **sin** with **Christ** and become an **enemy** to it; he only wants to walk upon roses in luxury and **foolish days**, and devour the sweat of the **miserable** in **pride**—for, says he, "**God does not draw me**." Yes, you **will not**: therefore he hardens you, and his **anger** draws you, as does the **devil** whom you **serve**.

177. Should **God** draw you? Then cast your false or wicked ways from you; set yourself as if you were to meet an **enemy** where **body** and **life** are at stake. If the **anger** draws you and holds you, simply **defend** yourself, and you will soon find **One** who will help you.

<margin>* Viz: Of God’s Anger.</margin>
178. Does the **anger** in your **conscience say**, "You are mine; you cannot be saved"? Then say in opposition: "I take only **CHRIST’S death** with me; do with me what you will." Take that death and wrap yourself in it. Let God’s anger and all devils roar over you and say and complain against you whatever they will; out of these **swaddling clothes** <note>original: "Swaddling clothes" refers to Christ's humility and incarnation; here, it is a metaphor for being wrapped in Christ's protection.</note> no **election** shall pluck YOU, whether it be of **God**, or the **devil**, or **man**.

179. But the wanton, **licentious** way which men now walk—where men only **tickle** and comfort the **old evil wicked one**, the **murderer**, the **proud, stately, covetous Babylonish Antichrist** <note>original: "Babylonish Antichrist" is Böhme’s term for the corrupt and worldly church systems of his time.</note> with **Christ’s sufferings** and **death**—claims that he should only be quiet and fatten himself well because **Christ** has satisfied the debt. They think if someone is marked or noted under **Christ’s blood banner** and **elected**, then he cannot be damned. This way is totally false or wicked, **murderous**, and **unrighteous**.

180. If you will be a **Christian**, then you must be and become conformable to **Christ’s image**, and walk in his **footsteps**. With him, you must suffer persecution, disgrace, and scorn; love the way of **truth** and **righteousness**; and do that which **Christ** has taught you—not with hypocrisy.

# I. Part. And who are hardened by God. Apology to Tilcke. II.

180. ...sacrifice, to take double or four-fold, and give a little piece of it to another; No, it must be earnest; you should not value anything you have as if it were your own alone. Instead, consider that you are only a *servant* in those matters, and serve your Lord in Heaven; therefore, you should dispose of your possessions according to HIS pleasure.

181. Do not exploit the miserable and then give a small portion to a beggar, saying, "I am indeed serving the poor." First, let them keep the fruit of their own labor <note>original: "leave them their Sweat"; meaning do not steal their wages or overwork them for your own profit.</note>; otherwise, you will be cursed in all your service to God and be held back from Him.

<margin>* John 20:25. † John 5:17. * John 15:5.</margin>
182. Serve Him with mind and heart; walk in the Light. Let the scorn of the world be like *the marks of Christ’s wounds* to you. Work, watch, and pray, and always remain careful and cautious against the Devil. Arm and fortify yourself continually against him, and consider that you are a pilgrim here and in the vineyard of Christ. Labor faithfully in the Kingdom of God, for all your labor follows after you; for Christ said, † *My Father works and I work also*; so must you also, as *a branch on the vine, work and bear fruit*.

<margin>† Romans 11:22. * Romans 9:18. † Note Note.</margin>
183. For a Christian is a branch on the tree of JESUS CHRIST; if it will not work and bear fruit, then it † *shall be cut off, so that it does not hinder other branches*. That is, it must completely wither and be hardened against the *Life of Christ*. These are the ones God will harden. Here it is said: *I harden whom I will*; namely, a branch that *will not bring forth fruit*. To such a person, God will not give the spiritual life-force <note>original: "Sap"</note> of Christ. It is not said, † "God will not be mine," but rather that you will not be His, and so you are parted.

<margin>* Note Note.</margin>
184. * Do you say, "God can make of me what He will, for He is all-powerful"? He makes of you what you yourself will; His Love is all-powerful, and so is His Anger. Whichever one captures you, holds you. The *wicked* is to God a foul odor <note>original: "good favour," likely a mistranslation or archaic use of "savor," referring to 2 Corinthians 2:15-16 where the same "aroma" leads some to death and others to life.</note> leading to death, and the saint or holy person is a fragrance leading to eternal holy life. As you grow, so you are; you bear the fruit of whatever spiritual life-force you draw into yourself.

185. Why do you blame God? God, in so far as He is called "God," CANNOT will evil; for He is good, and there is no evil will in Him. But according to His Anger, He desires wood or fuel for His fire—whatever is suitable for or fits the fire.

<margin>† Romans 6:16.</margin>
186. Therefore, the Apostle rightly says: † *To whom you give yourselves as servants in obedience, his servants you are—whether of God’s Love or His Anger*. Here the Apostle speaks of human choice <term>Election</term>, showing that a person CAN surrender himself and be surrendered. And although he cannot take or receive grace by his own power alone, God gives him the ability to take or receive it, for He has promised it to him.

->187.<-

The doctrine of my opponent is consistently nothing other than this: *If God makes a good tree, then it is so*; that is, if He makes someone a *Christian*, then they are one—as if a person needs to do nothing in the matter, and does not need to work or labor to become a *good tree*.

188. Alas! May God pity us. Why has God given us the *LAW* and its teachings, and said, "You shall not do this or that," if He actually desires evil? How very shamefully this man goes astray! <margin>* Psalm 95:7-8. Hebrews 3:7-8 and 4:7.</margin>

He should instead tell them that they must *repent*, as God says through the prophets: *Today, when you hear the voice of the Lord, do not harden your hearts* <note>original: "Today when you heare the voyce of the Lord, Harden not your hearts"</note>. Let my word enter into your hearts and ears.

190. But he says that it cannot enter; God makes either a *good* or an *evil* tree. This reasoning serves only to encourage all kinds of careless negligence and wickedness, and leads ultimately to *despair*. That is the end result of his *doctrine*; you will find nothing better or more in his views on *election by grace* or *predestination* <note>term: Grace-Election; the theological concept that God chooses who will be saved based solely on His own will, rather than human merit.</note>.

191. And I say with firm standing—and it is the precious truth—that if such a doctrine were to be embraced or accepted, the world would eventually become a murderous den of devils. Everyone would say: *How can I do otherwise than God drives me? If God wants me to be His child, He will teach and lead me well enough. But if I am not elected, why should I bother showing favor to the honest and virtuous? I will do as the devil does and hate them, and be their enemy; I belong to his kingdom. I will steal, rob, murder, cheat, and deceive the simple so that I may be powerful and self-indulgent. Nothing else will come of it, since God will not draw me to Him; therefore, I...*

Whichever one the soul works within is what manifests itself in the soul.

One part of this seed comes from *Divine* substantiality—from the holy and pure element in which Paradise and Heaven exist, as well as the *tincture* <term>tincture: in Böhme’s terminology, a spiritual essence or transformative power that links spirit and matter</term> of fire and light. That specific seed disappeared in *Adam* when he fell, of which God said, "*In the day that you eat of this tree, you shall die*" <note>Genesis 2:17</note>.

222. The other seed—meaning the spirit—is the *center* of Eternal Nature (that is, of the dark world), which is why God calls Himself an "angry God." 223. Now, *Adam* was also enclosed within the dominion and the spirit of the outward world. ## Of the Becoming Man or Incarnation and Person of Christ.

### *How Christ has become Man or Incarnate, not out of any foreign seed, but out of Mary; and yet indeed not in Eve's earthly essence—the Holy Spirit was the Man or Masculine principle within her.*

->230.<-

<margin>* Or Aurora <note>Jacob Böhme’s first book was titled *Aurora*, meaning "the dawning of the day."</note>.</margin>
My opponent, tell me here: what is the woman’s seed upon which you base your doctrine of election? # Part II. *How Christ is Incarnated of* Mary. Apology to Tilke. III

234. Now, if *Mary, Christ’s Mother*, is not descended from us human beings, then Christ is not the *Son of Man*—as he so very often calls himself. And if that were true, where then would my poor soul remain, which lies captive in a dark dungeon? If God wanted to regenerate the soul simply as the dew comes out of the morning's red glow, he could have easily done so without becoming man.

235. Besides, if *Mary* were not a human being from our own race, what profit would this *foreign* <note>original: "strange"</note> CHRIST be to me? Then it would *not* be true that the Word became flesh. *Or how could I participate in Christ’s suffering, dying, and death, if it were not done in my own nature?*

<margin>* Galatians 2:20.</margin>
236. But I can say with truth, as the Apostle says, that I believe *I am crucified and dead with Christ, and I rise up in and with him, and bear his image upon me.*

237. My opponent argues that Christ would have been conceived in a sinful seed if *Eve* had been the "woman" mentioned in the Promise. No, I do not say that.

<margin>* Note: the dry Rod of Aaron <note>A reference to Numbers 17, where Aaron’s wooden staff miraculously sprouted blossoms, symbolizing life coming from something dead or dormant.</note> did not grow through the four elements of water and fire.</margin>
238. Christ—namely, the Living Word—was not generated from *human* seed. Instead, he was generated in the closed-up seed of the "heavenly part," which had *faded* or disappeared in *Eve*. This is what the *dry or withered Rod of Aaron* signifies. He became the sap and life of the dead parts once again. For the sin did not fall upon the heavenly part; rather, that part died—meaning its substance became dormant. This does not apply to God's Spirit, which rested in the Covenant until it reached the limit of that Covenant in *Mary*.

239. The anger of God manifested or revealed itself as a "life" in the earthly part of humanity. Meanwhile, the heavenly part disappeared or faded, just as God said: *The day you eat of it, you shall die.*

<margin>† Genesis 5:5.</margin>
240. He did not mean only physical death, for *Adam* lived † *nine hundred and thirty years* before he died. When God said, "The day you eat you shall die," he meant dying to the Kingdom of Heaven and living to the earthly world, which is exactly what happened.

241. I am not saying that God became man in *Eve’s* earthly essence (if he had, he would have needed a human father). Rather, *he* himself is the Father.

<margin>* Luke 1:35.</margin>
<margin>† The eternal love-fire and the water of the single Element.</margin>
242. Understand this correctly: * *The Angel said to Mary, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you."* Therein lies the point <note>original: "sticketh the Mark"</note> or the key. The Angel said he will come *upon* you, and the power of the Most High will *overshadow* you. Do you not understand this? I lament his misery more—that he is so blind in this matter—than I desire to answer him.

313. I exhort you all who read and hear this: do not harden <note>original: "stop"</note> your hearts. Look upon the time and consider it; see the era in which we and our ancestors have lived: namely, in vain contention and strife. Has the world—that is, Man—become more honest or better because of this strife? Not at all; it has only become more hellish, wicked, indulgent <note>original: "voluptuous"</note>, insulting, and more scornful.

314. Through the manifestation of the Gospel, man has actually become worse in his way of life. All the while they have argued, one brother has condemned <note>original: "contemned"</note> another, and persecuted and hated him. What kind of fruit of the *Gospel* do you show at present, as there should be?

315. Must the dear and precious Name of God now be the cover for man’s wickedness? Are not the current so-called Christians, as well as Turks <note>original: "Turks"; a historical term used here to refer to Muslims</note>, Jews, and heathens, all alike to one another in their way of life? What does the Name of Christ benefit you if you live only like a heathen? Do you suppose it is enough that you know that Christ died for sin? Do you think you only need to flatter and comfort yourselves with Christ's death while retaining the false or wicked man within, who is only proud, arrogant <note>original: "stately"</note>, and argumentative?

316. Can you not perceive what will suddenly follow from this? Since they are all alike in their life and will, they shall be judged alike before God. And so, if men seek nothing but strife and mere contention, it must lead to such a mixed confusion in the conflict that one people will devour the other.

317. For God withdraws his hand from people when they will not allow his Spirit to correct <note>original: "reprove"</note> them. Therefore, Wrath has taken up its sword and desire, and drives mightily in the minds of men, so that one people destroys and devours the other. What our fathers sowed <note>original: "layd in"</note> with reproach and scorn, their children will eat up with *sword* and *slaughter*.

318. And God allows that to happen because men only use his holy Name for cursing and swearing, and so misuse it. In the knowledge of his Name and Will, they are only self-willed; they use his Name only for an insult, so that one brother despises another only for the sake of his understanding of God's Name—even though he should seek God through knowledge in love and lead by example with a holy life.

320. Everyone says: "It will be good when this evil is past and gone."
