### III. Apol. How Angels and the Soul were Created. Text. I.

50. All angels and creatures created for eternal life are all *comprised* <margin>* Grasped or contracted.</margin> in the out-breathing of the Father through the Word. This occurs in the *Desire* as it moves in the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat," Latin for "let it be done," referring to God's creative command</note>, and in a *model* of the eternal longing delight. Just as the Eternal Spirit in Wisdom has understood it in its *wonders*, they are created into an image of that longing delight. In all things, there remains the *possibility* for good and evil, according to the complete divine nature—both light and darkness.

51. Yet we must not think that a spirit or angel is itself the out-breathing of the eternal *birth* <note>original: "Geniture"</note> of the Holy *Trinity* in the divine *voice*. Rather, it is the out-spoken Word—a *model* and image of the speaking Word, and a tuned *instrument* of the Spirit of God. Through this instrument, the Spirit of God plays, creates melodies, and sounds.

52. As long as the *instrument* remains in its *proper order*, aligned with the *desire* of the *Fiat*; which exists in all *angels* as their own property. With this, an angel’s will may lift itself into the good—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, into God’s love—or into his anger, and immerse itself into that *form* and *tone* <note>original: "tang"</note>. Then the sound of the Word from the Father’s love and anger is out-breathed and becomes an image in the *Word of creation* <note>original: "verbo Fiat"</note>.

53. This is seen in how some *Prince-Angels* give themselves over with *desire* to love, while others, like *Lucifer*, turn toward *anger*—that is, into the desire of the *Fiat*. They created or pulled out a will within the desire for anger, in the *power of fire*, wishing to live and rule according to the Father’s *property of anger*. In this way, they sought to dominate all angelic principalities and overrule love with the fierce, wrathful *power of fire*. Because of this, he was thrust out by the *Word of creation* <note>original: "Word Fiat"</note> into the *darkness* of God’s anger.

54. Thus, we cannot say regarding the creation of all things or substances that the eternal *substance* of the *Trinity* <note>original: "Ternary"</note> has formed itself into the image of an angel. Rather, they formed in the eternal *desire* that originated in the longing delight of the *Godhead*; through the movement of the Father of all things or substances, acting as an ETERNAL *nature* and a revelation or manifestation of the eternal *hidden nature*.

55. In that eternal, beginningless nature—namely, in the *all-being, all-substantial* working of the Great *Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum," a central concept in Boehme's work regarding the source of all things</note>—angels and human souls received their origin. This occurred in the eternal *out-spoken Word*, in the eternal *wisdom* of God, according to both love and anger.

56. For if they had originated only in the *holy voice* of God—that is, in *love* alone—then they could not have developed or framed within themselves any will toward anger. If the *love-will* of God within the angels had fallen, it would mean that God himself had fallen within the creature and become a *devil*, which would be an abominable thing to say.

# I. Text. How the Angels and Soul were Created. Apol. III.

57. No creaturely spirit <note>original: "Creaturely Spirit," referring to the spirit of a created being like an angel or human</note> can exist as a created being without the fire-world. Even the Love of God would not exist if his anger—or the *fire-world*—were not within him. The anger or the fire of God is the cause of light, power, strength, and omnipotence.

58. But within Love, the fire dies and transforms itself into the kingdom of *joy*. Death is the point of origin; it is like a dying within the fire. Out of this dying, the light originates as a different source or quality: namely, a *desire* for *love*. This is called God’s mercy, or the divine kingdom of joy. The life of *holiness*, which is free from pain or suffering, proceeds from this dying in the fire, shining forth like a glimpse of majesty or a glimpse of *liberty*.

59. Lucifer despised this "dying." He wanted to live and dominate in the fire's own rule, within his own *self-hood* <note>original: "Self-hood," the ego or independent self-will</note>. Consequently, he was driven out of the fire and back into the *root* of the fire—which is darkness.

60. Every angel and soul that wishes to live in God’s light and power must die to the "self-hood" of the fire’s dominance. They must do this within their *desire* and completely immerse or cast themselves—and their own sense of property—into God’s will, which is the divine sound. They must die to their own self-will in the fire but bud or sprout forth in the light of love. Through this resignation <term>original: "Resignation," the act of surrendering one's will to God</term>, they enter into God’s sound or *Word* as a fruit of God’s love, so that God’s will-spirit may rule and guide their life.

61. Thus, the holy *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture," a spiritual essence or quality that transforms or "colors" reality</note> of the fire and light may become the shine of their life's radiance. From this, a divine will and desire originate once again, allowing that life to live in the power and virtue of the *wisdom* of God. In that wisdom, the soul can behold itself and form or attract a divine will.

62. This *wisdom* is the food of the angels. From it, they generate eternal *praise* for their Creator. Thus, God’s joyful play or melody, expressed through the angelic voice, becomes an *instrument* of the Spirit of God, all directed into the harmony of the *divine* kingdom of joy.

63. For every *Prince-Angel* bears the name of the Great God, each according to his own specific property, serving as a unique *instrument* tuned for the praise of God in the divine sound.

They did not come out of the sound of the *divine* property itself, but through the word *fiat* <note>original: "fiat," Latin for "let it be done"</note>—that is, through the *impression* <note>original: "Impression," the process of spiritual energy condensing into substance</note> of the eternal mystery. This came from the desire of the eternal fire and light and entered into a *substance* according to the properties of fire and darkness, as well as according to the desire of the light (the property of free, longing delight). # I. Text. On Man's Origin. Apologia III.

<margin>* Ephesians 1:3–4.</margin>
<margin>74.</margin>
74. Saint Paul says: * "Man was foreseen or chosen <note>original: "elected"</note> in Christ before the foundation of the world was laid." In this lies the kernel <note>original: "Kernell," the core essence or truth</note>: before the ages of this world began, the model of Man was known in the Eternal Wisdom. It was an out-breathing of the Word, emerging from the Fire and Light as a form within Divine Wisdom. However, it did not yet exist as a physical creature or image, but rather in a magical way, like an image that appears to someone in a dream, which exists without physical substance.

75. This is the appearance within the universal, out-breathed "expressed substance" <note>original: "out-spoken-substance"</note> in the Spirit of God. This Spirit has known all things according to the specific quality of each—namely, according to the anger of the Fire's quality in the Darkness, and according to the Light in the Love.

76. For the flash of Creation, coming out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum," the hidden source of all things</note>, was seen within Wisdom in both Evil and Good, according to the nature of both desires, as an eternal contradiction.

<margin>† The Image.</margin>
77. The Anger—that is, the Dark-world—has seen the image or likeness of God within its own desire. Likewise, the Love has seen it within its own free, longing, and delightful desire. 78. Through this, the Spirit of God—which eternally proceeds from the Father’s Fire and Light—knew of the Fall within the Anger of God. He knew that when this image of the form of God was created into a living substance, it would also be drawn toward the fierce wrath and lose its glory.

79. Here, in this place, the Christ, in the Name of Jesus, acted as a "will" toward the Christ. He set himself toward this likeness of God and gave his Will—out of the name of Jesus—into the created humanity, in order to be a Christ or Savior.

Now, understand me correctly: just as God shines through everything in the Holy Light-world and infuses <note>original: "tinctureth," to dye or permeate with a quality</note> all things, transforming them from a fiery state into the power of joy, he also presses through the outward world with that same power, giving all things life and power.

This is its own *fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done," the divine command of creation</note> or self-generation, like an impression made according to the nature of the eternal spiritual mystery, serving as a manifestation or revelation of it.

### III. A: How man was elected before the foundation of the World. T. I.

Within the glimpse of the knowledge or the *representation* of the Spirit, which is like a *Looking-Glass* <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"; Böhme uses this term to describe Divine Wisdom as a mirror in which God sees the possibilities of creation</note>, man was created into an Image out of the heavenly and earthly elementary substance. He was made from the breathed-out substance of eternity and the substance of time, existing one within the other, just as eternity exists within time; neither is the other, yet they are not separated, except as distinct principles <note>referring to the different levels of reality: the dark world, the light world, and the physical world</note>.

93. The substance of eternity is the pure **Element** in which vegetative or growing life is a *Paradise*. By contrast, the substance of time consists of the four elements in which the constellations create a bubbling <margin>NOTE.</margin> life—specifically, an earthly and *mortal Paradise*.

94. For this earthly bubbling <note>original: "seething"; the active, boiling energy of life</note> has its origin in the Mystery, where the properties of fire and light divide into *two* principles, each existing within itself. Therefore, it is both evil and good, breathed out from God’s love and anger.

95. God moved that breathed-out property at the beginning of time and introduced it into a *Desire*. This desire generated earth and stones through the "impression" <note>the process of spirit densifying into matter</note>, according to the properties of the Dark, Fire, and Light worlds. *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt* <note>the three fundamental alchemical qualities: Sulphur (the soul/fire), Mercury (the spirit/movement), and Salt (the body/substance)</note> were the properties of that desire; in that regard, those very properties are the life of all elementary substances or things.

96. Understand us correctly: in these properties, we find the *Oil* <note>a spiritual substance representing light and joy that balances the fire</note> in all things, which is the likeness of the heavenly light's property derived from the Good. Out of this substance, the outward body (from the *third* principle) was formed by the word "*Let it be*" <note>original: "Fiat"</note>. In the *second* principle (the angelic world), the pure element was formed within the **paradisiacal *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt* of power.**

97. That was the body which God created in his image and likeness—meaning the human image which God has seen from eternity in his breathed-out glimpse of Wisdom within the Looking-Glass.

98. In that Looking-Glass, he impressed substance from the two principles through the word "*Let it be*" <note>original: "Fiat"</note> and created it into an image. He then introduced or breathed in the breathed-out sound or voice of his Word from all three principles to be a soul and spirit—to be a life, understanding, and governance <note>original: "Regiment"</note> originating from the sound of his mouth. This was a spirit of fire, light, and air, drawn from both eternity and time; that was the image of God.

# Concerning His Rule or Dominion.

99. As Light is the rule or dominion in every form of life, and that very light of life burns and shines out of the oil of the Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt <note>original: "Sulphur Mercury and Sal"; these are Böhme's three fundamental spiritual-chemical principles representing the soul’s fire (Sulphur), the spirit’s motion (Mercury), and the body’s substance (Salt)</note> of power—as no understanding person can deny—so it was in the inward man. This inward man was created out of the Second Principle—that is, out of the pure Element—where the pure Paradisiacal Sulphur and Mercury burned. In that pure fire-burning or life, which was totally without blemish, God’s true light shone.

100. For the name JESUS had incorporated itself into the image of eternity as a future CHRIST, who would become a Savior to man. Out of the dying of the "Anger" <note>the harsh, dark, or "wrathful" property of nature</note>, He would generate man anew in the pure Sulphur of divine and Paradisiacal power.

101. Understand this correctly: The pure Element in the **Holy Sulphur** permeated the outward man and took the four elements into its power. Heat and cold were not manifested in the flesh; they did exist within the Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt of the body, but while God’s light shone within them, they were in equal harmony, so that neither could be felt or manifested above the other.

102. For all the desires in the "Mercury"—that is, in the cold and hot fire-wheel <note>the energetic, rotating movement of the spirit</note>—stood in the light and were wholly enlightened through and through. Their desire was a paradise of joyfulness or the Kingdom of Joy; no enmity of nature was manifested in them.

<margin>* Colossians 1:15, 17.</margin>
103. Just as God the Father is called a fierce, wrathful, zealous, or jealous God and a consuming fire—and indeed He is so in these properties—yet in His light and love-desire (that is, in His firstborn from eternity, which is His beloved Heart), none of these harsh properties become manifested or revealed.

104. According to this "Heart," He calls Himself GOD, for in this He is the GOOD. But according to the fire, He calls Himself "Anger." And according to the desire for the fire-life—which is the revelation or manifestation of the generative process, where the free longing delight introduces itself out of the "Nothing" into "Something" (that is, into an *impression* of the desire)—He creates Nature and the dark world. Out of these properties, Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt exist.

105. The reader is referred to that book for a better understanding, and I will leave the matter briefly for now.

# Concerning the Fall of Man.

->106.<-

The will-spirit of the Soul, arising out of the *property of fire* <note>In Böhme’s thought, "fire" represents the foundational, energetic, and sometimes harsh core of existence</note>, lifted itself up into *earthly* desire. In this state, both evil and good were hidden within the center of the soul, beneath the paradisiacal source or quality. They existed in *equal accord* <note>meaning: in perfect balance or harmony</note>, but the soul introduced itself into a desire for both evil and good in order to make them manifest within itself.

107. Furthermore, the *Devil* gave the soul a reason to do so. He introduced his own desire or "imagination" into the soul's "evil" part—specifically into the fierce, wrathful, and fiery *Mercury* <term>Mercury: In this context, an alchemical term for the active life-force or the "word" of nature that causes movement and change</term> in its own property, where the "poison" and "anger-life" reside. Consequently, this poisonous life began to hunger for things that matched its own nature.

<margin>† Genesis 2:17</margin>
108. Then came the commandment of God, which said to the Soul: † *“Do not eat of the tree of the growth of the knowledge of good and evil; otherwise you will die”* to the holy divine life, within the pure *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur: In alchemical terms, this refers to the substance or "oil" that fuels the light of life</term> and the *Element* <note>original: "Element of the Substance"</note> of the soul’s being. *“On the day that you eat of it, you will die the death.”*

109. For within the poisonous *Mercury*—according to the property of the Father’s anger—was the *dying life*. This state had not been manifested or revealed before; however, through the *Devil’s* imagination, it was stirred up and introduced into the *desire* for things like itself.

110. Thus, understand that we have truly and deeply perceived that the "Tree of Temptation" grew through this power—the hunger to apprehend and know both evil and good. Yet, one canNOT say that it was a DIFFERENT tree or vegetable from the rest; it was only that the *earthly* source or quality of evil and good was manifested and revealed within it.

111. In the other trees and plants, the *holy paradisiacal Mercury* pressed through everything, and all properties were in equal balance. The "evil" of heat and cold was not revealed in them. But in this specific tree, the properties of heat and cold within the poisonous earthly *Mercury* were made manifest.

112. The hunger of the soul caused this. For the soul was a *spark* out of the great omnipotence of God; regarding this, *Christ* said to us:
<margin>* Matthew 21:21</margin>
\* *“If one were born or generated of God again in faith, they might say to the mountain, 'Lift yourself up and cast yourself into the sea,' and it would be done.”*

113. How, then, would the soul—standing in the strong might of God—not be able to bring forth these properties within the tree?

114. To this end, the Devil, acting through the serpent’s nature, positioned himself and
<margin>† Genesis 3:5, 6</margin>
persuaded Eve that † *she would be wise if she ate of both evil and good*.

### III. Apology. We should say we are unprofitable servants. Text 1.

116. And by the Fall, we are to understand nothing else but that the *earthly* property—which before was, as it were, swallowed up in *Paradise*—manifested itself in the soul's desire. 117. There, the paradisiacal *sulphur* <term>sulphur: In alchemical terms, this refers to the "oil" or substance that allows the light of life to burn</term> in the holy element lost its life, and the divine *substance* disappeared.

It wanted to be its own master, to know good and evil and to *live* in both. It died to God and awakened to the earthly world, living according to the will of the Devil—namely, to the stern anger of God—in nothing but anxiety, lamentation, misery, toil, and necessity, as we poor children of *Eve* now see and feel within us.

### I. Text. *We should say we are unprofitable Servants.* Apology III.

<margin>* Or in imitation of His likeness.</margin>
...to himself, an *Image* <margin>*</margin> according to his *Likeness*, for a *Sport of Joy*; as a Master of Music does an instrument, which nevertheless makes such a melody as the *Master* wills: but He does not make such another Master as Himself, but only makes [the image] of or out of Himself.

124. Therefore, seeing God is a *Spirit* and *not a substance*, nor even Nature; therefore Man is not God, but his life is founded upon and comes out of God's life; yet understand, it comes out of the THREE Principles. <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Three Principles" are the dark fire-world (the Father's power), the light world (the Son's love), and the physical world (the Holy Spirit's manifestation).</note>

125. This does not mean that the life is God himself; *otherwise*, if it should fall and become a Devil—as *Lucifer* did—then God would have become a Devil.

<margin>* 2 Samuel 22:26–27; Psalm 17:25–26.</margin>
126. Human life is the out-spoken Word, in which the speaking Word *lives*, in either Evil or Good, depending on how the Out-spoken Word draws a quality out of God's Harmony or Concord into itself; <margin>*</margin> *as a people are, such a God they also have within them;* and yet there is but ONE God; however, he manifests himself in ALL and every life according to the life's desire, whether in good or evil.

127. *First:* Therefore, the *strife* or *controversy* between me and that *Author* <note>Böhme is likely referring to a contemporary critic like Balthasar Tilke, who accused him of confusing the creature with the Creator.</note> is this: he mixes or *confounds* everything together and provides no correct or direct understanding. He presents himself so elegantly as a *creature* within the holy Trinity, as the *firstborn* or *begotten* before all creatures. Therefore, he concludes the Creation is within *CHRIST*, but he errs; he should conclude it is in JESUS or JEHOVAH—in the Eternal Word of the Father, as *Saint John* does in the *First Chapter.*

128. He should not create for me a *Woman* out of the *Birth-giver* <note>original: "Genetrix," referring to the divine matrix or source of generation</note> of God, in whom Christ is born or generated from eternity; instead, he should say, according to the Scripture, that the Father generates the Word, and that the Word is the *Voice* of God and the Second Person in the *Deity*; and that the Holy Spirit goes out from the Father and the Son.

129. It is not *supposition* or an *opinion* that will suffice—nor setting oneself up as a *Fair Bride* <note>A metaphor for spiritual pride or the soul claiming a premature union with God.</note> while still stuck full of sins and evil inclinations. Instead, one must humble oneself before God and be submissive to him. One must not say, "*Here is the Lord, namely:* the Voice of the holy Trinity sounding out of God's Heart." No, we will not grant that to this *Author*. He should remain in the Harmony and hear what kind of note the Lord brings forth in the creatures through the resonance <term>tang: a sharp, ringing sound or resonance</term> of that Harmony, as the Lord sounds.

130. And even if it had been at its *best*—where perhaps a glimpse of the Holy Spirit had allowed itself to be heard in the harmony of his *tone*—he should still say: Lord, <margin>* Luke 17:10.</margin> <margin>*</margin> *I am an unprofitable servant:* You do what you will.

### III. Apol. Distinguishing the Human Will from God's Will. Text. I.

131. Do not say, "I will, and shall, speak to you out of God’s Heart, out of the *Voice* of the Holy Trinity." No *Angel* or *Prophet* has ever done that; instead, they have all only said that the LORD *had laid his Word* in them, to make known to them the *Word of the Lord*. For the Prophet says only, "*Thus says the LORD*"; he considers himself only an instrument, commanded to speak what he is told.

132. He does not say, "I am the Woman, the Bride of the Voice of God; I will *speak in and out of God’s Heart*." [He does not say] "My sound is God’s Voice," but rather he *bears God’s sound* within his own human voice. The *Spirit of God* sounds in the human voice only when and how He wills. A person should not *assume* this as their own property, but should stand before Him in fear and trembling, lending their human voice as an instrument. One should not say, "I have understood *beforehand* what the Spirit of God will speak," unless they have an *express* command by word of mouth.

133. The name JESUS—which in humanity has also become CHRIST—stands *within* the Holy Trinity. It stands in its own principle in the birth or generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note> of the Holy Trinity, and *not* in the power or authority of the creature.

<margin>
† John 5:31, 37.
* John 16:27, 28.
</margin>
134. Yet *Christ* says, *† "If I testify concerning myself, my witness is nothing; but it is my Father in me who testifies concerning me* that I have come forth from God: I have proceeded forth from God and come into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father."*

<margin>
† John 14:10.
</margin>

136. People should always distinguish the humanity from the Deity, and the human will from God's will. For no man can reach God's mind, sense, thoughts, or will through *selfhood* <note>Böhme uses "selfhood" to describe the ego or the independent, fallen human will that tries to operate apart from God.</note>. Man sees after or behind the Spirit of God; even *Moses *could not see God’s face* or countenance; he had to see from behind, or *† behind Him. When he did see Him, he saw only the Lord’s track or footsteps.* How then will this man <note>Böhme is likely critiquing a specific opponent here.</note> speak in, with, and through God? Even if the Lord does speak through him, he does not know it until he *sees and knows* His footsteps.

137. It is therefore a vain enterprise or rashness, which is not sufficiently grounded. It is only *intricate* confusion. He wishes not to be Nature, and yet in man there can be *no* divine knowledge without Nature.

138. *Nature is God’s Revelation* or manifestation. The human spirit is—or comes from—the Eternal Nature (meaning the Soul); and the outward spirit is—or comes from—the outward nature. Yet they are not two spirits, but they exist within one another in *Three Degrees*, according to the nature of the *Three Principles*. <note>In Böhme’s system, the "Three Principles" represent the dark fire-world (the Father), the light world (the Son), and the physical world (the Holy Spirit's manifestation).</note>

167. The soul departed from JESUS into its own self-will, but God took mercy and compassion on it. He promised to move Himself in Man once more through the Name JESUS, and to generate the CHRIST within Man out of both God's and Man’s substance.

168. This was NOT out of the sinful flesh of the outward world, but out of the Divine Flesh. In *Adam*, when he entered the outward earthly realm, this divine flesh disappeared and died, so that only the outward flesh remained attached to him.

# I. Text. The Husk of Sin only dies. Apol. III.

<margin>
† **NOTE**
What Dies
in Man.
</margin>
170. Just as a grain of *seed* is sown into the earth, out of which a beautiful *stalk* grows with many fruits—where the *essence* of the *grain* produces that *stalk* and only the † *shell* or *husk* dies—so also in man, only the husk of *sin* dies. The human essence in the Name *JESUS*, within the *CHRIST* who became manifest in man, becomes that very *CHRIST*. This is not the *trunk* or the *stock*, but a little *twig* or *branch* out of that very same *stock*.

171. Therefore, this man <note>Referring to the opponent, Esaias Stiefel.</note> cannot persuade us unless he demonstrates to us that *CHRIST*, the *Express Image of God*, was generated from *eternity* out of the *stock* of the love of his *Mother* <note>likely referring to the Divine Sophia or the "eternal nature" out of which the form of man is derived</note>, and was an *Express Image of God*.

172. But in this way, He was the *Express Image of God* from *eternity*: namely, in the *Figure of Man*. In this figure, God created man with a beginning and as a *creature*; there, the *image* of the *likeness* became known in God. This occurred in the *Name JESUS*, which in this *looking-glass* <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"; in Boehme’s thought, this is the mirror of Divine Wisdom through which God envisions creation</note> of the *Express Image*, through the power of *JESUS*, would become a *CHRIST*.

173. *The Life of Christ* began with the *second moving*, when God moved Himself according to His *Heart* within *human nature* <note>original: "Humane Property"</note>. This happened in the *eternal, seen likeness of God*, in the *JESUS*, and he received the Name of *CHRIST* as a *Savior* or *healer of the wound* <note>original: "Sore"</note>—and not from *eternity*.

174. For the likeness of God, which was *seen* in God’s wisdom from eternity and known in *JEHOVAH* (in which God created man), existed before the times of the world *without life and substance*. It was only a *looking-glass* of the *image*, in which God saw Himself and how He *might be* within an image.

# III. Apology. We are generated in Christ. Text. I.

...mediator between God and Man, for God has set him up to be a Throne of Grace. But he who is set up is not the Throne itself; instead, he brings his gift—namely, the prize or spoil which he had won in the battle against God's anger—to the *Throne*.

179. There, I say, Man was not created in Christ at first, as this <margin>* E. S. <note>Esaias Stiefel, the spiritualist teacher Boehme is writing against.</note></margin> author would have it; rather, he has become generated in Christ a second time. The Name *Christ* was within the Name *JESUS*, in which Man was created, and whose origin was from eternity.

180. They are indeed one, but the author brings forth strange ideas about this. One cannot accept his claim that he should *fold up* all creatures into the Name of *CHRIST*, nor his desire for the redemption of ALL creatures in the Name of *Christ*.

181. It looks very strange, and yet one can clearly see what he means by it: namely, that HE would be the very same and only *Christ* whom men are to *hear* as the Word of God. Yet at his best, he is *scarcely a little twig* or branch on that tree—not the *Mother* herself, who has generated and will generate. I do not put my trust in him, but in the *First Christ*, who became a *CHRIST* in *JESUS*, and whose twig or branch I *desire* to be.

182. *CHRIST* was hidden in *JESUS*, and all the powers of wisdom—which no *angel's tongue* can express—lay within the hidden Christ. This revealed itself for the first time when *JEHOVAH* (who is *JESUS*) moved within humanity. There, *CHRIST* was *first* manifested. In the *first Adam*, *JEHOVAH* was manifested; and in the *second Adam*, *CHRIST* was manifested: namely, <margin>† Colossians 2:3.</margin>† *the treasure of the wisdom of God*.

183. The *first Adam* was created *perfect* in *JEHOVAH* and for eternal life—specifically, in the *eternal natural* state. However, because the eternal natural state would not endure, *JEHOVAH* then manifested *Christ* within the natural life so that *Christ* might generate and bring the natural state back into *perfection*. Thus, through his birth or generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note>, Christ has opened the treasures of wisdom that were in *JEHOVAH*.

184. Yet *CHRIST* was *hidden* in the treasure of wisdom. That wisdom was manifest in *JEHOVAH* within the *first Adam*, but not in the way that life breaks *anger into pieces*. This was not necessary if *Adam* had remained standing; but when he fell, it became necessary for this *form* to be made manifest.

185. Even this form is called *CHRIST* and dwells in *JEHOVAH*, *for* it has become manifest out of *JEHOVAH*. Therefore, since *JEHOVAH* was manifest in *Adam*, God was also manifest in him. Otherwise, it would follow that *JEHOVAH* had created *Adam* to sin so that He might manifest the treasures of wisdom in him—which is not the case. For God, in so far as He is called God, can NOT will evil.

### III. Defense: What is the Firstborn before all Creatures? Text I.

...from the Desire. In the Desire, the Will generates—specifically in the impression of the Desire—*three properties*: Darkness, Fire, and Light. In this generating, the Eternal Voice exists, which the Will of the Free-Desire <note>original: "Lust"</note> or Longing carries along with it.

<margin>† Colossians 1:15, 17</margin>
201. This Voice is God’s Word—the † *Firstborn*, existing without and before all creatures. Through this Voice, the Will in its impression generates darkness and anguish, as well as perceptibility and feeling: the Eternal Nature. This nature consists of a spiritual *Sulphur, Mercury,* and *Sal* <note>The three principles of alchemy, representing soul, spirit, and body/structure in Boehme's mysticism</note>, which is a likeness and out-breathed substance of the voice of the Eternal Will of the Abyss—that is, of God.

202. The Voice in the Eternal Will, which is a Spirit, is resonant, or something that is capable of sounding—a *possibility* of a sound—but in itself, it is still quiet or silent. The properties of the impression (Nature) are the Voice of the Will’s instrument, through which God’s Voice manifests itself.

# I. Text. Christ is the Restorer of what Adam lost. Apology III.

222. No! God created **Adam** for eternal life in Paradise, with paradisiacal quality <note>original: "source or quality" — Böhme often uses these terms to describe the active properties or "flavors" of divine or natural forces</note> and perfection. He forbade him from eating of the quality of evil and good. He created a perfect, expressed image in the mirror <note>original: "Looking-Glass"</note> of the eternal, perceived image that exists without physical substance. The power of **Jehovah**—that is, the love of God the Father—thoroughly enlightened him, just as the sun shines through and illuminates the whole world.

223. The divine sun shone through and through **Adam** in his heavenly substance—that is, in the pure element <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "pure element" is the spiritual substance behind the four physical elements</note>. Outwardly, the physical sun enlightened him. Neither heat nor cold affected him, for he lived in perfect harmony and balance with them. The pure element held the four physical elements <note>fire, air, water, and earth</note> gathered and contained within itself, as the day contains the night. No one shall persuade me that God was not manifested in **Adam**; He is indeed manifested in all things, but according to the specific nature or property of each thing.

224. In the specific nature in which **Adam** was created, God was manifested within him. But when Adam manifested the center of the "anger" <note>In this context, "anger" refers to the harsh, contracting force of nature separated from divine love</note> within himself, God established enmity against evil. He then manifested the "Serpent-Crusher" <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head</note> in man. This power had previously been hidden in God's power before sin; it existed in the divine **unity** within the love of God, in **Jesus**. Thus, this Crusher of the serpent was set as a boundary or goal for man, toward which he should turn his desire.

225. This does not mean that man should become **Jesus** or a god, but that we should direct our faith toward Him. Through our desire, we should receive **Christ** into ourselves—He who has broken death into pieces—so that He may make our soul and the faded image of **Adam** live again in the divine life within Himself.

# III: Apology. *We must continually slay the Earthly Will.* Text. I.

229. That which was lost is not restored for the sake of the earthly man, so that he should keep his dominion. Rather, Christ came so that He might regenerate that part of Adam which disappeared and died when he awakened to sin. <margin>Genesis 2:17.</margin> Concerning this, God said, *In the day you eat of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, you shall surely die.* Adam died to the divine world and awakened to the outward world—namely, to the **sin-house**, which is full of misery and an *ever*-dying state of existence <note>original: "source or quality," a term Böhme uses to describe the active properties or "flavor" of a spiritual state</note>.

230. Christ would not give life to the sin-nature anew. Instead, He died in His body to *our* life of sin (which existed within the dominion of the four elements because of Adam's sin) and brought our true life of the pure element <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "pure element" is the spiritual substance behind the four physical elements</note> to the surface again. *His death was our life.* The four elements held us captive in "the Anger" <note>The harsh, contracting force of nature separated from divine love</note>, but He brought our life out of the four elements *through death* and back into the pure element. In doing so, He made a path or way to heaven for us within human life once again.

231. Now we must follow after Him and also die away from the life of the four elements mentioned before. Yet first of all, we must receive Christ within us; He leads us through the death of our own dying into His path, through death into the **pure element**.

232. This outward, visible body cannot inherit the element of God unless it is first broken in pieces. But if we have "put on Christ" through the desire of faith, He introduces our life's essence into Himself—into His mystery—namely, into His **rest** in the grave.

<margin>Psalm 16:8, 9.</margin>
233. Concerning this, David says that *he should rest secure*. For the Lord was set before him in Christ, and he rested under Christ’s protection. This rest was found in the "limit" or "mark" of the Covenant—in the mirror <note>original: "Looking-Glasse"</note> of Christ, which God set before him in the Covenant of circumcision and in the sacrifices, as if Christ were present in them. For God had promised Christ through those signs until He finally came in the flesh.

<margin>* Esaias Stiefel</margin>
234. Therefore, let this author <note>E.S. refers to Esaias Stiefel, a contemporary whose perfectionist views Böhme contested</note> not persuade us **that the earthly man, while still in sin and without the *breaking* of his outward life, can *wholly* put on Christ both inwardly and outwardly. Nor should he persuade us that the *sinful* outward nature completely dies when a man enters into repentance, or that Christ alone awakes or arises to be generated both inwardly and outwardly within the man.**

235. No! Christ came to heal the sore that Adam caused when he immediately died to the Kingdom of Heaven through the **sin-bite** <note>original: "Sinne-Bit," likely referring to the eating of the forbidden fruit</note>. Christ came to awaken or raise up the inward man that disappeared in Adam, to regenerate it by His power, to lead the poor soul back into a divine will, and to grant it the noble **Jewel** of the Holy Spirit once again.

9. The man **Adam** was *not* created and manifested in *Christ's* image, but in his own image, which **God** had seen from eternity in His wisdom in the spoken Word; He can show us no other.

10. **God** created man in His image, and to the image of **God**; it is not written "of *Christ*," but "of **God**." He was created as a substance <note>original: "to substance"; meaning man was made into a substantial, essential being</note> according to that image, and was created in his own image known from eternity by the Spirit of **God**.

<margin>† Psalm 104:3.</margin>

With this instrument, He would govern everything that exists and lives in the world, and so manifest Himself in this human sound in man's voice, riding upon the wings of man's spirit; as *David* says, † *The Lord rides upon the wings of the wind.*

For *Adam’s* spirit went out from him.

# Chapter 3. In Christ, we should resist the desires of our flesh until our death. Text II.

50. The purpose is that the shell—into which the devil has introduced his imagination and made his den of thieves—may be *altogether* broken apart so that there is no more life in it. Then, as soon as the outward man <note>The "outward man" refers to the physical body and the temporary, earthly personality.</note> dies, the *soul* is freed from that evil beast. THEN it has the open gate in its beloved image, in which Christ has revealed himself with the divine love-fire.

51. And then the union is already there; the *bride* cheers her *bridegroom*—namely, the noble virgin <note>original: "Noble Virgin"; in Böhme’s theology, this is the "Heavenly Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, the spiritual counterpart to the soul.</note> in the love of *Christ*, being awakened again. She takes the soul—that is, her loving bridegroom and husband—into her arms of divine desire. What happens there, I have no pen to write; it is beyond anything human or natural to describe.

52. A converted man experiences what God's love and *sweetness* are when he returns to his Father and acknowledges himself as a *swineherd* <note>A reference to the Prodigal Son in Luke 15.</note>, bewailing his past sins and seeking the Father's grace and favor. This happens when Christ, his bridegroom, places upon him the virgin-like garland or crown, where the pearl of the divine reception of grace is first sown.

53. What joy the virgin has when she obtains *life* again and receives her bridegroom, *Christ*! How very affectionately and blessedly she presents herself toward the soul, embracing the soul—her man or *husband*—in her love. At this, indeed, both soul and body tremble with joy.

<margin>* E. S. <note>These initials refer to Erasmus Schmidt, a professor and critic of Böhme.</note></margin>

54. Only those who have been guests in this place know this. 55. For he is but a "literal saint" and a disputant—and, moreover, a high-minded despiser of the children of Christ and their *different* gifts. ### III. T. We should distinguish between the heavenly and the earthly man. Appendix III.

<margin>* Jacob Boehme's <note>original: "Behme's"</note> Answer:</margin>
Here follows my Answer and Explanation, which the reader should consider very carefully.

->I.<-

First, concerning the text of *Isaiah 54:5*, which this author explains: he has confused it even more. He has moved it entirely away from a correct and orderly understanding into a confused, unintelligible matter or substance, and has completely confounded the eternal birth of the Holy Trinity with the created being <note>original: "Creature"</note>.

2. His intent is to investigate the *birth* or *origin* <term>geniture: the process of birth or generation</term> and the source of all things or substances. He has immersed <note>original: "demersed"</note> himself into the *birth* or *generation* of the Deity and elevated himself so high that he has set himself up to be exactly like God, making himself a *god*. Yet he understands as little about it as a cow understands the *bell* she carries around her neck; she only hears it sound and *ring*.

3. *Second*: He involves all heavenly and earthly creatures in the destruction <note>original: "perdition"</note> of man, claiming they must all be reborn and redeemed again in Christ. He creates a pitiful, forced ruin of correct understanding by confusing one thing with another.

4. *Third*: He totally confuses the *distinction* between God and the created being <note>original: "Creature"</note>, forcing them together into one against all reason and truth. He places the earthly man—provided he simply *believes*—entirely within the Deity along with his mortal substance. He gives him full power or authority in heaven and earth, which is quite contrary to the foundation of Holy Scripture and also contrary to visible or apparent things.

5. He desires to be, rule, overpower, know, and understand *everything* in *all things*—even God himself. Yet he does not understand the basic nature <note>original: "Ground"</note> of a *fly* in its essence and substance, *much less* the divine and uncreated nature. He creates a confused cycle like a *drunken stupor*.

6. And if such flattering hypocrisy were ever fully believed, then the *greatest* Antichrist of all would be born. This Antichrist sets itself on the seat or throne of God, very audaciously presenting itself as GOD, and displaying its own great holiness as if it were without blemish or mortality.

7. This is entirely contrary to the visible foundation of all truth. It completely hides the "man of sin" <note>A biblical reference to the fallen, sinful nature of humanity or a specific figure of lawlessness</note> within the anger of God and turns him into a "dear son of God" in his *outward* flesh. Thus, he leads us so far away from true understanding that we cannot see how Christ is born IN us, or what the difference is between the heavenly and earthly man.

8. He wants to persuade us that we are *both* inwardly and outwardly totally perfect, holy, and *without* any blemish or sin, as long as we simply believe.

<header>III. Appendix: We should distinguish between the heavenly and the earthly man. Part III.</header>

...believe, and then the natural, outward, sinful man *dies* and becomes wholly and completely changed into *Christ's* person. He claims that, while a man is here on earth, he is (as the opponent says) *wholly* and altogether *Christ*—who sits in heaven at the right hand of God and is on earth a total, perfect God-man, inwardly and outwardly, without defect.

9. And there is nothing left to do but for the poor sinner—who would gladly repent and believe—to fall down before THIS great, holy God (which the opponent himself claims to BE) and worship him, so that the opponent may receive the sinner into grace, into HIS holiness.

10. For he insists on being the Christ in ALL things, in divine omnipotence and substance. He does not distinguish at all between what God, Christ, and man are, or what the creature, humanity, and God are; in him, flesh and spirit are all one; furthermore, mortality and immortality are the same.

11. Yet I would very much like to see him, to know whether he is any different from other men. In all my life, I have never heard anyone tell of any such wonderful man in the world, nor have I read of such a *wonder* in any history. If what he says is true, then according to the standard of the Scriptures, he must shine seven times brighter than the SUN, and other men and living creatures would be *struck* blind before him because of his great holiness and clarity or brightness.

12. But he might say that men cannot see that in him—as indeed he does say—and that no man on earth has seen it in him or in any other man. This is especially true since heat and cold, as well as pain and sickness, take hold of him, and he continually clothes himself with the clothing of *beasts* <note>original: "Cloathing of Beasts" — meaning clothing made from animal products, a sign of the fallen, earthly state</note>. He sleeps and wakes, uses *earthly* food and drink under the curse of God, and—what is much more—he lives by reproaching and cursing honest people who love God.

13. In that regard, we still strongly doubt his perfect *holiness*, and we do not take his confusion for God's voice coming out of God's holy substance. This is especially true since we see that he still understands nothing of the divine and natural birth or generation <term>geniture: the process of birth or generation</term> and the eternal *revelation* or *manifestation* of all things or substances, and how one originates out of another. Yet he elevates himself like this, without divine knowledge, based on a mere *literal* concept which he perverts, flying high without wings before his feathers have even grown.

14. But since this is a subtle, wandering <note>original: "extravagant," meaning wandering outside the bounds of reason</note> error, which might seduce honest hearts who fear God in their innocence (if they do not sufficiently search into this eccentricity), I want the reader who loves the truth to be *informed* of this almost completely hidden error. I will unfold it a little so that people may see this "insuperably superlative" sense <note>original: "fence," likely an OCR error for "sense"</note> as he imagines it, and in doing so, I will reveal the true foundation, which has *better testimony* and also agrees with what is visible and apparent.

15. I do not wish to argue with this confused *wheel* <note>original: "Wheel"; Boehme often uses the image of a spinning wheel to describe a mind in a state of chaotic or circular reasoning</note> or to defame him, but I do this for the sake of Christ’s children, whom Christ has redeemed with his blood, to see whether many will gain better discernment...

At the beginning, he makes a great speech or sermon, signifying how he will *answer out of Christ the Triune God*, out of God’s mouth and heart, and out of all saints; he says men should listen to it and look upon it as God’s infallible word.

17. This has now been sufficiently explained above—that such a claim is groundless and that to speak in such a manner is ineffectual. Furthermore, it does not become any angel or man to speak so.

18. But concerning the text of *Isaiah 54:5*, the explanation of it has been very sufficiently made before; yet for the reader’s sake, I will set down *something more*.

<margin>* Isaiah 54:5</margin>
19. The Prophet says, *“He who has made you is your husband; the Lord of Hosts is his name; and your Redeemer, the Holy One in Israel, who is called the God of all things.”*

20. The Prophet speaks here in his own understanding, not of a literal man or husband, but by way of *similitude* <note>original: "Similitude" — an analogy or comparison</note>. In the same way that the seed of a man lies within the man or husband, from which a person becomes manifested, so everything—yes, all whatsoever is manifested—lay in the *Eternal* Man or Husband, namely, in the Generator of all things or substances.

<margin>† John 1:4</margin>
21. This is especially true of man’s life, which He *breathed* into the created image according to the similitude of His substantiality <note>original: "Substantiality" — the divine essence or spiritual substance</note>, and out of all His out-breathed substance; as *John* says: † *The life of man was in HIM*.

22. And yet, in this we are not to think as if the in-breathed life or substance of man were only and solely the Spirit of God in divine holiness and omnipotence. No; otherwise, if that life had perished [as happened in the Fall], then God would have perished. Instead, the life of every creature is *given* to the creature out of the original source of its own substance.

23. So the substance of man is *given forth out of the Three Principles* <note>Boehme’s "Three Principles" refer to the dark fire-world (First Principle), the light world (Second Principle), and the external physical world (Third Principle).</note>, namely: out of eternity and out of time. This includes the substance and source or quality of darkness, which contains nature—namely, *Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt* <note>original: "Sulphur, Mercurius and Sal" — in alchemy, these represent the fundamental spiritual/physical properties of all matter: energy, fluidity, and stability.</note>.

24. Regarding the *first* part and Principle: it is spiritual, acting as a rule <note>original: "Regiment"</note> or dominion and source or quality out of which substance arises. Regarding the *second* part: it relates to the outward world and is corporeal. It is fiery in the *first* Principle; and in the *third* Principle, it is earthly (from the dark impression), made of the four elements, and sidereal <note>original: "sydereall" — influenced by the stars and planets</note> from the sun and stars. And from the *second* Principle, it comes from the light and power of that out-breathed or generated substance, which is heavenly, holy, and oily <note>original: "Oyly" — a term Boehme uses to describe the gentle, life-giving essence of the divine light.</note>,

30. Adam squandered this life and lived only in the dark, fiery, and earthly part. But God has manifested *that life* again in man through JESUS—that is, out of the greatest depth of humility in CHRIST, and out of God himself.

31. *Thirdly*, God’s Spirit has breathed into him the "Air"—that is, the soul of the outward earthly substance—through the earthly flesh. This is a life of the earthly flesh which should have been *subjected* to the holy life. It was meant to stay hidden within him as a help and instrument, keeping heat and cold in equal agreement. Neither of them was intended to rule; instead, the holy life of the Second Principle in the Son *should rule*. The *Sulphur* and *Mercurius* <note>original: "Sulphur" and "Mercurius" — alchemical terms used here to represent the active, transformative forces of nature</note> should rule in a holy power (meaning, in a "Quintessence" <note>original: "Quintessence" — the purest "fifth element" that balances and perfects the other four</note> within the pure Element). ## IV. T. The heavenly Image lives in some, but in some it does not. III. A. P. I.

24. The kingly prophet of God, David, * was a man after God's own heart, as the Scripture testifies of him, in whom was the Spirit of God; and he prophesied of *Christ*. But he also said, † *In sin was I born, and in sin did my mother conceive me.* This also manifested itself in him, so that he had, *alongside* the spiritual man, a sinful man WITHIN him, who was a **murderer** and an **adulterer**—as the same may be seen in the Patriarchs.

25. But who will now say of David that he was not holy, seeing he was a man after God's heart? Yet, who will say that his murder and adultery were without sin? -># Point 1, Article 3. What is the true drawing of the Father. Text 4.<-

32. The inward spiritual *flesh* is heavenly, and the Devil cannot possess it. 33. But when the wicked person turns toward God and turns the soul’s will toward God, then *Christ* is born as a man out of that disappeared seed. He is placed before the Devil in the outward *flesh* as a crusher or bruiser of the serpent <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, where the "seed of the woman" shall bruise the serpent's head</note>, who hinders and breaks the will of the evil flesh so that sin is NOT committed.

Then the anger of God comes into the *center* of the soul and also insists on its fierce, wrathful government; and the Devil, with his false or wicked *lusts*, crowds himself into that space.

35. And the *elementary spirit* <term>the part of the human spirit driven by physical elements and earthly needs</term> hungers constantly after its mother, the elements. Then the Devil brings the lust to the surface and revolves the desire; then the hand and the mouth take action and perform the work of the false or *evil* desire.

36. Then *Christ* stands in his tender humanity within the inward holy body and reproves the outward man. He presses upon him, takes his power from him, and sets it before the eyes of the *mind* that this act is an abomination and *sin*. He drives the man again to unload that which the fleshly desire has burdened him with—namely, toward *abstinence* and repentance.

37. This is nothing else but a departure from the abomination. Then the committed abomination remains as food for God's anger and for the Devil—that is ITS refreshment—but the *mystery* of man becomes *free* again within itself.

41. And if the soul enters in, then Jesus Christ—as a true man—exists within that faded, disappeared substance <note>original: "faded disappeared Substance"; Boehme’s term for the divine image in humanity that became dormant after the Fall</note>, and he possesses the "Gates of the Deep" <note>the fundamental spiritual foundations or depths of reality</note>. ->42.<-

But concerning the *Conception of Children*: the claim that a truly regenerate Christian man should beget children who are *totally* holy and without guilt—as 
<margin>† E. S. <note>likely referring to Esaias Stiefel, a contemporary opponent of Boehme</note></margin>
† this author imagines—is "Babel" <note>meaning a source of confusion or false religious doctrine</note> and a great error. It is a deception introduced by the serpent, under which it tries to cover itself so that a person might not recognize its "kitten" <note>original: "Kitling"; here used metaphorically to mean the offspring or product of a deceptive spirit</note>. It desperately wants to be called "holy." For a long time, men have called the serpent the "black, slippery, evil devil," but now it would like to be called "Christ" and "a god." But the Most High has unmasked it, so that we see and know it; and I would have you warned in a Christian manner.

43. Every tree and vegetable brings forth fruit out of itself, according to what the plant is. But know this: the spirit of nature presses so hard into the power from which the branch grows that the branch often becomes evil and withered—yes, even an altogether dry, rotten branch.

44. It is the same with man: that which is sown is what grows. But God’s anger—through the Devil's influence <note>original: "Imagination"</note>, especially when the Devil observes that the outward alignment <note>original: "Constellation"</note> of the stars in the elements is evil—often forces itself in as well. Thus, honest parents beget evil children, and on the contrary, evil parents many times beget honest children, as experience makes apparent before our eyes.

45. And to that end, Christ has commanded us to practice 
<margin>* Infant Baptism <note>original: "Pedobaptisme"</note></margin>
* *Infant Baptism*, to baptize the child in the name of the Holy Trinity. In this covenant, He will be powerful; with His power, He kindles again the poor, imprisoned "tinder" <note>the latent spark of divine life or potential for grace within the soul</note> and takes the serpent's poison away from the light of life, so that the divine drawing remains open.

# I. P. A. III, Strife is as long as the outward life continues. T. IV.

...itself, in its substance, is *iron* at one time as well as another. It is never fire in its own *self-property* <note>original: "self-property"; its inherent nature or essence</note>, and yet it is *fire*. But the *fire’s might* <note>original: "might"; power or force</note> does not reside in the iron; rather, the fire only lends its nature to it as an instrument or a *body* in which the fire blazes.

<margin>* NOTE</margin>
61. * Thus understand us also, concerning GOD and the CREATURE. The fire, when it *blazes* in the iron, signifies the soul when it is *kindled* in God’s light. The light and the shining of the fire signify the *Holy Fire* and the *Virgin* <note>The "Noble Virgin" or Sophic Wisdom represents the divine mirror or image of God</note>. The *power* of the light is the Pearly-Garland <note>A symbol of spiritual rebirth and the soul's victory in Christ</note> about which I write in my books. The Virgin does not give THAT to the fire-soul—namely <note>original: "viz:"</note> to the origin of the fire—to be its own property.

62. But she sets the same upon it and *presses* the same into its heart; yet the soul cannot comprehend it as its very *own*, just as fire cannot comprehend the light. And yet, the light shines out of the fire. The fire has a different source or *quality* than the light. The fire is the Father and the light is the Son, and yet they form two principles, one WITHIN another.

63. Know then: the creature is not God; it remains eternally beneath God. But God blazes through it with His desire for the Love-Fire—namely, with His light and shining. And the soul—namely, the person—retains that very light as its own *so long* as the *will* remains in God’s light.

64. But if the soul enters again into its own property—namely, into the *center* of its origin in its own power, moving out of resignation <note>original: "resignation"; the state of surrendering one's ego or will to God</note> and into self-centeredness—then the Virgin takes away this Pearly-Garland from the soul. For the soul—namely, the bridegroom—*has run away* from its spouse *Christ* (that is, from its Love-Fire) and has become *perjured* <note>broken its sacred vow</note>.

65. Then the soul goes into the outward flesh, into the Devil’s net in dark restraint, and seeks its *own place* and rest, but finds nothing except the *bestial pleasure* of the flesh, with which it *pampers itself*.

66. But the Noble Virgin calls it continually to *return* again. If it returns, then it is well and readily received, but the *first* wedding is not held again. There is indeed a *glorious* welcome, but it is not like the first betrothal <note>original: "espousal"</note>. We speak of what we know.

67. But if the bridegroom—namely, the soul—does *not* return, then *Christ* takes back the garland which He gave to the Virgin for a life. Then the soul remains in its *nothingness*—without source or quality, as if vanished or faded—and it is eternally *not* perceptible or visible to the *soul*.

68. And the soul remains in its † anxiety, if the *sore* <note>original: "Soare"; pain or wound</note> † *bitter wrath* <note>original: "Gremen"; likely from the German "Grimmen," referring to the fierce wrath or spiritual anguish of the soul's dark fire</note> is in it at the end of the *outward* body. In that regard, it stands in eternal shame and scorn because it has lost its kingly crown.

74. The *properties* <note>original: "Properties"; the inherent qualities or forces that make up the soul</note> of the soul are not in perfect harmony, as God created the first soul. In this multiplicity of wills is the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; a Latin term meaning "turmoil" or "disturbance," referring to the destructive force that arises when natural elements are in conflict</note>; for one will is the enemy of the other. These cannot be broken because their origin is in eternity, from the *Center of Nature*.

75. *Unless* God’s light kindles itself within them, they cannot be *transmuted* <note>transformed from one state to another</note> into One Will. Only then does the enmity and contrary will in the *center* of the soul's life *cease*. At that point, the outward life in the child also exists within the flesh of perdition <note>original: "perdition"; the state of being lost or fallen</note> and is subject to *death*.

76. For just as the properties in the soul's life are in strife and contradiction, so too are the properties of the outward life; for in *Adam* all...

# IV. T. Distinguish the holy from the bestial in love. III. A. P. II.

<meta>catchword: 8. For</meta>

<margin>† F. B.</margin>
->Now follows † my answer to this second point,<-
->together with an explanation of it.<-

->1.<-
<margin>* E. S.</margin>
**THAT** which this * author sets down concerning **Christian married people—that it IS so**—should certainly be wished that it *were* so. But it is not so, *perfectly*, in anyone. They lack a good source <note>original: "Good Spring"; meaning a pure origin or fountainhead</note>, for this great holiness was squandered away in *Adam*.

<margin>† Matthew 18:20</margin>
2. Indeed, Christ says: † *“Wherever two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the midst of them.”* Christ is indeed with holy married people who fear God, if they begin all their affairs in his name. He governs and blesses them if they remain with him in earnest sincerity. I do not speak against that at all; also, all their works in the true married state are acceptable to him, for Christ has come so that he might destroy the works of the *devil*.

<margin>* E. S.</margin>
3. But the * author must not ascribe such great and *perfect* holiness here to the work of human propagation <note>original: "propagation"; the production of offspring</note>. And though it may indeed be called holy, it must be better distinguished *what* in it is holy and what is unholy. Otherwise, every person's burning, brutish, and bestial lust of the flesh would be *accounted* as holiness.

4. For example, when they vehemently tickle themselves <note>original: "tickle themselves"; here meaning to excite or gratify their own desires</note> with imagination and desire toward a husband or wife, as if there were great, *perfect* holiness in it, and as if it were done only and solely by God's prompting, through *Christ's* power and instigation.

<margin>† E. S.</margin>
5. And here the † author does NOT *distinguish* between what is divine and what is natural. He jumbles the whole work into one and calls it ALL divine, as if the work of such union—and the inclination of the desire of one toward the other—were all done by the driving of the Spirit of *Christ*.

6. He also applies this totally to the coming together of two married people. Regarding honest, virtuous children <note>original: "children"; here likely meaning "people" or "offspring of God"</note> who pray to God in earnest *sincerity* for it beforehand and submit their will to his, it is indeed true that two persons often come together through God’s sending.

7. I also praise this when it is SO done, for there may be *more* blessing and salvation or happiness than in THOSE whom the "lust of the eye" merely brings together and nature couples. I would not oppose the author in this, but would willingly receive and allow it as right, IF the thorn and poison did not stick in it and under it—namely, the claim of *total* holy perfection, by which he supposes he *begets* children who are *void* of original inherited sin.

## II. P. A. III. Distinguish the holy from the bestial in love. T. IV

8. For the sake of this one article, I will explain this point so that people may see what is divine and what is natural, what is holy and what is bestial. I do this so that the flattering hypocrisy and **seeming holiness**—under which people try to cover their original inherited sin—might be exposed.

9. And I do this so that honest married people should not be complacent or careless, but rather realize that they too are sinners. They must learn to be afraid of God's anger and be humble before Him. They should diligently learn, with great caution, to pray with one another, so that the Devil does not exploit <note>original: "sift"; to test or try someone's faith, often through temptation</note> their natural impurity and throw them into a bestial state.

10. This state is indeed joined to the work of *marriage*, for the holy work is performed alongside a bestial work. This originates from the Fall of *Adam* and *Eve*. Married people should learn to distinguish the holy aspect of love from the bestial, and learn to remain modest,
->**Chaste and Temperate**,<-
before God and humanity in this work.

<margin>* E. S.</margin>
11. One should not act like a burning, lustful bull. This * author <note>referring to E.S.</note> opens a wide door to such brutish behavior by calling it entirely holy; in his holy proclamation, all shame would eventually be extinguished.

12. Yet understanding and nature itself testify that an *abomination* <note>original: "Abomination"; something that causes disgust or hatred, specifically in a religious or moral sense</note> is attached to it, which is not entirely holy before God. Even nature itself, along with the soul, is **ashamed** of it—a fact that ought to be well-considered. Consider how the poor soul, which reveals itself through the eyes, is ashamed before its *Bridegroom, Christ*, because after the Fall, it must now reproduce itself in such a bestial manner, like other animals.

13. For this reason, I will explain it so that married people may learn to know themselves. I do not want *this* author to make them so totally blind that they live in abomination before God like animals, without any knowledge of it. Unless it were for this reason, I would not specifically oppose him on this article; for holy people should also produce holy children, yet this miserably and often fails, as is apparent to our eyes.

<margin>† Genesis 1:26.</margin>
14. We know what *Moses* says: That † God said: *“Let us make Man,* <gloss>an image that is like us</gloss>.” He does not say two images, but one image that is like us.

### IV. Text. Man is the inward and outward World. III. Ap. Po. II.

16. But God is manifested in TWO Principles: specifically, through the stern Fire-world according to the Father's attribute, and through the Light and Love-world in the Son's attribute. Yet He is but ONE single undivided substance, one God; just as Fire and Light are one.

17. In this way, He also created His Image, Man, according to His likeness, out of His spoken-forth substance—out of ALL things into ONE substance, into one single Image. He also breathed the Spirit of all THREE Principles into one single Spirit.

18. All the *Three worlds*—namely, the eternal dark, cold, and fiery world (the Eternal Nature), as well as the eternal light and fiery world together with its substance (the pure Element, and within it, Paradise)—as well as the *outward* four-elemental and celestial <note>original: "Syderiall"; relating to the stars or constellations</note> world with its substance, were all in this created Image. They existed as one in equal harmony and agreement.

19. Man was and is both the inward and outward world. The inward *world* is the Heaven where God dwells; thus, Man was on Earth as if in *Heaven*. The inward and outward were one. The inward manifested itself in the outward—that is, God manifested in Time. The outward is *Time*, which in Man was swallowed up by Eternity. However, it was manifested in itself, not entirely for the sake of ruling, but for the *wonder* of the dominion of the Divine World.

20. The outward world did not recognize itself within Time, but worked within itself as an instrument of the *Master*. The outward *Sulphur* and *Mercury* <note>In this mystical context, Sulphur and Mercury refer to spiritual qualities or "principles" of matter rather than just physical chemicals.</note> of the body were manifested in the power of the inward, spiritual *Sulphur* and *Mercury*. The *tinctures* <note>original: "Tinctures"; in alchemy and mysticism, a spiritualized substance or energy that can transform or infuse other materials with its qualities</note> of both were manifested in one another as one. The Spirit worked through *Time*, and that was a Paradise where neither heat nor cold could be felt.

21. The life of *both worlds*—the heavenly and holy in the pure Element, and the outward in the four elements—was only one single life. This was a *likeness* of God; specifically, an *exact* image.

22. For God dwells in Time, yet Time is not manifested *within* him, but *before* him, as a likeness. It is within him in his dominion all the same. Time is his *servant* and his work; it lives in itself, but God is the life of *Time*, though He is incomprehensible to Time. Time does not rule God, but exists in him as an instrument with which He rules and creates.

From that center, it was breathed into *Adam* by the Holy Spirit, through the movement of the Father out of the Three Principles.

## II. P. A. III. *The Discord of the Properties was the Fall.* Te. IV.

24. And this is its Fall and Sin: that it has, through its powerful desire, revealed the properties of the Dark World in the **Center** of Eternal Nature. This was done through **Imagination**; in that it introduced its lust into the "instrument of time"—that is, into the outward world.

25. And it wanted to test how it tasted when the equality of harmony departed or separated from one another, so that evil and good were revealed, each in itself. It lusted to taste the flavor of both, and thereby be all-knowing and cunning; in the same way, **Lucifer** perished. He lusted after the dark **Center** in the fire-birth and stirred that up with his desire, so that the harmony or equal agreement within him might be revealed in an awakening of all properties. From this, lust and falsehood (or wickedness) came into existence for him.

26. For if the life’s forms—namely, the forms of Eternal Nature—were revealed **each one** on its own, then there is a great conflict, for every one wants to rule, and every one has its own will. If this were not so, then there would be neither perception nor discovery, but only an eternal **stillness**.

27. But now, the life's forms should not be revealed by **each** acting or pressing itself forward; rather, they should exist in equal harmony, like a tuned lute. And the **Spirit** which was produced out of this equal harmony by God’s Spirit was also in equal harmony—specifically, the spirit of the soul. Just as the **air** comes out of the **fire**, the soul’s spirit should enter into the "Sound" of God and strengthen itself in the power of the light, and with that very power strike the **cittern** <note>original: "Cittron"; a lute-like stringed instrument. The author uses it as a metaphor for the harmony of the human soul.</note> of the life’s forms.

28. But the soul did not do that. Instead, it entered into its own will and reached for the **Center** of the life’s forms and stirred it up. It wanted to be GOD itself and made itself a **dark devil**, according to the first formation in the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be done," referring to the creative word of God</note> of its own quality. Out of this, in this world, evil poisonous worms and beasts have come to be, according to the outward formation. And that is the actual fall of the **devil**, as well as of **Adam**.

-> 29. <-

But so that we may make it easier to understand concerning **Adam**, as also concerning his **Wife**: **Adam** was a total, entire image of God. When God had created him, he was both man and wife, and yet neither of them; but a pure **virgin** in the likeness of God.

30. He had the fire’s **Matrix** <note>original: "Matrix"; the womb or generative source from which something grows</note>, and also the light’s **Matrix**, out of which water is generated through the "dying" (or transformation) in the fire through the element. He had the fire’s and light’s **desire** in him—specifically, the source of love and of wrath, according to the Principles.

At that point, the beautiful Image was compromised, for vanity loved *itself*. It would not enter into God’s Love—that is, into the Holy power—nor could it, for God does NOT accept that as a child.

->41.<-
<margin>As a Mediator.</margin>
Now when this was done, God saw the Fall, just as He had known it would happen beforehand. In that regard, He saw and foresaw Man in the Center of His Heart within His loving desire. 43. He, *Adam*, could no longer generate life spiritually, for he had clearly passed into the *lust* of self-centeredness. If he had kept GOD as his *help*, he would have been able; but seeing that he could not, *therefore God said*: *It is not good*. In the beginning, it was indeed *good*, but within this lust, it was *not good*.

44. For the ability stands in God alone, and *Adam* had left God to pursue self-centeredness. Consequently, the Father's wrath gathered itself within the creative command <note>original: "Fiat"</note> above and sought to take creaturely form. From this, the lust for both evil and good *intertwined*—namely, the hunger for darkness, fire, and light, and the substance of all these things.

45. However, the power of the creature was gone because it relied on self-centeredness; then that self-centeredness sank down into powerlessness <note>original: "unability"</note>.

<margin>Genesis 2:21.</margin>
46. Now then, *Moses* says: *And God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him.* Seeing that he had departed from God into self-centeredness, God let him fall into powerlessness—that is, into sleep. He allowed this to happen because he fell into incapacity. For in his self-centeredness, he would have become a devil through the power of the "fire" <note>The harsh, consuming aspect of the soul's nature</note>, and so he was not capable of staying awake. Instead, he slept; and **this sleep is Christ’s rest in the grave.**

The **creative command** <note>original: "Fiat"; the Latin word meaning "let it be done," referring to God's act of creation</note> went forth, and here Adam lost his chaste "love-sport" and his spiritual purity <note>original: "Virginity"; refers to Adam's original state of spiritual wholeness before the separation of the sexes</note>, which Christ brought back to him again. # IV. Text: Why the Flesh Must Totally Die. III. Ap. P. II.

The soul's spirit in Adam and Eve was ashamed when they saw that they stood in such misery within their own self-centeredness <note>original: "self-hood"; the state of being focused on one's own ego and private desires rather than on God</note>, and that heat and cold pressed upon them.

<margin>Genesis 3:10–14</margin>
64. And when God called them again with the voice of Grace, Adam said, "I am naked, and I am afraid." But God said, "Who has told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree which I forbade you?" And he said, "The woman gave it to me, and I ate." And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me."

65. Here now lies the whole previously mentioned matter—or substance—of how it came to pass. For the lust resided in Adam and was introduced into physical substance through the "love-desire" within the creative command <note>original: "Fiat"; the Latin word for "let it be done," referring to God's creative act</note>. In this, Adam had his "birth" or nature established, which then became divided from him. And now, that very abomination of false or wicked desire began to lust within the woman, fully raising up the entire work of sin and abomination against God’s holiness.

66. This is the very abomination before God: that the forms of life <note>These "forms" are the fundamental spiritual properties or forces that Boehme believes constitute all reality</note> have departed from their equal agreement, each manifesting itself independently. From this, conflict arises within life—namely, the rising up of pride, as well as greed, envy, anger, and wicked cunning.

67. Thus, every form knows only itself in its self-centeredness and is manifest only to itself. Because of this, humanity—namely, the flesh—is brought into **sickness**, woe, pain, and corruption through this internal conflict.

68. For in equal harmony, no corruption can exist, because all the wills of the forms of life are but one single substance. They move in one equal harmony, where every property is the "good taste" and "love-desire" for the other. But in inequality or disharmony, there is nothing but pure enmity, where one property is not at all willing to hear, see, smell, taste, or feel the others.

69. The **enmity** of life resides in these **five senses**, which contain nothing but pure strife because of the disharmony—a disharmony that the sound, namely the voice of God, does not receive or allow to enter into itself. This remains the case unless the many conflicting wills let go of their "right" or self-interest <note>original: "propriety"</note> and sink down again totally in surrender <note>original: "resignation"; the spiritual act of yielding the individual's self-will to the divine will</note> into God’s mercy.

70. As Christ says, "*Unless you are converted and become as children—who know nothing of falsehood or wickedness—you shall not inherit the kingdom of heaven.*" Also, "*You must be born anew.*" That is, this will of falsehood and vanity must totally break, and a new will must spring forth which no longer desires falsehood or wickedness; otherwise, there is no blessedness or salvation.

71. Therefore, the flesh—in which the abomination and vanity reside as physical substance—must totally die and decay. It must go back again to the origin where it first existed in Adam, toward a new revelation or manifestation.
