# Part II. Those who desire to have Jacob Boehme do not desire to have the Primate. Apology IV.

->Answer.<-

<margin><unclear>scribble</unclear>}</margin>
158. Christ at this very day bestows on his children the **Water of Life** <note>original: "Water of Life" — a biblical reference to spiritual life and salvation</note>, and gives them **His blood of Love** to drink. That very water he gives to my thirsty soul to drink, for which I thank him eternally; for through this water, he has made me living and seeing. That is the very water I drink, and it is a water for or against death, even though the **Primate** <note>original: "Primate" — Jacob Boehme’s title for his accuser, Pastor Gregorius Richter</note> speaks of it in a perverted way.

159. But when he says that I run every morning for **brandy** <note>original: "Brande-wine"</note> or **strong liquor** <note>original: "Strong-Water"</note>, that is not true. I may not, nor can I, drink any brandy; I have for a long time had a dislike for it. It is so contrary to me that I do not even willingly smell it. It is a wonder to me that he, being a "High Priest," should be so very much mistaken. He would take it very poorly if a common man did the same; in that case, one would say he was a **liar**. I do not know at all what answer I should give to such an untruth; I believe truly that the **satanic spirit of error** has fabricated this lie.

160. I counsel you to hunt that spirit away from you; it defiles you greatly with such untruths. But if you want to be proven right, then bring forward an honest, honorable man of credit—whether he be from the city or outside the city, whoever he may be—who can say with truth that he sees me every morning drinking brandy. I appeal to the whole city and even to the **cellar-keeper of the Noble Councilors** <note>The person in charge of the city council's wine and spirits storage</note>: let them say if there is any man who can say this of me.

161. It is a great shame that you cause such untruths to be printed to the reproach of another. In your own house, people may well find great cups and glasses of brandy; but just as you are mistaken and in error regarding this, so you are mistaken also in all other articles of the **libel** <note>original: "Libell" — a formal written accusation or defamatory pamphlet</note>. There is not one of them true in the sense you represent them.

->Libel.<-

**162. CHRIST scarcely drank any wine, but the Shoemaker guzzles freely imported wine and brandy.**

->Answer.<-

<margin>* John 2:1 to 10.</margin>
163. * Christ made water into good wine (John 2) and is himself the **good wine** for the thirsty soul, which my soul freely loves to drink. But when the Primate says I love to guzzle **imported wine** <note>original: "Outlandish wine" — wine from foreign lands, which was an expensive luxury</note> and brandy, he takes that from his own example and thinks another does as he himself does. Oh, no—we poor men do not have the money to pay for it. We must be content with a draft of beer or **small drink** <note>original: "small Drink" — weak, low-alcohol beer, common for everyday hydration</note> as we are able to buy it. But people must indeed give the Primate imported wine, even though other guests at the same time must be content with something lesser.

# IV. Apology. *Christ turned Water into Good Wine.* Part II.

<margin>* Spanish wine <note>original: "Sack"—a term for fortified white wine, like Sherry</note>.</margin> 164. Spanish wine causes men to sometimes lose their wits <note>original: "loose the Primate"—likely a pun on Richter's title, suggesting he loses his dignity or senses</note> for a while. Also, one may see by the red wine-pimples on his face that he drinks strong wine much more than I do, for I have no such signs of it as he does. He drinks more foreign wine in a *week* than I do in a whole *year*.

165. But I understand very well where the matter *pinches* <note>meaning: where the real problem lies</note>. He knows that I, through *divine appointment*, have often been requested to go to **Great Lords and Noblemen**. Therefore, he thinks that when we meet, we sit together and drink our fill, as he is accustomed to doing with his companions. But no! The nobility and *powerful authorities* in positions of power, who are served with full cups, do not send for me to come to *them* for that reason, but only honest lords who fear God and who earnestly seek after *salvation*.

166. But there is in the *Primate* <note>Boehme's title for Pastor Richter</note> a distrust and resentment <note>original: "grutching"</note>; he thinks something is being taken away from him, but he need not fear it. Those people who desire to have ME do not desire to have HIM at all. There is a great difference between hypocrisy or flattery and telling the truth to one’s face. Whether the *Primate* will believe it or not, it is not my custom to flatter the rich for gifts and presents, as he supposes.

167. I truly believe that some old *scoundrels* <note>original: "Ruffians"</note> have brought him those reports as news concerning me. And the *Good Lord* <note>Boehme's sarcastic reference to Richter</note> has believed it as Gospel and written it with great earnestness. He has so enraged himself at it that he has condemned the poor shoemaker without a hearing. But it would look strange if men should ask for the *basis* of it and compare this *answer* with the *libel* <note>the defamatory pamphlet written by Richter</note>.

168. It is truly a serious matter for such a man as you are to deal with the truth in this way. The city of *Görlitz* knows very well that for a long time, I have not entered any man’s house unless *necessary*. The taverns and wine cellars are at peace as far as I am concerned. Because you have so judged and condemned me, I would willingly go nowhere. Now, if I should go to drink in taverns, how many hundreds of your insults <note>original: "Flouts"</note> would I receive? You have spread these among the common people, and these are all your "fruits" which will follow you; you may well rejoice in them.

Hold yourself close to the Word of God, and beware of the Shoemaker’s scholars or disciples, who—*

whether they be noblemen or doctors, tailors, men or women; may the LORD CHRIST destroy Satan’s instrument, and let not YOUR Word be suppressed or obscured.

->Answer.<-

170. In these words it may well be observed why the libel <note>original: "Libell"—a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation</note> has been written, namely: so that he might bring my writings to nothing and quite root them out by these defamatory reproaches. It vexes the Devil that my writings expose his *smoke-hole* <note>original: "Smoak-Hole"—likely a reference to the vent of hell or a place of hidden deception</note>, and therefore he portrays me in such a light so that NO ONE should READ me. Men might otherwise repent, and so there would be a greater breach made in his kingdom.

171. But this Devil is so very grossly vile that he goes quite naked; the people may easily observe him and learn to know him, for men see his paws in his character and reproaches, and see that he is altogether a poisonous, venomous, or spiteful spirit. It is now a quite different time than it has been; men will not now so suddenly believe what everyone says. Men will see *proof* for it. Why does he not demonstrate what he says from the *printed book*, since he forbids it to the congregation of the people? Such defamatory reproaches are no demonstrations; men may well call them filth and dung.

172. He speaks of the lion’s paw <note>Richter used the "lion's paw" as a derogatory way to identify Boehme, perhaps mocking his trade or status</note> by which men should know the *Shoemaker*. Now it may well be true that men at present may easily see the lion’s paw in me—how the lion, with contemning and reproaching, has *gripped* and *clawed* me—but the blood of JESUS CHRIST has hitherto withstood the lion, otherwise he would have torn the Shoemaker into pieces.

173. But when he says that the *Shoemaker’s doctrine is filth and dung*, he is calling CHRIST’S mind, thoughts, and *Spirit* "filth and dung." And as for his warning that men should beware of the *Shoemaker’s scholars* or disciples: to that I say, I know of no scholars or disciples, but only of Christian men, where one SOUL is refreshed by *another*. I have no *new doctrine*, but only the old, which is to be found in the BIBLE and in the kingdom of NATURE.

174. But regarding the fact that he calls his reproaching blasphemies "GOD’S WORD" (which he says men should hear only from HIM) and that he should reproach me as he does: I offer that to Christian hearts to consider, *whose child he is in spirit*.

## The Third Part of the Libel

### *A Spending-Money for the Journey*
<note>original: "Spending Penny"—historically, a small sum given to a traveler for expenses; here, Richter uses it sarcastically as a "parting gift" of insults.</note>

->Libel<-
->175<-

**T**he City of Görlitz still drives you, the Shoemaker, away and commands you to be gone to where your writings are highly esteemed. Go quickly and get a great distance away, you vain mouth who reproaches and blasphemes GOD! Try, you miserable man, to see what mischief is prepared for you.

->Answer<-

<margin>* 1 Corinthians 10:12</margin>
176. O Prince! Keep this *spending-money* for yourself for when you go to heaven; I desire nothing from you. Your vain, reproaching blasphemies will indeed follow after you as your own *spending-money*. * Be not deceived: let him who stands take heed lest he fall. Although you indeed persecute me and intend to banish me, who knows who it is that will also persecute you in a short time?

177. The *signatures* <note>original: "Signatures"—in Boehme’s philosophy, these are the outward signs or "marks" in nature that reveal an object’s inner spiritual essence</note>, or the signs of it, are at hand. It is only fair that you beforehand do to others as you would want done to you afterward as a punishment; but you must fill up your measure. If you do not repent, then the evil spirits will one day sing you a very grievous song and command you to go far away from the countenance of God. For what you do now, you do to CHRIST in his members; and that will He also do to you, if you do not quickly convert and repent.

<header>Part II. Peter’s shadow harmed the Devil. Apology IV.</header>

*...your shadow hurts many of them exceedingly.*

->Answer<-

<margin>* Acts 5:15–16</margin>
179. The * *shadow of St. Peter also did the Devil great harm*; likewise, my shadow also only harms the Devil and the Antichrist <note>original: "Antichrist"—Boehme, like many reformers, used this term to describe the corrupt institutional church or anyone opposing the "true" spirit of Christ</note>. It is likely you suppose that *my shadow might harm your earthly life* because I make known the imitation—the following—of Christ. Consequently, the people who receive that doctrine would require that you also should live as the Apostles of Christ did and imitate their example. That *does not appeal to you*, and therefore you say my *shadow* hurts some—namely, the false or wicked spirituality, or clergy—very *mightily*. It cannot be otherwise; it *must* happen this way.

180. But I know very many spiritual priests, or clergymen, whom it will **NOT** hurt, but rather do them good—those who sincerely and earnestly intend to fulfill their office of ministry. **BUT** who can do anything *before the time which brings* **ALL THINGS** *to pass*?

181. If the *Primate* <note>original: "Primate"—here referring to Pastor Gregorius Richter as the chief ecclesiastical authority in Görlitz</note> intends his warning or admonition so faithfully, then let him stop his reproachful blasphemies in the **PULPIT**. Let him only require me to come to him and show me my error. If I found that he had any truth against me and would show me a *better way*, oh, how I would cheerfully love him and faithfully thank him for it! But instead, he *rejoices* that he has anything at all that he **CAN** reproach.

<margin>* Note: Jacob Boehme did refrain from writing his works for six years.</margin>
182. **AT the beginning**, after his first reproachful blasphemy and persecution, I bowed and yielded to him for * six years together and wrote no more of my works. Why did he not stop his reproaching? Who did anything to him? But he could not stop. Why? Because God had made him a driving *hammer* <note>Boehme views Richter's persecution as a tool used by God to force his spiritual development</note> that must drive the work forward.

183. His reproaching has become my strength and growth. Through his persecution, my **Pearl** <note>In Boehme’s mystical theology, the "Pearl" represents the precious divine wisdom or the "new man" born within the soul through trial</note> has grown; he has pressed it forth and *published it himself*. In that regard, I wish him God’s mercy and compassion so that he might yet partake of it, seeing that God has used him as *my instrument* in my work.

184. I would

<margin>{</margin> 184. I would deal much more humbly toward him if he would convert than he has done toward me. He does not need to think I avoid coming before his face; I have a good conscience, and I wish him one too.

<margin>{</margin> 185. In no court of law is it useful to sentence someone unheard. I do not submit myself to his judgment in such a way, for my heart is not convinced by such a sentence. I am innocent of all that is laid to my charge. Everything he has spoken against me in the pulpit is quite contrary to my sense and meaning; not one word of it is true. He has twisted and perverted all my words with a strange interpretation.

<margin>{</margin> 186. Therefore, seeing I can now have no other judge <note>original: "Richter"—the author is making a pun on his opponent's name, Pastor Richter, which means "judge" in German</note> who will actually understand my spiritual gift, I appeal from his decision <note>original: "Judicium"—judgment or sentence</note> and censure **to the judgment of my Savior JESUS CHRIST until I can be properly heard; then I will give an account of my cause.**

->Libel<- <note>original: "Libell"—referring to the defamatory pamphlet written by Richter</note>

187. *You have so far imitated or followed after Cerinthus* <note>Cerinthus was a first-century gnostic teacher whom the early church fathers branded a heretic</note> *in that you have invented and cooked up wondrous matters and proclaim horrible things. When this Cerinthus was in the bath, he despised the LORD CHRIST and raged in his railing, babbling vehemently against GOD, but the house fell down and killed him. Thus was the teacher, along with his scholars or disciples, brought to destruction.*

->Answer<-

188. *Was Cerinthus against Christ?* I leave that matter as it is; I am with Christ and acknowledge JESUS CHRIST as my LORD and GOD. I have submitted and given myself up in obedience to Him, to live according to His will and commandment. But when the Primate <note>original: "Primate"—Richter, as the chief local clergyman</note> says that I have acted *like Cerinthus*, that certainly needs to be demonstrated; otherwise, it is not true.

<margin>{</margin> 189. But regarding his comments on my *Wondrous Things*: to that, I say in truth that I have written of no *wondrous things*. I have only written about what NATURE and MAN are. But since this seems to be *wondrous* to the Primate, the fault lies only in this: that he does NOT understand it.

<margin>Your speech betrays you</margin>

### IV. Apology. Bless those who Curse you, says Christ. Part III.

*You, his companions, beware and take heed lest you and these notorious writings of this notorious man <note>original: "this notorious Man"—referring to Boehme himself in the words of his accuser</note> perish together.*

->Answer<-

196. Men indeed find at present in Silesia many excellent, learned men who fear God and see further than the Lord Primate <note>Boehme’s sarcastic title for his chief accuser, Pastor Gregorius Richter</note> does. Their Christianity is sincere and earnest; they walk in the imitation and following of Christ. They read many good books which lead to the true ground or foundation stone. They did not first learn the imitation of Christ from me, for they possessed it before; now they simply rejoice that God also pours out such knowledge into simple people <note>common or uneducated laypeople</note>, which is indeed a wonder of God.

197. But you ascribe it to the Devil, just as the High Priests did to Christ. Some of the nobility also follow your lead; yet some of the highest nobility in Silesia observe the times and see that God has some great work in hand. You, however, are blind to it and hardened, just as the Pharisees were in the time of Christ. Therefore, the day of your punishment from God is coming quickly and is near—know that for certain.

->Libel<-

> 198. *O, now then, be gone and never return, so that you may miserably perish; rather take a shoe into your hand than a PEN.*
> ->March 27, 1624<-

->Answer<-

199. Christ said, "If they curse you, then bless them, and then you are the children of the Most High" (Matthew 5:44). Seeing, therefore, that the Primate wishes me a miserable death, his wish must certainly be from the Devil, for it runs quite contrary to God's will and commandment, as well as contrary to all honorable reason and honesty.
<margin>Luke 6:44</margin> *One shall know the tree by its fruit, and everyone may well perceive from what spirit and mind he persecutes me; he does it to please Satan and is no minister or servant of Christ.

<margin>† Note</margin> 200. But seeing † he curses me, I therefore bless him through the blood and death of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; Amen.

## Libel <note>original: "Libell"—referring to the written list of accusations or the defamatory pamphlet published against Boehme.</note>.

**NO** error <note>original: "Errour"</note> is so gross or abominable that it does not have those who support it and maintain or stand by it.

->Answer.<-

A good man supports or stands by what is **GOOD**, and an **evil** man stands by what is **EVIL**—namely <note>original: "viz"</note>, by reproaching and blasphemy. But *for those who love God, all things must work together for their best* (Romans 8:28). Even if they were stuck in the midst of all errors, they would still be in God's hands and preserved from you, the reproaching blasphemer; for such behavior is a horror to them, and they do not willingly hear people despise and reproach others.

->Libel.<-

**THE** error is small at first, and at length it becomes great.

->Answer.<-

**CHRIST** says, *The Kingdom of God is first small, like a grain of mustard seed; afterward, it grows as large as a tree* (Matthew 13:31, Mark 4:31).

## IV. Apology: God Works Eternally. Part III.

->Statement<- <note>original: "Libell." In this period, a "libel" often referred to a short written statement or a formal legal or theological challenge.</note>

> *In the world, there is always one kind of drama or scene being acted, only with changes of time, place, and persons.* <note>original: "Comedy." Here, the author uses "comedy" in the classical sense of a staged play or human drama.</note>

->Answer<-

GOD has worked from eternity, and works in eternity, and yet remains uniquely the same: the ONE, only, eternal GOD.

<meta>This page provides an interpretive key to the symbolic imagery found on the engraved title page of Jacob Boehme's "Theosophical Letters." ### An
### Abstract from Mr. <note>original: "Herre". A German title of respect similar to "Mr." or "Lord."</note> **Abraham von Frankenberg's** Letter of
### September 7 / August 28, 1651, concerning the Explanation
### of the Copperplate Title <note>original: "Copper Title". This refers to the decorative title page printed from an engraved copper plate.</note> of **Jacob Boehme’s** <note>original: "Behm’s". Jakob Böhme (1575–1624) was a German mystic whose work heavily influenced Western esotericism.</note>
### **Theosophical Letters.** <note>original: "Theoſophick Epiſtles".</note>

1. In the title page of the letters, at the upper right-hand side, is a dove with an olive branch. At the left-hand side is the city of Alexandria, or Leiden, with the dove which carries a letter or epistle sealed up, as historical accounts mention. <note>This likely refers to the historical use of carrier pigeons for mail in these cities, specifically the legendary pigeon posts of the East and the Siege of Leiden (1574).</note>

2. These are two doves, in the midst of which is the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove, with the Gospel of Peace.

3. Thus there are THREE doves, signifying the threefold spirit: 1. of God, 2. of Nature, and 3. of art. <term>In this context, "Art" refers to human skill, alchemy, or the practical application of spiritual knowledge to understand the natural world.</term>

<summary>This page contains an explanation by Abraham von Frankenberg regarding the symbolic meaning of the three doves depicted on the title page of Jacob Boehme's "Theosophical Letters." These birds represent the Holy Spirit and the three realms of God, Nature, and Art.</summary>

## The Preface of Abraham von Frankenberg, the Publisher of Jacob Boehme's <note>original: "Behm's"</note> 62 Letters called Theosophical Epistles.

Of which 21, not yet being in English, are here translated and published; with a letter concerning the author, also translated into English. <note>original: "Englished"</note>

# The Preface

-> To the Reader who loves God and the Truth. <-

-> 1. <-

If you intend to fruitfully know the true simplicity of the blessed, saving faith, and the clear, immaculate innocence of the holy life of God in Christ Jesus; together with the secret mystery of divine and natural wisdom—arising from the Light of Grace and of Nature in a very childlike and fundamental way for your temporal and eternal welfare, blessedness, happiness, and salvation: then you will certainly find a distinct, plain glimpse and a taste <note>original: "Relish"</note> of it to your satisfaction and content in these letters, which have been previously unknown to the world, yet are very Christian and divinely blessed.

2. For that reason, among other causes, we have brought these to light and published them with no small effort and expense, so that the seeker of divine and natural wonders and secret mysteries might have a true example or pattern. This instruction is not taken from books of human art <term>In this context, "art" refers to academic learning, worldly scholarship, or intellectual artifice as opposed to spiritual revelation.</term>, but is received and brought forth from divinely revealed and living experience—given to everyone according to his own measure. By this, one might honorably and edifyingly build up and refresh or enliven <note>original: "quicken"</note> oneself in a Christian, brotherly union and communion.

3. As will be clearly shown, the right manner of understanding and using these writings—especially with the fruit of repentance and active faith—leads to all blessedness and the way of salvation.

4. Concerning the author, Jacob Boehme <note>original: "Jacob Boeme"</note>, called the "Teutonic Philosopher" <note>original: "Theutonick"</note> of Alt Seidenberg <note>original: "Old-Seidenburg". Seidenberg (now Zawidów) was Boehme's birthplace.</note>: more will be declared concerning his person and his gift in his other wondrous writings mentioned here. The diligent seeker may find that information there; with these truly Christian letters, the seeker may be better prepared in the future to read the great work of his other writings.

5. These we also, with the assistance of God, [offer] for the higher knowledge of the present age, which is more scornful and perverted than it is divinely learned... <note>The text ends mid-sentence at the bottom of the page; the catchword "ned" suggests the word "learned" was split across pages or the next word began with "ned."</note>

<summary>In this preface, Abraham von Frankenberg introduces Jacob Boehme’s letters as a practical guide to divine wisdom, contrasting Boehme's "living experience" with mere academic learning. He presents these writings as a means for readers to achieve spiritual "refreshment" and prepare for Boehme's more complex theological works.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Abraham von Frankenberg, Theosophical Epistles, Light of Nature, Light of Grace, Teutonic Philosopher, mysticism, 17th-century spirituality</keywords>

## The Ninth Epistle

### To C. B., Dated 12 September 1620.

->Light, salvation, and eternal power, out of the wellspring or fountain of the Heart of JESUS CHRIST, be our refreshing, quickening, and enlivening.<-

1. Honorable and esteemed Sir, and loving brother in Christ: I received the letter you sent me along with the enclosed *Rix-dollar* <note>original: "Rix-Doller"; a silver coin used throughout the Holy Roman Empire</note>, and I return my thanks for it. God will, according to his word, richly repay it.

<margin>* Acts 8:18</margin>
2. Although * the gifts of God are not sold for money or any *earthly goods*, I find in you, according to your letter, an earnest diligence. You are desirous to study divine wisdom, and you have the *zeal* to write out a copy for yourself of that which is given to me by God out of *grace*. I acknowledge this to be done out of thankfulness and obedience toward God, and in that regard, I also willingly accept it.

<margin>* NOTE.</margin>
3. And I exhort you as a brother in Christ to proceed according to the course you have begun. Strive as a *constant soldier* against your own outward reason in flesh and blood, and also against the Devil and the *hypocritical*, flattering, evil world. Do so with firm trust and confidence in God, with a zealous spirit and *mind*, in a still, quiet life. In this way, you may obtain the noble crown or garland of victory, which indeed assists a young fellow-companion who fears God and is very acceptable in the presence of God and his angels. If this crown is once set upon you, you will clearly discern *what God IS and what he CAN do*.

<margin>† Luke 17:21</margin>
4. And then you will not *much need* to learn from others when the right Teacher is WITHIN you; he who teaches ALL men and confirms to God’s children that which he teaches from or out of man. For † *the kingdom of God is WITHIN man*, if he is born again in Christ.

5. As you will find it sufficiently described in my writings—which did not proceed or spring from conceit <note>original: "conceipt"; meaning personal imagination or whim</note> or opinion, but in such a way as they themselves signify and express: namely, con-

6. I have written this for my own remembrance and meditation, and also for the sake of those whom God will visit or stir up through it, and whom he will also *crown* with this *garland* (as I have been given to know). For this reason, I have written according to the high gifts in the Light of God, and I have suppressed my outward *reason* as if it were folly or a foolish *virgin*. I have not used this to advance my *outward* life or honor, because much scorn and persecution have become my reward, besides whatever else may yet happen to me.

<margin>Genesis 3:15</margin>

We must become wholly † conformable to his *image* <note>The restored image of God in man</note> and come to him only under his purple mantle <note>Refers to Christ’s suffering and royalty, used here as a protective covering of grace</note>. He alone must cover us; otherwise, we are caught in the Devil’s and Antichrist's net, standing quite naked and ashamed before the face of God, just like the Babylonish whore.

<margin>James 1:12</margin>
9. But since God has already opened your heart so that you see with different eyes, it is highly necessary for you to move forward and remain constant. For he who will crown you is already on his way, but you must * endure *affliction* and hold out. Do not give way or room to carnal *reason*, for the Devil vehemently attacks the grain of *mustard seed* sown by the Holy Spirit, seeking to destroy it continually.

10. It is the same with a newborn child of *Christ* as it is with a young, tender tree that is easily destroyed. But once it grows and becomes strong, then it can stand firm. Even if a branch is likely torn off many times by a windstorm, the *trunk* <note>original: "Stock"</note> or body of the tree remains standing and brings forth other branches.

11. But it must be true earnestness that fights with the Devil and overcomes the anger of God. One's own *reason* must drown and kill *itself* and surrender itself to God, so that God might live in the *understanding* of man—that He might be man's will and his action. Otherwise, nothing can be found in divine wisdom. The Spirit of God must only find itself in man, so that the true image may be His work and wonder.

12. For everything that is taught and spoken concerning God,

Anything without the *Spirit of God* is merely *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; referring to the biblical Tower of Babel as a symbol of human confusion, prideful reasoning, and false religious systems</note>, no matter how much it plays the hypocrite or tries to flatter. 16. In the book sent with this one—which was also produced by this "school"—you will find further grounds concerning this author.

The noble Pearl <note>a recurring symbol in Boehme's work for divine wisdom or the Christ-spirit within</note> reveals or manifests itself in those who seek it now; for it is an acceptable time, both in *heaven* and *hell*. Both doors currently stand open with their own desires. It is a time to seek oneself; let no one take this as anything but earnest, or else they will fall back into the fierce, wrathful anger of God and be consumed by the *vengeance* of that fierce wrath.

## The Fourteenth Epistle

### June 21, 1621. To C. B.

->May the open wellspring or fountain in the heart of *Jesus Christ* be our life-giving refreshment.<-

<margin>* On the Three Principles <note>original: "De tribus Principiis"</note>,</margin>
1. My dear Mr. <note>original: "Herr"</note> *Christianus*, and esteemed friend. Your welfare and happiness are always dear to me. I send you with this letter *On the Three Principles*, the book of the **Three Principles**, for you to copy out fully if you wish. I exhort you in the love of Christ, as one member of his body should encourage another, to be diligent in study and prayer to God, so that our faith and knowledge may grow and take root among us, and that we might at last reap the fruit and enjoy it.

2. Only be watchful in Christ to fight against *human reason*, the *world*, and the *will* of the **flesh**. Fight like a valiant *soldier*; your victory is in the Lord’s hands, who will grant it to you when it pleases him.

<margin>* Philippians 3:10–11; Romans 8:29.</margin>
3. The *crown* for which you fight is set aside and kept for you, and you will not regret seeking it. But you must bear the *wound-marks of Christ* in this world and * be conformed to his image; otherwise, you will NOT attain the *crown*. I tell you this in a brotherly manner.

4. Prepare yourself diligently, for a great *storm* is at hand. May you be preserved for the praise of God and for the year of the *lily* which is *blossoming* <note>original: "springeth"</note>. I commit you to the love of Jesus Christ.

I ask you, after you have copied it, to send it back again, for it is in demand; *scholars* have been found to whom it should be lent.

<summary>Boehme concludes his thirteenth letter by emphasizing divine honor over worldly status and begins his fourteenth letter to "C. B.," sending a copy of his book On the Three Principles. He encourages the recipient to remain steadfast through spiritual struggle and impending social turmoil, symbolized by a coming "storm" and the eventual "year of the lily."</summary>

<header>Nineteenth Epistle: The Highest Joy in the Spiritual Philosopher's Stone.</header>

# The Nineteenth Epistle
->July 3, 1622. To Mr.<-
<margin>† Christians.</margin>
->C. B.<-

> May God's grace, salvation, and eternal light be our life-giving refreshment.

->1.<-

Truly honorable and esteemed Sir, my very loving and good friend: Please accept my willing and diligent service at all times, along with my *desire* for your total welfare and happiness.

<margin>* Being <note>original: "Wesen"</note>.</margin>
2. I have received your letter sent to me during Advent and understand your very diligent and Christian *mind* and *desire*. Though I am a stranger to you, I have received sufficient information about your *conduct* <note>original: "Conversation"</note> and character from Mr. Walter’s letter.

3. Furthermore, he informs me of your intense and diligent *longing* in the letter you sent me. Because of this, I am not only willing to welcome you into my circle <note>original: "skill"</note> and friendship, but I rejoice greatly that *a mind such as yours* is born of God. 5. When you attain it, you will have the **highest joy**. Whoever finds it is **richer** than any prince on **earth**; he possesses the **art** and understanding of the entire world, and within him lie hidden **all the powers of heaven and earth**.

## The Twenty-First Epistle

->July 8, 1621.<-
->To C. B.<-

I suggest to you privately that you prepare yourself; for a violent tribulation <note>original: "Tribulation"; likely referring to the escalating conflicts of the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648).</note> will exceedingly seize upon some of our countrymen.

2. But seek diligently to enclose yourself in THAT peace which Christ has brought back to us, and defend yourself with it as if with a wall or fortress.

3. ->Your willing servant,<-
->Jacob Boehme.<-

# Epistle 23: *We must be constant in Christ's warfare.*

## The Twenty-Third Epistle

->October 29, 1621. To <insert>Mr.</insert> C. B.<-

->Emmanuel!<- <note>original: "Emanuel"; a Hebrew name meaning "God is with us," commonly used as a greeting in spiritual correspondence.</note>

1. Honorable, much-beloved, and esteemed friend in *Christ*. I wish for you only and solely what my soul continually wishes and desires from God: namely, the right, *true knowledge* of God in the love of Jesus Christ. <margin>* Revelation 22:16.</margin> May the *bright Morning Star* <note>original: "bright Morning Starre"; a biblical reference to Jesus Christ and the dawning of spiritual enlightenment</note> continually arise within you and shine in you through this vale of *misery* to your eternal joy.

2. And I urge you in the love of *Christ*, out of my sincere good intentions toward you, to go on and remain constant in the way you have begun in Christ's *warfare*. Then, as the little paradisiacal tree or plant sprouts and takes root, you will eventually see its noble or precious fruit and enjoy it eternally. You will find sufficient refreshment there, for even though it is covered for a long time by the earthly field or soil, the noble gold grows without any ceasing at all.

3. I would be very pleased to know how your brother is doing at <margin>† Beuthen.</margin> † *Beuthen* <note>original: "Beuten"; modern Bytom, Poland</note>, to whom you have lent those writings, and what judgment he makes of them. There are other people in Beuthen who also have some of them and exceedingly desire the others. You would do a service to your loving brother and others if you would lend them whatever more they desire; I will shortly send you *some more* which you still lack.

4. <insert>Mr.</insert> *Caspar Lindner*, a customs official <note>original: "Customer"; a collector of customs duties or tolls</note> at Beuthen and a member of the Council, is also a *lover* of these writings. If he desires any of them, you should do well to lend them to him; he is not in the habit of keeping them for *long*.

5. These writings are spread far and wide in many countries, among both the high and the low, and have even become known to highly *learned* people. May God guide this to his honor and glory.

6. I am sending you, along with instructions, *three sacks* for the *corn* that <insert>Mr.</insert> *Rudolf* will send. Please take the trouble to receive it for me. <margin>* Rauscha.</margin> When *Specht* or the other man from *Rauscha* <note>original: "Rausche"; likely the town of Rauscha in Upper Lusatia</note> comes over, if you see him, tell him about it and ask him to pick it up. I will look for him as well and tell him the same; he will bring it to me quite easily. I will return the favor in a friendly manner. I commend you to the love of Jesus Christ. Dated as above.

->Your willingly helpful friend and brother,<-

->*Jacob Boehme.*<-

# The Gospel shall be preached to all Nations. Epistle 26.

## The Twenty-Sixth Epistle
### of April 28, 1622.
### To Mr. C. B. <note>original: "An Herrn C. B."</note>

->May the open fountain in the heart of *Jesus Christ* be our quickening, refreshing, and constant light.<-

1. Honorable and esteemed friend, beloved in Christ: let my faithful wishes for you—of the love and grace of our Savior Christ and all temporal welfare <note>original: "temporall welfare"; referring to physical health and earthly well-being</note>—be presented to you.

2. When I heard from the people mentioned before how much you, sir, are a lover of God and a student of wisdom, I could not refrain from reaching out. Even though I am essentially unknown to you, I seek you with this letter from a true heart and a Christian mind, in order to gain your acquaintance.

3. For it brings joy to my heart when I perceive how God's love works in His children. I rejoice with them and in them in the Tree of Life, *Jesus Christ*, in and from whom we are conceived and born anew, becoming branches or little sprouts in Him.

<margin>* 1 Corinthians 5:3; Colossians 2:5.</margin>
4. Therefore, my mind has stirred me to seek and refresh myself with you, sir, as my fellow member in the spirit and love of Christ. * Though we are absent in person, we are present in the will-spirit <note>original: "will-spirit"; a Böhmean term referring to the core of human intention or the soul's direction</note>, especially in this troublesome time. We are surrounded by enemies on all sides, and our Tree is very weak and withered in many of its branches.

<margin>† Hebrews 3:13. * Revelation 18:4.</margin>
5. But since the Grace-Sun <note>original: "Grace-Sun"; a metaphor for Christ's enlightening and life-giving presence</note>, JESUS CHRIST, is currently shining on us with a bright look, he opens his door of love and high knowledge through many different gifts. Thus, we may know the great wonders of his unsurpassed wisdom. Therefore, we should do well to † exhort one another in love as brothers, * and go out from BABEL <note>original: "BABEL"; representing the confused and corrupt religious institutions of the world</note>, which is ignited in the Anger-Fire <note>original: "Anger-Fire"; in Böhme’s philosophy, this is the harsh, judgmental aspect of God's nature</note> of God. For it is truly a time of great earnestness and severity, wherein we should seek with great sincerity to know ourselves and see where we stand.

6. And yet it is true that one currently sees many glorious, beautiful sprouts in the Tree of CHRIST, even in the midst of God’s fire. I rejoice highly that the Grace-Sun shines forth again in bright clarity, and that God still keeps His faithful promise.

<margin>† Isaiah 49:16. * NOTE</margin>
7. As He says in Isaiah, † He has signed or imprinted us in His hands. In some people today, this reveals itself in power, showing how the fountain of JESUS CHRIST works strongly in them. In a * short time, this will be done even more powerfully, as He has promised.

<header>Out of the agonizing birth the Light arises. Epistle 27</header>

# The Twenty-Seventh Epistle
->June 21, 1622.<-
->To Mr. C. B.<-

->May the open fountain of *Jesus Christ* be our reviving,<-
->refreshing, and constant light.<-

<margin>1.</margin>
My very worthy and loving friend, I wish you and yours, and all the children of *Christ* in the kingdom of our *angelic* fraternity, God’s love and blessing. May the fountain of *Christ* in us spring up, grow, and bear much fruit; it is in this sprouting that our true regeneration consists. I hope assuredly in God—as indeed has been shown to me—that the time is NEAR at hand when it will clearly sprout, a fact in which I rejoice.

2. And though at present I see the fire burning in *Babel* <note>original: "Babell." For Böhme, Babel represents the confusion and corruption of the institutionalized, divided churches of his day.</note>, yet out of the FIRE will emerge a clear, shining light which will drive away the dark night; however, THAT will be generated through a great, agonizing birth <note>original: "anxious birth." In Böhme's thought, *Angst* (anxiety or agony) is the necessary state of contraction and tension from which the Light is born.</note>.

3. I urge my loving brothers to surrender themselves to that agonizing birth or generation <note>original: "Geniture."</note>, so that they may also sprout forth in the life of God, in the *Light*, and not be overtaken by the *Turba* <term>A Latin term used by Böhme to describe the "turmoil" or "disturbing element" in nature and the soul that leads to destruction and divine wrath.</term>. At present, the *Turba* abominably spreads itself abroad with its properties—namely, *covetousness*, *envy*, *anger*, and *pride*—and the *fruits* that grow out from these; it powerfully draws its fire to itself, by which they clearly burn in many places.

4. At the request and entreaty of others, I have written a *little* book on *repentance*, together with a form of prayer. It is all very earnest, and serves as a right beginning and entrance into the *Theosophical* school <note>The "Theosophick School" refers to Böhme’s specific mystical-philosophical study of the nature of God and creation.</note>. Upon request, I am sending it herewith to *Mr. R. B. G.* at *Weicha* <margin>Weicha.</margin>. I entreat you to send it to him; you may please open it, and if you wish, you may also quickly write a copy of it for yourself, provided that the letter to *Mr. R.* remains sealed.

5. I ask that you do not, if possible, keep it for more than three or four days, as it is *small* and may be quickly copied out and sent on to *Mr. R.*

6. Also, your brother is not to be forgotten, for without doubt it will be acceptable to him and be a true KEY; I wish as much good for him, according to my greetings, as I do for my own life.

# XXVII. Epistle: *Out of the agonizing birth the Light arises:*

7. If you would enter into the *practice* of this book, you would soon *experience* its benefit. For it is generated out of an agonizing branch <note>original: "anxious Twig." In Böhme’s thought, "anxious" or "agonizing" refers to the state of tension and constriction from which spiritual light is born.</note> through fire; it was and is my very own process or path, *by which* I have attained the PEARL of divine knowledge.

8. And though I must live in weakness or human frailty like other men, yet this *Pearl* is more precious to me than all the world’s goods. For its sake, I willingly suffer and endure everything, so long as I may keep it.

<margin>Sagan</margin>
9. I am writing to inform you that *Mr. D. A. B. M.* at Sagan <note>Now Żagań, Poland.</note> has written to me for the *third* time. He has requested my friendship and earnestly entreated me to lend him some of these writings.

10. Although I have almost none of my own writings here at home, I would like to provide him with something to copy out; we shall see whether it might serve God’s honor. However, if you *notice* that he only intends to find *fault* with them, or to pry into them with a critical eye—though I hope that is not the case—then you will know better how to proceed.

<margin>* Galatians 6:7</margin>
11. Build and grow, as you have received growth from *divine grace*; you will surely * reap what you have sown.

12. As soon as you can, send him the letter I have written to him, along with a treatise that you have transcribed <note>original: "of your writing."</note>. Tell him that he should not keep it for a long time, as some people do.

13. I truly respect him, but we must see what God will do. With the "Book of Repentance" sent with this letter, you may also find growth once you have copied it; for it offers a great *harvest*, and no one will be much against it, provided he is a human being and *not* a *beast*. Thus, I commend you to the gentle love of JESUS CHRIST. Dated as above.

->Your willing servant and brother,<-

->**Jacob Böhme.**<-

<header>We must put on Christ. Epistle: 31.</header>

## The Thirty-First Epistle

->November 12, 1622.<-
->To Mr. C. B.<-
->V. H. I. L. I. C.<-
<note>original: "V. H. I. L. I. C." is an abbreviation for the German phrase "Unser Heil im Leben Jesu Christi," which the author translates in the next line.</note>
->Our Salvation is in the Life of *Jesus Christ* .<-

1. My very loving Sir and worthy friend, I wish you much joy in the power of the divine vision, and the ability to find and perceive God <note>original: "Inventibility and Perceptibility"</note>; together with bodily welfare. I rejoice at your steadfastness in divine exercise, which to me is a mark of our eternal brotherhood <note>original: "Fraternity"</note> in the divine essence. I exhort you in love to remain in earnest steadfastness and to wait for the eternal wages. Only do not turn toward worldly scorn and apish mimicry <note>original: "Apish-Mimick works"</note> or mere imitation.

<margin>* Romans 13:14; Galatians 3:27.</margin>
2. For a true Christian must not only be a mouth-only or verbal Christian, but must walk in Christ—in his way or process—and *put on Christ*. I hope this is clearly done by you; only do not put on the Devil's flattering or hypocritical worldly mask <term>original: "Vizard"; a mask or disguise, often used to imply deception.</term>. For the time is short, after which the eternal wages follow. Please greet your brothers and fellow-brethren in the Lord on my behalf.

3. I am sending you here *two sacks*, and I pray you to take the pains to fill them with grain <note>original: "Corn"; in this period, "corn" referred to any cereal grain like wheat or rye, rather than maize.</note>. Take notice of them and seal them a little. Inside the sack is a packet for Mr. Rudolph von Gersdorf and Mr. Frederick von Kregwitz. This should only be sent to Mr. von Gersdorf; he will send Mr. von Kregwitz’s part well enough. But please take the trouble to convey it to Mr. von Gersdorf. If you cannot find a messenger to your liking, then send it by a messenger specifically for this purpose; he will be well paid by von Gersdorf. If he is not, I will pay him myself.

4. Please make up the pack again, for I have left it unsealed for you. There is a treatise <note>A formal written work or essay.</note> attached to each letter which will be useful for you. You would do well to copy them out as soon as it is convenient, and then speedily, without further delay, send them to the place mentioned before.

5. But please pack each treatise with its own specific letter and seal that by itself, so that each treatise is not separated from its intended letter.

7. Regarding the *List of Books* from Mr. Lindener at Beuthen, I answer that those *mentioned books* are all mine; they were all written half a year ago, and some of them this summer. The one you have now received from Gersdorff's is a work against the *Methists* <note>original: "Methists"; followers of the sectarian Ezekiel Meths.</note>. Here in Kregwitz's writing, you may also find one on true *Resignation*. The others are partly large works, especially the book *The Signature of All Things* <note>original: "de signatura Rerum"</note>, which concerns the origin of the creation and its form or impression <term>original: "impresse"; the outward mark or signature that reveals an object's inner nature.</term>. It is a very profound work of forty-one sheets <note>A "sheet" in this context refers to a large piece of paper that, when folded, created several pages of a book.</note> which has been copied out several times.

<margin>
Brux
Troppau
</margin>
8. Doctor Brux also has one, and Doctor Gyller of Troppau <note>original: "Troppen"</note> has one. When I have gotten them back into my hands, I will continue to send them to you one after another. Just let me know when you have time to write. If you wish to copy those you have now received from Gersdorff, you may do so; however, first copy the two I am sending with this letter and send them away. Then, send Mr. Gersdorff's manuscript back to me along with the shipment of grain.

<margin>
Litoměřice
Bohemia
Leipa
Lusatia

9. Concerning the *Cossacks*: I inform you that they are stationed in Litoměřice <note>original: "Leuten-meritz"</note> in Bohemia, extending as far as Leipa <note>original: "Lippe"</note>, and they are greatly wasting the country. It is said they are to pass by us and go toward Poland.

10. But we have no certain news. I suspect they will remain in Bohemia or Lusatia and not see Poland at all, for we shall shortly have "new times." The current peace is not stable, for the "sickness is unto death" <note>A biblical allusion suggesting the social and political order is beyond recovery.</note> and was never greater, as time will soon reveal.

11. I would very much like to know how you are and what your condition is. If you had written to tell me what I owe you, I would have sent the payment. I know well enough, Sir, that you will have the opportunity to copy these works. I commend you to the love of JESUS CHRIST.

->Jacob Böhme.<-

<header>Prepare for Tribulation. Epistle XXXIV.</header>

## The Thirty-Fourth Epistle

->December 13, 1622<-

->To Mr. C. B.<-

->Our Salvation is in the Life of *Jesus Christ*<-

1. 
My very loving and worthy sir, and good friend: I wish you God’s rich grace in both *temporal* and *eternal* ***salvation!*** I am writing to inform you that I have safely received your letter.

2. I also rejoice at your constant divine mindset, which I hope in God still grows and increases more and more in divine knowledge. In this knowledge, sir, you are bound up in the bond of the living God and may be defended in *this great tribulation*, which has now begun.

3. Now is the time to earnestly shelter ourselves in the fountain of life, JESUS CHRIST; for the *sword* of God’s anger will cut mightily and be set against both body and soul.

4. Therefore, we would do well to banish the *Antichrist*, the *Beast*, and the *Whore* <note>Böhme uses these apocalyptic figures from the Book of Revelation to represent corruption within the self and the institutional church.</note> out of the HEART; for they shall and must fall. But in whomever they are still found, the Confusion <note>original: "Turba"; a term Böhme uses to describe the spirit of divine wrath, disorder, or the source of destruction.</note> will carry those people away with them.

5. *Next spring*, I intend—if God permits and grants us enough *peace* and quiet—to see you personally and provide a little of what is necessary, along with other good friends and brothers in *Christ*. I faithfully exhort you to *prepare for tribulation*, for it cannot be otherwise; it is near and proceeds mightily in the Great Confusion <note>original: "Turba Magna"; Latin for 'the Great Turba' or 'Great Confusion,' referring to the apocalyptic upheaval and war Böhme saw breaking out.</note>.

6. This difficult <note>original: "dear"; in this context meaning expensive or high-priced due to famine.</note> time of scarcity will become even greater and lead to great *necessity*. Everyone should apply themselves to earnest sincerity. Great wars, uprisings, insurrections, calamity, and death will fall upon us mightily in a *short* time.

I inform you of this, sir, based on my knowledge, for your brotherly consideration.

7. But if you have any desire to read my writings, you may obtain them from *Dr. Gersdorff*. I have written to him about

### The Fortieth Epistle

->To Mr. **C. B.**<-
->October 18, 1623.<-

->O.S.I.T.L.O.J.C.I.U. <note>original initials: "V. H. I. L. I. C. I. V."</note><-

->Our salvation is in the life of Jesus Christ in us! <note>original German: "Unser Heil Im Leben Jesu Christi In Uns!"</note><-

#### 1.

<margin>* Colossians 3:16</margin>
Very loving sir and Christian brother: I wish you the working power of God, so that the fountain in the *life* of JESUS CHRIST may well up in you *richly*, and that your soul may continually be satisfied and refreshed in it. May you drink of this holy water and in it grow, sprout, and bear much good fruit—as well as enjoy bodily welfare!

2. And I rejoice at your happy condition, and that God has restored your house and family to *health* again—praised be God. I am glad that you are still in health and acknowledge God's work in my *talent* <note>Böhme refers to his spiritual insights and writings as his "talent," a reference to the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25.</note>. For God has more and more opened his door of grace to me—and not only to ME, but also to many OTHERS who get to read these writings, whose hearts God has touched. They have entered into repentance and conversion (or amendment of life), and they have come to the *inward* divine vision within themselves. They desire to cast away the *garment* of sins and impurity, and to follow CHRIST in *life* and *will*.

<header>One accounted himself as dung in the presence of God. Epistle 40.</header>

3. As indeed a few days ago, such a spiritual movement <note>original: "Motion"</note> of two people was presented to me. These individuals are high-ranking in the world and previously loved worldly things. In them, I saw the new birth <note>The "New Birth" is Böhme's term for spiritual regeneration or being "born again" in the Spirit.</note> in great power and in the triumph of **divine knowledge**, expressed with such deep humility that I never saw the like since my very childhood—except for what God has worked in my own poor self. This would not have been possible for me to believe if I had not found it by experience and had the same myself.

4. One of them despised himself regarding his earthly, worldly matters and looked down on his former way of life <note>original: "conversation"</note>. He also sank so deeply into resignation <note>Resignation (Gelassenheit) is a core Böhme concept meaning the total surrender of one's own will to the will of God.</note> and into repentance that he accounted himself **too unworthy** to offer his prayers before God. Instead, he esteemed himself as dead and altogether unworthy, and threw himself into God's **mercy**, letting Him do with him and through him whatever He would, so that he would pray and repent through Him.

GOD <note>original German: "GOTT"</note>.
† DUNG <note>original German: "KOHT"</note>
or filthy rottenness.

5. Upon this, the divine **sun** instantly shone within him, and through his mouth for **three** hours he spoke nothing else but these words: \* **GOD**, † **Dung**; **GOD**, **DUNG**. He accounted **himself** as **dung** *in the presence of God*. In this expression—<gloss>To God I am but dung</gloss>—the divine sun of joyfulness and great knowledge arose, and it wholly moved and renewed his heart and mind.

6. Afterward, he and *another man in the same condition* came to me. After I had seen that spiritual movement in him, he rejoiced greatly with me that they were brought to it through my *Book of Repentance* <note>Böhme refers to his treatise "On True Repentance," often included in his collection *The Way to Christ*.</note>.

7. Indeed, in a short time many more people were seen in the same condition, which I perceived with great wonder. I saw how the door of grace so mightily moved and opened itself to those who are earnest, just as it had been shown to me a long time ago. Dear sir and brother, I tell and show this to you in certain truth and in the presence of God, seeing that you are one of the *first fruits* of those to whose hands this talent <note>Böhme refers to his spiritual insights and writings as his "talent," referencing the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25.</note> has come through divine appointment.

8. You have also received it with joy and have taken great pains with it. Though you do not long for such an experience as mentioned above concerning those **two people**, nor labor for it so that you might receive it from God—which, if you did, would be a great joy to my spirit—yet indeed a person should not intend to receive from God according to his **own** will, but only sink down into God's **will**, just like the aforementioned people;

<header>The world's Enmity our Exaltation in Christ. XLIII. Epistle</header>

# The Forty-Third Epistle

->To **Mr.** G. B.<-

->December 27, 1623.<-

->Our salvation is in the life of **Jesus Christ** within us.<-

1.
Dearly beloved Sir *Christianus* <note>likely a pseudonym or spiritual title meaning "a Christian"</note>; after wishing you the divine **working of love**! I would gladly know how your condition is with you, and whether you are still assaulted by the *Pharisaical* <term>Pharisaical: hypocritically self-righteous or legalistic, referring here to rigid religious authorities</term> venom or poison. Its **fire** is near, in which it shall be **transmuted** <term>transmuted: transformed or changed in nature, often an alchemical term</term> or changed; we wait for this in *divine patience*. For I perceive that very poison in *Babel* <note>original: "Babell"; Böhme used this to describe the confused and corrupt state of the established churches</note> will burn intensely against you and me.

2. But on the contrary, I have also seen the great **Love-Fire** kindled in some, so that I know certainly that the time of the divine visitation <term>divine visitation: a time when God intervenes in human affairs for either judgment or blessing</term> is NEAR and clearly at hand. You, together with me and other children of **CHRIST**, should endure in **patience** until the anger of God overthrows the evil beast, together with the *Whore* <note>A reference to the "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, symbolizing spiritual corruption</note>.

3. As children of Christ, we ought to suffer with Christ, and through suffering be made conformable to His image. Only do not let it seem strange to you if the world hates you and is fiercely enraged with you; it must be so. The world's enmity <term>enmity: active opposition or hostility</term> is our exaltation in **CHRIST**, for we are strange guests in the world, wandering the pilgrim's path back into our Father's native country! I commit you to the love of **JESUS CHRIST**! Dated as above.

->Yours in the well-known love of **Jesus Christ**,<-

->*Jacob Böhme.* <note>original: "Jacob Behme"</note><-

He reminds the reader that the world's hatred is a sign of their true home in Christ and urges patience until divine justice prevails.</summary>

...in which he would have placed me, if God had not hindered it through some honest hearts to whom our way is better known.

5. For the Superintendent—or Chief Pharisee, namely the *Primate*—has raged so vehemently against my printed book as if his own son had been murdered and all his goods burned. He has vomited out such a heap of lies against me, along with such shameful attacks on my reputation, as can be read in his public *lampooning* <note>original: "Pasquill"; a lampoon or satirical attack</note> pamphlet or libel, which I have sent with this letter.

6. He has not only spread such shameful lies and scandal from the *pulpit*, but has also written about it to *Liegnitz* to the pastor named *Prisius*. He asked him not only to proclaim it from the *pulpit* (which he did), but to have it *printed*. He also urged him to complain about it to the *City Council* at *Görlitz* and to present it in *such a way* that it appeared to be the complaint of ALL the *priests* in the *district of Liegnitz* <term>original: "Weichbild Lignitz"; Weichbild refers to a municipal area or district</term> against my writings—especially against my printed little book.

7. *Prisius* did this, and at the desire of our *Primate*, he misrepresented me to a counselor at *Görlitz* with a *lying letter*.

8. Following this, our *Primate* went frequently to the highest *lords* of our city. He raged against me with such vehement lies and shouted against me, demanding that as soon as I returned home, they should put me into *prison* and then banish me from the city. He also submitted such a lying complaint to the Council, and even "set hell on fire" against me and "prepared the lake" <note>likely a reference to the "lake of fire" from the Book of Revelation</note>.

9. However, because *most* of the *lords* of the Council had read my little printed book and found *nothing* unchristian *in it*—in fact, it was very much liked and loved by some of them, as well as by many of the *citizens* <term>original: "Burgers"</term>—many of them considered the *Primate's* proposal and desire to be unfair <term>original: "unequall"</term>. They believed there was no just cause for such persecution of me, and they spoke against it, saying that THIS religion was NOT *new*, but was the very BASIS <term>original: "ground"</term> of the ancient holy Fathers, whose writings contain many more books like it.

10. But some, especially those whom the *Primate* had instigated, thought it best to summon me and compel me to appear before a Council. I was to see whether the Emperor or the Prince-*Elector* <note>The Elector of Saxony, who ruled Görlitz at the time</note> would not be stirred up by the *priests* to allow them to arrest me. Just as it happened, when I came before the Council, they said this to me: they ordered me to *step aside for a moment* so that they would not be troubled or disturbed by me.

<margin>* Jacob Böhme's answer to Gregory Richter.</margin>

11. Upon this, I had prepared my *answer in writing* and would have—

<header>One of the Primate's retinue derided the Holy Spirit. Epistle XLVI.</header>

...[I] would have delivered it to *them*; but the *Primate* <note>original: "Primarius"; the chief pastor or ecclesiastical head of the city, Gregory Richter</note> hindered it, so that they would not receive any *answer* from me in writing, for he feared that HE would be forced to *answer* for his *lies*.

12. And so it was not received by the *Council*, but I was only warned to go away for a while to live with some people who would *host* <note>original: "entertaine"</note> me, and so submit to them so that they might be at peace. However, no official command was laid upon me.

13. To this I answered that since *men* would not hear my *answer* so that I might declare my *innocence*, and since I could be admitted to no *defense* against the *Primate's* complaints and unjust *slanders*, I must commit the matter to God. I must see whether God would bring me somewhere to honest, good people and finally shelter me so that I might at last escape the *Primate's* sight.

14. This was acceptable to *them*, but they gave NO command that I should or must be gone; they only advised <note>original: "admonished"</note> me to do so.

15. Whereupon I went home from the *Council*. There, at the *Council door* in the outer *porch*, some spiteful mockers from the *Primate's* retinue—perhaps sent by him—stood and insulted me. One of them, a wicked *buffoon* <term>original: "Buffoone"; a low jester or person given to ridiculing others</term>, "anatomized" <note>meaning he picked apart Böhme's appearance and character with insults</note> me from the *crown* of my head to the sole of my foot regarding my *clothes* and *gifts*. He also vehemently *attacked* the *Holy Spirit* and mocked IT; at last, he also said:

### That eventually the Holy Spirit 
### would be as common as pieces of leather 
### at the tanner's <note>original: "Skinners"; those who prepare skins or hides</note>.

16. Thus this came to an end. The *Primate* then caused this *lampoon* <note>original: "Pasquill"; a satirical public attack</note> or *libel* to be printed; and now I must immediately stand under the *cross* of CHRIST. Let God order it according to His *counsel*!

17. I beg you, sir, to let me know your *thoughts* <note>original: "pleasure"</note> on this and to communicate them to me. I suffer it all with patience, but my *children* will be shamefully discredited by it. Yet this must happen so that the measure of iniquity may be full <note>a biblical idiom suggesting that a situation must reach its worst point before divine judgment occurs</note> and the punishment come.

# The Forty-Ninth Epistle

### Our Salvation is in Christ.

<margin>* Dresden. † Castle <note>original: "Schloße"</note>.</margin>

No one can say anything disgraceful about us except for one wicked man <note>referring to Gregor Richter, the primary pastor of Görlitz and Böhme's chief antagonist</note>, who slanders us and persecutes us for Christ’s sake. # The Fifty-Third Epistle

## Of May 19, 1624.
<note>The original text says 1623, but based on the context of Böhme's travel to Dresden and the publication of his "printed book" (The Way to Christ), the actual year was 1624.</note>

->To Mr. T. K.<-

->O. S. I. T. L. O. J. C. I. U.<-

->Our Salvation In the Life of Jesus Christ In Us.<-

My very loving Sir and Christian Brother: after my faithful, hearty, and brotherly <note>original: "memberlike"</note> wish for the continually enduring power of Love, so that our soul may *always* draw and drink from the fountain of Christ.

<margin>Dresden</margin>
2. If things are going well with you and your family, and our dear friends, as well as with my *wife*, it will be pleasing to me. As for *me*, I thank God, who has wonderfully guided me according to His good pleasure. I arrived in *Dresden* in good health in the *middle* of the week before Christ's *Ascension* <note>The feast day celebrating Jesus's ascent into heaven, 40 days after Easter.</note>, together with *Mr. Melchior Bernten*. I am staying with *Mr. Benedict H.*, where I am receiving all Christian love and friendship; I am being well hosted, and we have many good conversations <note>original: "Converse"</note>.

3. And among the *Prince Elector’s Council* <note>The high-ranking advisors to the Elector of Saxony, one of the most powerful rulers in the Holy Roman Empire.</note>, and indeed the highest-ranking of them, there are very loving Christian gentlemen who find this *theosophical foundation* <note>original: "Theosophick Ground"; Böhme's mystical philosophical system.</note> very agreeable; they also read and love my writings. For my *printed book* <note>The Way to Christ, published in late 1623/early 1624.</note> has already reached the hands of *many officials* and other *learned men*. I consider all of this to be good and a gift from God. They are working and planning how such good writings—which lead people to the <margin>* Matthew 10:38 and 16:24. Mark 8:34. Luke 9:23.</margin> * following of Christ—may be published, and they will help to promote them and *not* suppress them, as is being done in my home country <note>Görlitz, where Böhme faced persecution.</note> out of personal hatred toward me. May God have mercy and help.

4. And the *Primate’s* <note>Referring to Gregor Richter, the head pastor of Görlitz and Böhme’s primary antagonist.</note> slanderous pamphlet <note>original: "Libell"</note> is viewed with great wonder by the Council and the learned. Some suppose that a malicious, evil, and spiteful spirit dictated it to him. He is even despised by the priests here, who say that he oversteps and goes beyond the bounds of his *office*. For *Mr. Henckel* has shown it to the Council.

Although I can get no hearing in Görlitz—which seems amazing to these Lords, that a citizen would not be allowed to take notice of a legal case—yet I will not make any complaint against my Lords at Görlitz without further cause.

But because it troubles the Primate <note>Gregory Richter, the chief clergyman of Görlitz and Böhme's primary antagonist.</note> that I have answered him in writing, and because he will fly into a rage <note>original: "flye aloft"</note> and insult me even more, I say this: if he is not satisfied with the written answer, I will send it to the printing press, as many learned people have encouraged me to do. I have a good reason for it; it would be better for him to stop his slandering, otherwise he will see and hear things that will not please him.

11. Though indeed I take no pleasure in **THAT**, for I see very well that the Devil would love to sully and defile my talent with **contention** and **dispute**; but I hope to stand under divine protection and defense. I now powerfully experience how God leads and protects His children; therefore, HE is to be praised.

12. And it will not be possible for the Primate to drive away all those people from Görlitz who read my little book; for then he would also have to come to Dresden and many other places to drive away the Prince-Elector’s council and priests. But let him be careful that God’s anger does not drive him into the hellish fire <image-desc>triangle symbol pointing upwards</image-desc>; it would be good for him to repent.

13. But if he intends to begin a "reformation," then the Prince-Elector will also look into what manner of reformation he is conducting in his country. You do not need to be afraid of him; it is only a Pharisaic <note>term: hypocritical or legalistic zeal, like that of the biblical Pharisees</note> zeal without any real foundation.

<margin>
Meissen
Saxony
Thuringia
Sea-Cities <note>original: *See-Stadten*</note>
</margin>
14. I still hope that the *Time of the Great Reformation* will suddenly come, when men will be commanded to reform and to teach Christ, and not "shoemaker's pitch and blacking" <note>Richter frequently mocked Böhme's former trade as a shoemaker to suggest he was too uneducated to write on theology.</note>, and to stop insulting the children of Christ. Let him just come to the bookstores in Dresden; he will see the *New Reformation* clearly enough, which matches my own foundation regarding theological matters. I hear no one insulting it here, for it is read with joy. Even the *Superintendent* <note>The chief ecclesiastical official of the district.</note> himself and *Doctor Höe* now teach about the *New Birth* and the *Inward Man*. The Primate of Görlitz might try to forbid it to them—as well as to many others in Meissen, Saxony, Thuringia, and the sea-cities who write and teach about it correctly. If our Primate wants to hinder **THAT**, he would need time to convene a council and take the reformation upon himself; otherwise, they will ALL be "Enthusiasts" <note>term: *Enthusiasts* was a derogatory label used by the orthodox church for those who claimed direct, internal divine inspiration.</note> as he calls them.

# The Sixty-First Epistle

->To Mr. **C. B.**, without date.<-

->*Emmanuel!* <note>original: "Emanuel"; Hebrew for "God with us," a common greeting for Böhme.</note><-

**M**ost honorable, highly esteemed Sir and faithful friend: Your salvation and welfare are very welcome to me. I would have visited you with a *letter* long ago, for I also long to understand your condition, seeing that you devote yourself to the study of **WISDOM**. This is more dear to me than the *whole world*, and I wish that I might once *confer* with you about it, as it is necessary. As I hope to make a journey toward you shortly, I will speak with you then.

2. Hitherto I have been hindered by God's permission, for these **six weeks** I have been cast down by the sickness caused by the evil-raised soldiers <note>This likely refers to the physical and social distress caused by the military presence during the Thirty Years' War, which Böhme often linked to "evil" or "wrathful" spiritual influences.</note>, and I have scarcely regained my health.

<margin>Take note of this.</margin>
3. Also, if you know anything of our Dr. *Walther* <note>original: "Waltern"; referring to Balthasar Walther, a physician and close associate of Böhme.</note>, or where he is, please inform me. Let me know also how you proceed in your study, and whether the Door of Grace is opened further to you to apprehend the high Divine Mystery. It would be very welcome to me to know this; for I hope that if you order your life accordingly and put the *practice* into *exercise*, that door would be opened to you, so that you would see with right or true *magical* eyes into *Divine Magic* <note>original: "Magiam Divinam." In Böhme's terminology, "Magic" refers to the spiritual power of the will and the creative desire of God, not common sorcery.</note>.

<margin>* 1 Corinthians 2:10.</margin>
4. For as soon as the sprout of the **New Man** <note>The "New Man" refers to the regenerate or spiritual self in Christian theology.</note> springs forth, it has its own vision or sight. For just as the outward man sees this outward world, so also the **New Man** sees the *divine world* in which he dwells; for it is written: *The Spirit of man in the Spirit of Christ searches all things, even the depths of the Deity.*

5. And although this does not lie in *searching* and flying high if men try to search by **Reason**, it lies instead in a humble, lowly submission—to enter into it so that the soul desires nothing but *God's Love*. Now, when the soul attains **THAT**, it suddenly brings the richly joyful Spirit of God (the soul's image or the similitude of God) into the heavenly divine *school* of noble and precious knowledge; where then it

<meta>This page continues the 61st Epistle. Böhme is explaining that spiritual knowledge is not something a human achieves through intellectual "Reason," but something granted by God when the human "will-spirit" unites with the Divine.</meta>

<page-num>27</page-num>
<header>J. B. is sick. We are not to search for Divine Things in Reason. Epistle 61.</header>

...is taught more than in the school of this world; for it studies in the school of **Divine Wisdom**. The **Holy Spirit** is its schoolmaster, as well as its knowledge and understanding.

6. It is not a true knowledge of God when a **CREATURE** merely knows or feels God through its own effort; rather, it is **THAT** knowledge alone which exists **IN** God. Just as a twig draws the sap of the tree into itself, if a person does not enter into God with their "will-spirit" <note>the part of the human spirit that directs the will toward the divine</note> but instead stays in outward reason, then they are **BLIND** to **God**.

7. But if they earnestly desire God, then they become pregnant with God’s substance through that desire. God’s substance is then given to them as their **OWN** property <note>original: "propriety"; meaning a personal possession or inherent quality</note>, where the Spirit of God rules; and they become God’s child—namely, a twig on the Tree.

<margin>† Proverbs 16:6</margin>
8. Since I see from *Mr. Walther* <note>Balthasar Walther, a friend and traveling companion of Böhme.</note> that you lead your life in † *The Fear of God*, and he has also shown me your writings which reveal your desire for **Divine Wisdom** and the fountain of **Christ**, I am all the more encouraged to write to you and inform you of the **WAY** to find it. It brings me pure joy when I recognize any of God’s children.

9. Just as one twig of a tree enjoys the presence of another twig through their lovely shared essence, so do the children of **Christ**. If anything in my writings is misunderstood, simply let me know, and I will explain it more clearly for you. If it seems too deep for your mind or thoughts, I would set it down more simply and like a child, so that the "pearl" <note>A reference to the "pearl of great price" from Matthew 13:45-46, representing spiritual truth.</note> might be sought and found *with delight*; for it is not given in vain.

10. But seeing you are one of the *first* whom God will favor with it, I exhort you in true Christian love to diligently seek the *Noble Jewel*. You will certainly attain it, even if it seems at times that you will not. Do not let **THAT** discourage you, and do not shrink back, but stand firm. If anyone wishes to be a soldier, they must fight; often where God is *closest* of all, He does not reveal Himself immediately, for His children must be tested or *tried*.

<margin>Take note of this</margin>
11. We must enter into combat against the "Old **Adam**" <note>A theological term for the fallen, sinful nature of humanity inherited from Adam.</note> and kill that nature if a "New Man" is to grow out of him. If the beautiful crown or garland is once placed upon you, you will no longer need to go searching for it; you will have one within you who searches well enough, who will seek and find Himself **IN** you. Then you shall see God and the **Kingdom of Heaven** through that **glimpse** or discovery. I felt I must share this with you in friendship.

2. The earthly Adam <note>The "old Adam" refers to human nature in its fallen, physical state.</note> is a covering over it, so that Christ cannot be fully manifested in this earthly tabernacle; for holy † David, the man of God, says: *Those who go out sowing in tears shall reap in joy.*

3. I exhort you as a brother not to be discouraged, even if the sun of rich joyfulness does not shine in the old *Adam*. It is God’s will that it should be so; for that richly joyful gleam or those lustrous *beams* do *not belong to the earthly man*. Instead, it frequently gives itself to the *dead mystery, which faded away in Adam* <note>original: "Dead Mystery"; referring to the divine spark or image of God that was lost or hidden after the Fall.</note> and at the *Last Judgment Day shall* * arise in power. Such a friendly glimpse or expression is for the comfort of the poor soul and the strengthening of the *new sprout* <note>The "new sprout" is Böhme’s term for the beginning of spiritual regeneration.</note>. But here, it must be generated or born in mere longing and anxious desire. The sun often hides itself, but it does so only to seek into the *root*, so that it may produce a branch from the tree.

4. Wrestle cheerfully; the crown or garland is surely placed within you, and it will certainly be set upon you according to the measure that pleases God. For according to how he *will use* anyone in this world, he also manifests himself in that person's outward *man* in that same measure. But the true lily-branch <note>The "lily" is Böhme’s signature symbol for the flourishing of the Spirit and the coming age of spiritual peace.</note> does not stand in the outward world. It is an exceeding joy to me when I perceive that you long anxiously after the lily and think you do not have it; but I see much better than you *what* you *have*. This often delights me, and thus I use my exhortation to *awaken* and *stir it up*, so that the tree may grow and become great; for I would also gladly NOW partake of its *fruits*. For this reason, I labor toward YOU and *many* OTHERS, according as I am driven.

<margin>† Jacob Böhme’s little book, "The Two Testaments: Of Baptism and the Supper."</margin>
