I have in Jakob Böhme’s <note>original: "Jacob Behme's"</note> **own handwriting** a letter of his in German <note>original: "High-Dutch"</note> which was sent to me by Michael Le Blon, the Resident for the Queen of Sweden in Holland, serving with the States-General there, on April 12/20, 1650. This letter by Böhme was received by Le Blon from Abraham von Frankenberg, who was then staying with Mr. Beyerlands <note>Dirck Gerritsz Breyerland, a major collector and publisher of Böhme's works.</note> in Amsterdam. Böhme wrote to Frankenberg during his lifetime and conversed with him often; Frankenberg was a learned man, well-acquainted with the divine mysteries of the Holy Scriptures and other profound literature. I am also translating this letter into English and inserting it here.

Böhme used to put this mark on the back of his letters, as it appears in the letter I have:

# Jakob Böhme’s handwriting, or Manuscript Epistle in German <note>original: "High-Dutch"</note>; John Sparrow’s in English
## The Letter follows in German, in Jakob Böhme’s <note>original: "J. B’s."</note> own handwriting.

->OOO<-

> ->Light, Brightness <note>original German: "Hell"</note>, and Eternal Power from the<-
> ->Fountain of the Heart of Jesus Christ<-
> ->be our refreshment <note>original German: "erquickung"</note>.<-
>
> Honorable and well-named Sir, my willing services are always at your disposal. I am writing to let you know that I have been somewhat delayed with the promised writings which I intended to send you to copy, for they have also been copied by a lover of them. But because Mr. Balthasar Walther <note>original: "H. Baltzer W."</note> has returned to the country, he now has them under his own pen. However, if you desire to have something from them to copy, something shall be provided to you as soon as possible. I commend you to Divine protection. Dated at Görlitz <note>original: "Gerlitz"</note>.
>
> Jakob Böhme.

## Translated into English, written in John Sparrow’s <note>original: "J. S’s."</note> own handwriting.

->OOO<-

> ->Light, Salvation, and Eternal Power out of the<-
> ->Fountain of the heart of Jesus Christ, be<-
> ->our Refreshing.<-
>
> *Honorable worthy Sir, let my willing service be always presented to you. I must acquaint you that I have been somewhat hindered in the writings I promised you, which I was to send you to copy out; for they have been lately copied out by a lover of them. But seeing Balthasar Walther <note>original: "H. Baltzer Walter"</note> has come into this country again, he has them now himself in hand, under his pen; but if you have a mind to have any of them and to copy them out, as soon as is possible some of them shall be sent. So I commend you to the Divine Protection.*
>
> ->Dated at Görlitz<-
>
> Jakob Böhme.

John Sparrow.

## The Third Epistle.

->October 24, in the year <note>original Latin: "Anno"</note> 1619.<-

->1.<-

I present you my salutations through and from *God*, wishing you the light of the divine kingdom of joy in our *Immanuel* <note>original: "Emanuel"</note>.

<margin>* The Three Principles <note>Referring to Böhme’s work *Aurora*, which outlines three principles of divine essence.</note></margin>
2. I have safely received the *letter* you sent me, along with my writings, directly from *Zeigern*. As soon as I had sealed those writings, I sent them to H. N. by way of N. N., who was with me at that time. I felt I must send him this letter, since it was already sealed and provided with my *writings* enclosed within it. But now I understand in my mind—seeing that things have happened as they have—that your request for *them* may be an act of God's providence. Therefore, I am sending them to you *herewith*. Please consider them; there is a very noble jewel within them, which God has bestowed since your departure. I also inform you that a very lovely gate has sprung open, into which we will *enter* if it is God's will (as it highly appears to be). Regarding this, I cannot say anything yet, for it does not belong to my *outward* man. But just as all vegetation or plants of the earth rejoice when the *sun* rises and shines upon them with its power and virtue, so also my soul rejoices in the fair **Wonder-Blossom** <note>original: "Wonder-Blossom," likely referring to a moment of spiritual revelation or the "Wunder-Blume" of mystical experience</note>, wherein the Lord is so sweet and friendly. I hope I shall thoroughly refresh myself with it, which you will perceive in this last part of this *book*, if God opens the gates to you in HIS Spirit.

3. I cannot *write* IT to you, for it is wonderful. I hope God will open your heart so that you also may taste and relish something of it. You desire to know whether I had any conversation with the *gentleman* <note>original German: "Herr"</note> you know of; I must inform you that I could not get to him, for I have had much to do in *another country*, where indeed I was *not at home* in my outward man. I am hindered until now by a journey to *Prague* for *seven days*, and then whatever God wills shall be done. Although at present a deep gate stands open to me, and therein I shall do what GOD wills.

<margin>† The Threefold Life <note>Referring to Böhme’s book *The Threefold Life of Man*.</note></margin>
4. I am sending you the completion of this book, sealed. If you have an opportunity, either send it to H. N. or back to me again with the other writings. They were on their way to H. N., but when the messenger came from you, I thought it fit to send them all packed up this way. I desire you to mind it very seriously and exactly; there is † *another* very excellent high work, perceived in the Spirit, and I do hope God will vouchsafe it to us. You may search further after it; in a short time, it shall be sent to you. And so I commend you into the divine kingdom of the joy of the eternal wellspring or fountain.

->Jacob Böhme <note>original: "Behme"</note>.<-

# The Fifty-First Epistle.

## To Mr. F. K., M. D. <note>likely referring to a medical doctor friend</note>

### May 9, 1624.

->V. H. I. L. I. C. I. V.<-
->*Unser Heil Im Leben Jesu Christi In Uns.*<-
->Our Salvation Is in the Life of Jesus Christ In Us.<-

My very dear sir and faithful Christian friend, I heartily wish you divine love, so that the *Sun* of *Righteousness* may shine eternally in your soul and spirit! If you are still doing well, it would be a great joy for me to know; God be praised, I am at this time in good physical health. However, I am outwardly covered in *Satan's* filth by the *Pharisaic* spirit <note>original: "Pharisaicall spirit"; Böhme uses this to describe the rigid, institutional religious authorities who opposed his mystical teachings</note>. I can hardly write to you how enraged *Satan* is at me and my little printed *Book of Repentance*, mostly because of the chief *Pharisee* and those who are like him. For they fear their authority and respect might diminish if *unlearned* people should reveal the highest foundations <note>original: "Ground"; referring to the fundamental spiritual reality or "Ungrund"</note>, and that people might demand they imitate or follow *Christ* and his *apostles* in both life and doctrine. In that case, their "Belly-God" <note>A reference to those who serve their own physical appetites or worldly status rather than God</note> would fall, and their minds would have to become more humble—none of which tastes good to them.

2. But it must come to pass; the time is born, and no amount of reproach will help. For by their criticism, they cause people to *ask* about these writings, and so they promote them more than they hinder them, as is happening here at present. Almost everyone wants to *see* them to discover this "great wonder" and what kind of "wild beast" is inside. When they read them, they are amazed at their own blindness; they look inward and examine their lives accordingly. Because of this, many have *converted* and entered into *repentance*, seeking friendship with me. Those who *before* had been my critics have afterward become the *sheep* of *Christ*. The Lord manages his way so wonderfully, and *all things must work for the best for God's children.*

3. The *Primate* <note>Likely referring to Gregor Richter, the Pastor Primarius of Görlitz and Böhme's primary antagonist</note> here has caused a poisonous, lying pamphlet or libel of one sheet to be printed in *Latin*...

<summary>Jakob Böhme describes the religious persecution he is facing from church authorities, noting that their attempts to suppress his "Book of Repentance" have backfired by making the public more curious and leading many to spiritual conversion.</summary>
<keywords>Jakob Böhme, persecution, Pharisees, Book of Repentance, religious authority, conversion, Gregor Richter</keywords>

* In verse.
In meter.
</margin>
In *verse* against me, wherein men may clearly see his spirit and Satan with his claws. I have written an *answer* to it, which, together with the *libel* <note>original: "Libell"; a published statement or pamphlet that unfairly damages someone's reputation</note>, you may obtain from *Mr. Michael Ender*. He will willingly lend it to you; there you will see wonderfully strange things, which I cannot write to you here.

<margin>With the bearer</margin>
4. I am also sending you, by the bearer of this letter, one of the little *printed* books. I hope you will practice its teachings well, seeing as you are already a lover of the true foundation <note>original: "Ground"; referring to Böhme’s concept of the "Ungrund" or the fundamental spiritual reality</note>. I would have liked to send you some of my other writings, but I have lent them all out.

They also read and love my writings. May God give me grace and power for it; I shall inform you at another time of what may happen there.

He is a very great practitioner of them, a loving man, and also very discreet and faithful; you will have a good friend in him. I commend you to the love of our LORD JESUS CHRIST!

Dated as above.

->*Jakob Böhme*<-

## The Fifty-Seventh Epistle

### To N. N. <note>N. N. stands for "nomen nescio" (name unknown), used here because the recipient's name was withheld from the original publication</note>

1.
**MY** dear Sir, after wishing you the love of our LORD *Jesus Christ* in *soul* and *spirit*, I inform you, Sir, that during my *absence* on this *journey*—while I was abroad visiting *Mr. Hans Sigismund*—the *Pharisaical spirit* <note>A term Böhme used for the rigid, legalistic church authorities who opposed his mystical views</note> has raged as if he would storm *heaven* and break *hell* into pieces. All of this is because of the <margin>* The Way to Christ.</margin> little printed book, *The Way to Christ*.

# 57th Epistle: The Way to Christ, deeply loved by many

<margin>
+
† John 9:17, 31;

...little book, which yet is very deeply loved by many. I do not know yet how it will go with me regarding this Pharisaical spirit <note>original: "Pharisaical Spirit"; Böhme uses this to describe the rigid, legalistic religious authorities who opposed his mystical teachings.</note>, but I put my hope and whole confidence in the love of **Jesus Christ**. # J. B. loves a Christian Mind better than Riches. Ep. 59.

...might be done by the rich from their surplus for the sustenance of life, and for what further might be expected from this *talent* <term>talent: referencing the biblical parable (Matthew 25) where a "talent" represents a gift or responsibility entrusted by God to be used for His glory</term>; therefore, I desire nothing from anyone.

## The Sixtieth Epistle

## To Mr. A. C.

->Immanuel <note>original: "Immanuel"; Hebrew for "God with us," a common greeting in Böhme's letters.</note><-

1. Much beloved sir and friend in Christ, I wish you divine love, blessed knowledge, and all temporal welfare! In your well-intended beginning, you might indeed be somewhat hindered, but a truly righteous, Christian, zealous heart has its school within itself, even in the midst of all business and employments. For if we follow or imitate Christ and attain Him within ourselves, then He is the beginning and end of all things, and our teacher or schoolmaster within us.

2. It may indeed be very advantageous to our *conversation* <note>original: "conversation"; in the 17th century, this meant one's entire way of life, conduct, or social dealings, rather than just speech.</note>, since you have such a fair opportunity to have these writings in your hands. Take care that you do not give them up or neglect them, but apply yourself to them. You will find a very excellent understanding in the *Brief Summary* <note>Böhme is referring to his work "A Summary of the Right Way," written in 1624.</note> which I am currently writing, of which *Mr. Tobias* <note>Tobias Kober, a physician from Görlitz and a close friend who often transcribed Böhme's manuscripts.</note> has already transcribed a part.

<meta>catchword: 3. For</meta>

<summary>Böhme concludes a letter by emphasizing that spiritual fellowship is more valuable than money, then begins a new letter advising a friend that a true Christian can find spiritual instruction within themselves regardless of their worldly business.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the sixtieth epistle from Jacob Böhme to a friend identified as "A. C." (likely Abraham von Sommerfeld). Böhme continues to describe the spiritual awakening he believes is occurring in his time, using his characteristic mystical imagery.</meta>

<header>The 60th Epistle. How we shall be freed from all Error.</header>
<sig>A</sig>

3. For there is a very clear *Morning Star* arisen, at which—if your spirit might be unlocked—you would **wonder** at what the Most High favors us with at present. In this, men may clearly see how the *bright* day breaks forth in the midst of the *dark night*, at which many hungry hearts will rejoice, and thereby be freed from ALL **error**.

4. I exhort you as my dear brother that you would lay hold on this fair season and opportunity, and not miss the **Rose-Time** <note>original: "Rose-Time"; Böhme uses this term to refer to a period of spiritual blooming or divine grace.</note>, but bud forth together with others as good sprouts in our fair garden of delight.

5. For the end of *Babel* <term>Babel: referencing the biblical Tower of Babel; for Böhme, this represents the state of spiritual confusion, sectarianism, and the corrupt institutional church</term> is at hand, and the **Turba** <note>original: "Turba"; in Böhme’s theology, this refers to the spirit of disturbance, strife, or the "wrath-fire" that breaks things apart.</note> has a great harvest to reap, for it will be earnest and severe. But let everyone seek or search himself in the time of grace, and go forth out of the *fleshly* Babel, so that he is not also taken in it. It is high time, and this is no fiction forged by us; it has become deeply understood and known.

6. And I also exhort Mr. Tobias <note>original: "Herr Tobias"</note> brotherly, that he would make good use of his present fit and acceptable time, and seek or search himself. I intend this faithfully; thus I commend you to the meek love of *Jesus Christ*!

->Yours in love,<-

->**Jacob Böhme.**<-

He uses mystical metaphors like the "Morning Star" and "Rose-Time" to describe this divine opportunity.</summary>

21. The Monday morning following, when the magistrates were met at the council house, they sent for the falsely accused man to appear before them. They examined him and perceived no evil in him; they found no anger or dislike in his words, deeds, or behavior. Nor did they observe anything that was blameworthy. They asked him, *“What hurt have you done to the preacher?”* He answered that *he did not know, nor could he find out from the preacher himself.* Therefore, he entreated them most submissively and earnestly *that they, in their wisdom, would send for the complainant (the preacher) and require him to say what had been done to him.*

22. Upon this, the whole council concluded that it was only just that the preacher should be kindly invited to come to them. They required him specifically to clarify his **grievances** <note>original: "Gravamina"; a Latin legal term for formal complaints or causes of annoyance.</note>. Thereupon, they sent two men from the council to the preacher to honorably invite him to come to the council house, or to specifically relate those grievances to the members sent to him.

23. At this, the preacher was enraged and sent them word: *“What do I have to do with your courthouse or council house? What I have to say, I shall speak in the place of God—from the pulpit. There is my council-throne and the seat of my profession. What I have said there, you should follow, and you should banish this vain, wicked, unprincipled heretic from the city, so that he may no longer oppose the holy office of preaching and bring the punishment of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram <note>Biblical figures from the Book of Numbers who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron and were swallowed by the earth as divine punishment.</note> upon the whole city.”*

# J. B. Banished and brought home again. Epistle. C. W.

24. ...how they should justly help the Master <note>The "Master" refers to the preacher, Gregory Richter.</note>; fearing the vehemence of their preacher in his pulpit, they concluded to banish the innocent Jacob Boehme <note>original: "Behme"</note> out of the city. Regarding this conclusion, some men of the Council would NOT consent, but rose and went their way; however, the rest carried it out. By the executioners or city officers, they caused the uncondemned, faithful citizen to be instantly banished out of the gates.

25. Which the patient, blessed man did NOT dislike; but answered, *"In the name of God, my Lords, I will do as you command and depart the city; but may I not go to my house first, and take my family <note>original: "mine"</note> with me, or at least tell them of my necessity?"* But they forbade it and denied him, saying they could not alter the sentence which the whole Council had concluded. He was to be led instantly from the council house out of the city, with derision and scorn; then he said: *"Dear sirs, let it be done, seeing it cannot be otherwise; I am contented."* So he was banished and went away all night long.

26. But the following morning, when the Council met together again and had reconciled their disagreement, they made another decision: to hunt after the persecuted, innocent man. They sent up and down throughout the country to seek him, and at length found him and brought him solemnly with honor into the city again, which was a **wonder** from God in the midst of those acts and decrees of the Devil.

27. This much is what I am certainly informed of: that it was so done.

<meta>This page continues the testimonies regarding the character and reception of Jacob Boehme, specifically focusing on the accounts of Dr. Charles Weisner concerning the opinions of high-ranking officials and theologians.</meta>

Excerpts from C. W. <note>Charles Weisner</note>: The Illustrious Prince Elector had a private conference with J.B. <note>Jacob Boehme</note>. Neither Dr. Meisner answered him, nor I either, my brother; for who knows what may lie hidden within it <note>Boehme's work</note>? How can we judge what we have not understood, nor can understand? Whether it be right, black, or white, may God convert the man if he is in error, and keep us to His divine Truth. May He give us a further and better understanding, as well as a mind and the capacity <note>original: "apprehension"</note> to express it and spread it to the best of our ability. Besides this, something else was said, but I left.

36. Another time, I heard the Reverend Dr. Meisner at Wittenberg say, when Jacob Boehme <note>original: "Behme"</note> was spoken of and he was asked what judgment he would give of him: he answered that he desired neither to judge, nor to arrange for the man to be condemned, suppressed, or silenced. He is a man endowed with wonderfully high gifts of the Spirit, which a man can yet neither condemn nor approve.

### And now printed in English this : ☽ : 3 : ♄ : 1661 <note>The symbols ☽ (Moon/Monday) and ♄ (Saturn/Saturday) along with the number 3 likely refer to a specific astrological or calendar date for the printing, common in Hermetic or mystical publications of this era.</note>

<margin>Year (1) 1612.</margin>
The First Book, called the *Aurora*; dated Tuesday in Pentecost week <note>The week following Whitsunday/Pentecost, a major Christian feast</note>, the 37th year of his age: June 1st. Printed in a large type in quarto <term>A book size where each sheet of paper is folded twice to create four leaves, or eight pages.</term>, with some notes added in his own hand in 1620. <margin>11/II/3</margin>

<margin>2. 1619.</margin>
The Second Book: *Of the Three Principles of the One only Divine Substance*, with an appendix to it concerning the *Threefold Life of Man*. Printed in a small type in quarto. <margin>11/II/2</margin>

<margin>3. 1620.</margin>
The Third Book: *Of the Threefold Life of Man*. Printed in the same type, in quarto. <margin>11/II/3</margin>

<margin>4. 1620.</margin>
The Fourth Book: Being an *Answer to Forty Questions concerning the Soul*, in a letter to Doctor Balthazar Walter. In the middle of the answer to the first question is the scheme, or figure, of the Philosophical Globe—also called the "Turned Eye," the "Eye of the Wonders of Eternity," or the "Looking Glass of Wisdom"—with an exposition of it and of the Three Worlds signified by it. This includes an appendix concerning the soul, the image of the soul, and the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; Boehme's term for the "turmoil" or "disturbance" that destroys the divine image.</note> or Destroyer of the Image. In quarto. <margin>11/II/3</margin>

<margin>5. 1620.</margin>
The Fifth Book, dated in May: divided into three parts. <margin>11/II/2</margin>
The First: *Of the Incarnation of Jesus Christ*.
The Second: *Of the Suffering, Dying, Death, and Resurrection of Christ*.
The Third: *Of the Tree of Faith*. In quarto.

In this work, the clarity of representation that the honorable Swedenborg provides is lacking.

<margin>Page 86, Chapter 44, <gloss>First Part</gloss></margin>
A lily grows in the human essence, which will speak in its own tongue or language of the great deeds and wonders of God, which shall sound across the circumference of the earth. Hallelujah.

-> + See the 80th Epistle in the *Book of Letters*. <note>The *Book of Letters* refers to the published correspondence of Jacob Boehme, known for his influential Christian mysticism.</note> <-

13. Yet know that a lily blossoms for you in the northern countries; if you do not destroy it with the sectarian arguments of the scholars, then it will become a great tree among you. But if you choose to argue rather than to know the true God, then the ray of light passes by and kills only some <note>original: "killeth only some"; this likely refers to spiritual death or the loss of enlightenment for a few</note>, and afterward you will be forced to draw water for the thirst of your souls among foreign nations.

---

These must refer to Mr. Swedenborg. I admire him for this consummate knowledge in things both spiritual and natural. 
— H. Pedrett <note>Emanuel Swedenborg (1688–1772) was a Swedish pluralistic scientist and theologian who claimed to have received a new revelation from Jesus Christ.</note>
